For example, under the ITAR, we are required to determine the proper licensing jurisdiction and classification of products, software and technology; and obtain licenses or other forms of U.S. government authorizations to engage in certain activities related to and that support our business operations. The authorization requirements include the need to get permission to release controlled technology to foreign person employees and other foreign persons.
paras.zh: 发射和卫星运营受严格的出口管制以及经济和贸易制裁法律的约束，包括美国《国际武器贸易条例》（“ITAR”）、《出口管理条例》以及美国财政部外国资产控制办公室（“OFAC”）实施和执行的制裁。根据美国出口管制法律，我们须获得商务部或国务院的出口授权，方可向外国人（包括外籍员工）或向外国目的地出口或共享任何受管制的货物、技术或软件。此类授权的可获得性可能受到地缘政治格局重大变化的影响。美国政府可能修订出口管制法规、限制向新的或更多地点出口，或以其他方式改变其许可方式，这些变化虽不在我们控制范围内，却会对我们的国际供应链、现有出口许可证和业务运营产生重大影响。例如，根据 ITAR，我们须确定产品、软件和技术的适当许可管辖权和分类，并取得许可证或其他形式的美国政府授权，方可从事与我们的业务运营相关并支持业务运营的某些活动。授权要求包括：向外国员工和其他外国人披露受管制技术须获得许可。

paras.en: In addition, we are required to obtain OFAC authorization in certain situations, including to provide connectivity services or engage in other business operations in certain global markets that may be subject to economic sanctions or trade embargoes. While we have been successful in obtaining such authorizations in the past, there can be no assurances that authorizations or licenses will be available in the future. In addition, significant changes to the geopolitical landscape, such as the outbreak of armed conflict, could result in the imposition of new or expanded economic or trade sanctions that may impact or prevent our ability to provide services or otherwise operate in certain markets. Failures by us to comply with import, export control, or sanctions laws and regulations could result in civil or criminal penalties, fines, investigations, more onerous compliance requirements, loss of export privileges, debarment from government contracts, or limitations on our ability to enter into contracts with the U.S. government. Other regulators, such as the EU or UK, may also impose restrictions on our ability to operate in geopolitically sensitive countries or territories.
paras.zh: 此外，在某些情形下，我们需要获得 OFAC 授权，包括在可能受到经济制裁或贸易禁运的某些全球市场提供连接服务或开展其他业务运营。尽管我们过去曾成功获得此类授权，但无法保证未来仍能获得授权或许可。此外，地缘政治格局的重大变化，例如武装冲突的爆发，可能导致实施新的或扩大的经济或贸易制裁，从而可能影响或阻止我们在某些市场提供服务或以其他方式运营。我们未能遵守进口、出口管制或制裁法律法规，可能导致民事或刑事处罚、罚款、调查、更繁重的合规要求、丧失出口特权、被禁止参与政府合同，或限制我们与美国政府签订合同的能力。其他监管机构，例如欧盟或英国，也可能对我们在地缘政治敏感国家或地区的运营能力施加限制。

paras.en: **Our use of open source technology could impose limitations on our ability to commercialize our space-based internet and mobile phone services, AI products, and X platform, or otherwise negatively affect our business.**
paras.zh: **我们对开源技术的使用可能会限制我们将天基互联网和移动电话服务、AI 产品及 X 平台商业化的能力，或以其他方式对我们的业务产生负面影响。**

paras.en: We use open source technology in some of our software, including in our Starlink products and services, and in our AI segment’s and X platform’s software and products, and we expect to continue to use open source technology in the future. Open source technology is licensed by its authors or other third parties under open source licenses, which in some instances may subject us to certain unfavorable conditions. For example, certain open source licenses may give rise to requirements to disclose or license our proprietary source code or make available any derivative works or modifications of the open source code on unfavorable terms or at no cost. Although we monitor and have implemented policies relating to our use of open source technology to avoid subjecting our products and services to conditions we do not intend, we cannot guarantee such efforts will be successful and we may face allegations from others alleging ownership of, or seeking to enforce the terms of, an open source license, including by demanding release of the open source software, derivative works or modifications, or our proprietary source code that was developed using such technology, or demanding access to our software free of charge or on other unfavorable terms. These allegations could also result in litigation. Additionally, our AI products are trained on data sets that may include open source software, and it is possible that certain outputs of our AI products may be subject to open source license restrictions or obligations. The terms of many open source licenses are ambiguous and have not been interpreted by United States or foreign courts. There is a risk that these licenses could be construed in a way that could impose unanticipated conditions or restrictions on our ability to commercialize our AI segment’s products. In such an event, we may be required to seek licenses from third parties to continue commercially offering our AI segment’s products, to make our proprietary code generally available in source code form, to re-engineer our AI segment’s products or to discontinue the sale of our AI segment’s products or such other products if re-engineering could not be accomplished on a timely basis, any of which could adversely affect our business, financial condition, results of operations, and future prospects.
paras.zh: 我们在部分软件中使用了开源技术，包括我们的 Starlink 产品和服务，以及我们 AI 板块和 X 平台的软件和产品，并且我们预计未来将继续使用开源技术。开源技术由其作者或其他第三方依据开源许可证进行许可，在某些情况下，这可能使我们受到某些不利条件的约束。例如，某些开源许可证可能要求我们披露或许可我们的专有源代码，或以不利条款或免费提供开源代码的任何衍生作品或修改。尽管我们已针对开源技术的使用实施相关监控和政策，以避免我们的产品和服务受到我们无意承受的条件约束，但我们无法保证此类努力一定成功，且我们可能面临他人提出的主张，声称其拥有开源许可证的所有权或寻求强制执行开源许可证的条款，包括要求发布开源软件、衍生作品或修改，或我们使用此类技术开发的专有源代码，或要求免费或以其他不利条款获取我们的软件。此类主张还可能导致诉讼。此外，我们的 AI 产品是在可能包含开源软件的数据集上训练的，且我们 AI 产品的某些输出可能受到开源许可证限制或义务的约束。许多开源许可证的条款存在歧义，且尚未经美国或外国法院解释。存在此类许可证被解释为对我们 AI 板块产品的商业化能力施加意外条件或限制的风险。在此情况下，我们可能被要求向第三方寻求许可以继续商业提供我们 AI 板块的产品、以源代码形式普遍提供我们的专有代码、重新设计我们 AI 板块的产品，或在无法及时完成重新设计的情况下停止销售我们 AI 板块的产品或此类其他产品，任何一项均可能对我们的业务、财务状况、经营业绩和未来前景产生不利影响。

paras.en: In addition, the use of open source technology may entail greater technical and legal risks than those associated with the use of third-party commercial software as open source licensors generally do not provide support, warranties, controls on origin of the software, indemnification or other contractual protections regarding infringement claims or the quality of the code, including the existence of security vulnerabilities. Many of the risks associated with usage of open source technology, such as the lack of warranties or assurance of title, cannot be eliminated and could, if not properly addressed, negatively affect our business. To the extent that our technologies and other business operations depend upon the successful and secure operation of the open source technology we use, any undetected errors or defects in this open source software could prevent the deployment or impair the functionality of our software, delay the introduction of new technological capabilities, result in a failure of our technologies, and injure our brand and reputation. For example, undetected errors or defects in open source software could render it vulnerable to breaches or security attacks and make our AI segment’s products more vulnerable to data breaches or security attacks. Any of the foregoing would have a material adverse effect on our business, financial condition, results of operations and future prospects.
paras.zh: 此外，与使用第三方商业软件相比，使用开源技术可能带来更大的技术和法律风险，因为开源许可方通常不提供支持、保证、对软件来源的控制、赔偿或其他合同保护（涉及侵权索赔或代码质量，包括是否存在安全漏洞）。使用开源技术所涉及的许多风险，例如缺乏保证或所有权担保，无法消除，若未妥善处理，可能对我们的业务产生负面影响。若我们的技术及其他业务运营依赖于我们所使用开源技术成功且安全的运行，则此类开源软件中任何未被发现的错误或缺陷可能妨碍我们软件的部署或损害其功能、延迟新技术的推出、导致我们的技术失效，并损害我们的品牌和声誉。例如，开源软件中未被发现的错误或缺陷可能使其易受入侵或安全攻击，并使我们的 AI 板块产品更易遭受数据泄露或安全攻击。上述任何情形均可能对我们的业务、财务状况、经营业绩和未来前景产生重大不利影响。

paras.en: **Payment, banking, and other financial service-related activities may subject us to additional regulatory requirements, regulatory actions, and other risks that could be costly and difficult to comply with or that could harm our business.**
paras.zh: **支付、银行及其他金融服务相关活动可能使我们承担额外的监管要求、监管行动及其他风险，这些风险可能成本高昂且难以合规，或可能损害我们的业务。**

paras.en: We plan to publicly launch the Money Product, which will offer payment, banking and other financial services functionalities, including enabling our users to purchase tangible, virtual, and digital goods from merchants and send money to other users, among other activities. These activities will subject us to a variety of laws and regulations in the United States, Europe, and elsewhere globally, including those governing anti-money laundering and counter-terrorism financing, money transmission, stored value, gift cards and other prepaid access instruments, electronic funds transfer, virtual currency, consumer protection, charitable fundraising, global and local economic sanctions, and import and export restrictions. In addition, we could become subject to new consumer protection laws and regulations that may be adopted or amended, including those related to payment, banking, and other financial services activities as well as sharing, collection, and use of payment, banking, and other financial services-related data. Depending on how the Money Product evolves, we may also be subject to other laws and regulations including those governing gambling, cryptocurrencies, brokerage, banking, credit, and lending. In some jurisdictions, the application or interpretation of these laws and regulations is not clear. We have received certain payments licenses in the United States and other jurisdictions for our anticipated regulated payments-related products and activities. These licenses increase flexibility in how our use of payments may evolve, help mitigate regulatory uncertainty, and will generally require us to demonstrate compliance with many domestic and foreign laws in relation to our licensed payments products and activities. Our efforts to comply with these laws and regulations may still not guarantee compliance. In the event that we are found to be in violation of any such legal or regulatory requirements, we may be subject to monetary fines or other penalties such as a cease and desist order, or we may be required to make product changes, any of which could have a material and adverse effect on our business, financial condition, results of operations and future prospects.
paras.zh: 我们计划公开发布 Money 产品，该产品将提供支付、银行及其他金融服务功能，包括使用户能够从商户处购买有形、虚拟和数字商品，以及向其他用户转账等活动。这些活动将使我们受到美国、欧洲及全球其他地区各类法律法规的约束，包括规范反洗钱和反恐怖主义融资、资金传输、储值、礼品卡及其他预付接入工具、电子资金转账、虚拟货币、消费者保护、慈善募捐、全球和本地经济制裁以及进出口限制的法律法规。此外，我们可能受到新制定或修订的消费者保护法律法规的约束，包括与支付、银行及其他金融服务活动相关的法律法规，以及与支付、银行及其他金融服务相关数据的共享、收集和使用相关的法律法规。视 Money 产品的发展情况，我们还可能受到其他法律法规的约束，包括规范赌博、加密货币、经纪、银行、信贷和借贷的法律法规。在某些司法管辖区，这些法律法规的适用或解释并不明确。我们已就预期的受监管支付相关产品和活动在美国及其他司法管辖区取得了若干支付牌照。这些牌照增强了我们支付业务发展方式的灵活性，有助于缓解监管不确定性，并且通常要求我们证明我们的持牌支付产品和活动符合诸多国内外法律。我们为遵守这些法律法规所做的努力仍可能无法保证合规。如果我们被发现违反任何此类法律或监管要求，我们可能受到罚款或其他处罚，例如停止令，或被要求进行产品变更，其中任何一项都可能对我们的业务、财务状况、经营业绩和未来前景产生重大不利影响。

paras.en: In addition, we will be subject to a variety of additional risks as a result of payment, banking, and other financial services transactions, including: increased costs and other resources to address errors in transactions or customer disputes; potential fraudulent or otherwise illegal activity by users, developers, employees, or third parties; restrictions on the investment of consumer funds used to transact payments; and additional disclosure and reporting requirements. We plan to publicly launch the Money Product and may in the future undertake additional payment, banking, and other financial services initiatives, which may subject us to many of the foregoing risks and additional licensing requirements.
paras.zh: 此外，由于支付、银行及其他金融服务交易，我们将面临各种额外风险，包括：为解决交易错误或客户争议而增加的成本和其他资源；用户、开发者、员工或第三方潜在的欺诈或其他非法活动；对用于支付交易的消费者资金投资的限制；以及额外的披露和报告要求。我们计划公开发布 Money 产品，并可能在未来开展额外的支付、银行及其他金融服务举措，这可能使我们面临上述诸多风险以及额外的牌照要求。

paras.en: **Our efforts to support the creation of permanent installations on the Moon and Mars depend on the successful development and deployment of next-generation capabilities.**
paras.zh: **我们为支持在月球和火星上建造永久性设施所做的努力，取决于下一代能力的成功开发和部署。**

paras.en: Activities related to the industrialization and development of the Moon and Mars require the successful development and deployment of next-generation capabilities such as fully reusable launch vehicles, including Starship, in-space refueling and propellant storage, in space communications systems, and other capabilities required for operations beyond Earth’s orbit. These systems involve significant technological, engineering, and operational challenges, including the need to develop habitable transportation and surface environments, and perform complex in-orbit operations. Solving these challenges will require developing solutions that are novel or untested and will require substantial capital investment. If these efforts take longer than anticipated, or if technical, operational, or engineering challenges arise in connection with these efforts, our goals with respect to the Moon and Mars, including government contracts, and other and multiplanetary initiatives could be delayed, modified, or cancelled and could materially and adversely affect our business, financial condition, and results of operations. Even if such goals are achieved, they may not generate meaningful revenue or achieve profitability for an extended period of time.
paras.zh: 与月球和火星工业化及开发相关的活动，需要成功开发和部署下一代能力，例如包括 Starship 在内的完全可重复使用运载火箭、在轨加注与推进剂储存、太空通信系统，以及在地球轨道之外运行所需的其他能力。这些系统涉及重大的技术、工程和运营挑战，包括需要开发可居住的运输与地表环境，并执行复杂的在轨操作。解决这些挑战需要开发新颖或未经检验的解决方案，并将需要大量资本投入。如果这些努力耗时超出预期，或在这些努力过程中出现技术、运营或工程挑战，我们关于月球和火星的目标（包括政府合同）以及其他多行星计划可能会被延迟、修改或取消，并可能对我们的业务、财务状况和经营业绩产生重大不利影响。即使这些目标得以实现，它们也可能在较长时期内无法产生有意义的收入或实现盈利。

paras.en: **Our AI segment is recently formed, is still being fully integrated and optimized, operates in a rapidly evolving industry and is subject to significant execution, competitive and operational risks.**
paras.zh: **我们的 AI 业务板块系近期组建，仍在全面整合与优化之中，所处行业快速演变，并面临重大的执行、竞争和运营风险。**

paras.en: We acquired xAI in February 2026 as the foundational platform for our AI segment and as part of our ambitious vertical integration strategy intended to combine artificial intelligence capabilities with our established Space and Connectivity businesses. Prior to its acquisition by the Company, xAI itself was an early-stage company. As a result, our AI segment remains in a relatively early stage of organizational and operational maturity and is subject to integration, scaling and execution risks.
paras.zh: 我们于 2026 年 2 月收购 xAI，将其作为我们 AI 业务板块的基础平台，并作为我们雄心勃勃的垂直整合战略的一部分，该战略旨在将人工智能能力与我们既有的太空和连接业务相结合。在被本公司收购之前，xAI 本身是一家早期阶段公司。因此，我们的 AI 业务板块在组织与运营成熟度上仍处于相对早期阶段，并面临整合、规模化和执行风险。

paras.en: The successful integration of acquired businesses, technologies, strategic partners, and employees is inherently complex, costly and time-consuming, and may result in operational inefficiencies, delays, disruptions, increased costs, loss of knowledge and diversion of management attention. As is common in large acquisitions, we have had to take significant steps to integrate xAI’s operations into our broader corporate structure as part of our AI segment, including putting in place the management team and organizational structure needed to execute at the scale and pace our strategy demands, as well as controls and procedures appropriate for a larger organization like ours. Many of these steps are not yet complete.
paras.zh: 对被收购业务、技术、战略合作伙伴和员工的成功整合本质上复杂、昂贵且耗时，并可能导致运营效率低下、延迟、中断、成本增加、知识流失以及管理层注意力分散。正如大型收购中常见的情况，我们不得不采取重大举措，将 xAI 的运营整合到我们更广泛的公司架构中，作为我们 AI 业务板块的一部分，包括建立执行我们战略所要求的规模和速度所需的管理团队和组织结构，以及适合我们这样更大规模组织的控制措施和程序。其中许多举措尚未完成。

paras.en: We have undertaken, and continue to undertake, changes in personnel, strategic partnerships, infrastructure-sharing arrangements, organizational restructurings, acquisitions and other integration initiatives intended to accelerate development of our AI capabilities, compute infrastructure and commercial offerings. Management believes these initiatives may create long-term strategic advantages through the combination of engineering talent, compute infrastructure, proprietary data, software capabilities and integrated operational platforms across the Company’s businesses, among others. However, the successful integration of acquired businesses, management teams, employees, strategic partners, technologies and evolving product architectures is inherently complex, costly and time-consuming and may result in operational inefficiencies, delays, disruptions or the failure to realize anticipated synergies or commercial benefits.
paras.zh: 我们已实施并将继续实施人员、战略合作伙伴关系、基础设施共享安排、组织重组、收购及其他整合举措方面的变革，旨在加速发展我们的人工智能能力、算力基础设施和商业产品。管理层认为，这些举措通过整合公司各业务板块的工程人才、算力基础设施、专有数据、软件能力和一体化运营平台等，可能创造长期战略优势。然而，成功整合被收购业务、管理团队、员工、战略合作伙伴、技术及不断演进的产品架构本身具有复杂性、高成本和耗时性，并可能导致运营效率低下、延迟、中断或无法实现预期协同效应或商业利益。

paras.en: We have also pursued evolving commercial and technical strategies, including coding and software development (such as through our partnership with Cursor) and monetization of unused compute capacity (such as through our cloud compute services agreements with Anthropic), while simultaneously continuing to invest heavily in expanding datacenter and compute capacity for our own internal AI initiatives and products. These efforts may require substantial capital expenditures and management attention and may create operational complexity relating to infrastructure allocation, prioritization of internal versus external compute usage, integration of third-party technologies and partnerships, cybersecurity, data governance and commercialization strategy. We may elect to allocate capital and resources to long-term initiatives even if alternative uses with more short-term upside are available. There can be no assurance that these initiatives will achieve their intended operational or financial objectives.
paras.zh: 我们还推行了不断演进的商业和技术战略，包括编程和软件开发（例如通过与 Cursor 的合作）以及未使用算力容量的变现（例如通过与 Anthropic 的云计算服务协议），同时继续大力投资于扩展数据中心和算力容量，以支持我们自身的内部 AI 举措和产品。这些努力可能需要大量资本支出和管理层关注，并可能在基础设施分配、内部与外部算力使用的优先排序、第三方技术和合作伙伴关系的整合、网络安全、数据治理和商业化战略方面带来运营复杂性。我们可能选择将资本和资源分配给长期举措，即使存在具有更多短期上行空间的替代用途。无法保证这些举措将实现其预期的运营或财务目标。

paras.en: The artificial intelligence industry is highly dynamic and rapidly evolving. We face significant uncertainty relating to technological developments, changing customer preferences, evolving regulatory and legal frameworks, increasing public scrutiny, and intense competition for engineering talent, compute capacity, infrastructure, customers and capital. Some customers for compute services may not be cash flow positive and rely on external capital to fund their contractual obligations to us. In addition, the consumer AI market is characterized by rapid model iteration, frequent new entrants and intense competition for user attention; as a result, download and other usage metrics for any individual AI application, including Grok, can fluctuate significantly (including periods of decreased Grok app downloads and user activity) in response to competitor model releases, product update cycles, and broader shifts in user behavior. As a result of these market dynamics, we may need to modify our AI strategy, organizational structure, infrastructure deployment and capital allocation decisions in response to technological change, competitive pressures, regulatory developments or commercial adoption trends. Initiatives that management believes are strategically beneficial over the long term may nevertheless experience near-term operational disruptions, integration inefficiencies, product delays, technical setbacks, leadership turnover, employee attrition, infrastructure constraints, increased costs or uneven customer adoption during periods of transition or rapid scaling.
paras.zh: 人工智能行业高度动态且快速演变。我们在技术发展、客户偏好变化、监管与法律框架演进、公众审视加剧，以及工程人才、算力容量、基础设施、客户和资本方面的激烈竞争等方面面临重大不确定性。部分算力服务客户可能尚未实现正现金流，并依赖外部资本为其对我们的合同义务提供资金。此外，消费级 AI 市场的特点是模型迭代迅速、新进入者频繁涌现以及用户注意力竞争激烈；因此，任何单一 AI 应用（包括 Grok）的下载量及其他使用指标都可能因竞争对手模型发布、产品更新周期以及用户行为的更广泛变化而出现大幅波动（包括 Grok 应用下载量和用户活跃度下降的时期）。受这些市场动态影响，我们可能需要根据技术变革、竞争压力、监管进展或商业采用趋势，调整我们的 AI 战略、组织结构、基础设施部署和资本配置决策。管理层认为在长期具有战略利益的举措，在转型或快速扩张时期仍可能经历短期运营中断、整合效率低下、产品延迟、技术挫折、领导层更替、员工流失、基础设施约束、成本上升或客户采用不均衡。

paras.en: Management believes that our recent organizational restructuring efforts, infrastructure investments and strategic collaborations position the AI segment favorably for long-term growth and are consistent with the maturation process of rapidly scaling AI platforms and optimization of acquired companies. However, there can be no assurance that we will successfully integrate acquired businesses and technologies, retain key personnel, execute our AI strategy within anticipated timeframes, achieve meaningful commercial adoption, generate anticipated revenues or returns on investment, or compete effectively in a rapidly evolving and increasingly competitive and consolidated AI market. If we are unable to successfully execute our AI strategy, our business, financial condition, results of operations and prospects could be materially adversely affected.
paras.zh: 管理层认为，我们近期的组织重组工作、基础设施投资和战略合作使 AI 板块处于有利地位，有利于长期增长，并且符合快速扩张的 AI 平台走向成熟的过程以及被收购公司的优化进程。然而，无法保证我们将成功整合被收购的业务和技术、留住关键人员、在预期时间内执行我们的 AI 战略、实现有意义的商业采用、产生预期收入或投资回报，或在快速演变且日益激烈和整合的 AI 市场中有效竞争。如果我们无法成功执行我们的 AI 战略，我们的业务、财务状况、经营业绩和前景可能受到重大不利影响。

paras.en: **Our AI segment is capital intensive, has incurred significant operating losses, and operates in a nascent and rapidly evolving market in which the potential of AI remains uncertain.**
paras.zh: **我们的 AI 板块属于资本密集型，已产生重大经营亏损，并且处于一个新兴且快速演变的市场中，AI 的潜力仍存在不确定性。**

paras.en: AI is a nascent and rapidly evolving technology, and although we believe AI holds significant promise for consumers and enterprises, its long-term impact will depend on the degree to which AI products and services prove to be broadly useful in real-world applications. There can be no assurance that demand for AI solutions will develop or be sustained at the levels we anticipate, or at all. While industry interest in AI has grown substantially, the commercial value proposition of frontier AI models remains largely unproven, and long-term market acceptance of our AI products and services is uncertain. Developing, training, and providing inference for frontier AI models requires substantial and growing capital expenditures, including investments in specialized computing hardware, data center infrastructure, energy procurement, and technical personnel, and we expect these costs to continue to increase for the foreseeable future. In addition, we plan to allocate substantial capital to build our AI compute infrastructure, and we expect a multi-year investment horizon before these deployments translate into sustained positive AI Segment Adjusted EBITDA. Our AI segment has incurred significant operating losses since inception, and we may not achieve profitability in this segment, or, if achieved, sustain it, and there can be no assurance that the returns on our AI investments will be adequate to justify the capital deployed. Furthermore, the continued improvement of AI model capabilities has historically depended in part on scaling laws, the empirical observation that model performance improves with increased compute, data, and model size, but there is uncertainty as to how long these scaling relationships will continue to hold. As a result of these factors, our AI segment may not achieve the growth or returns we expect.
paras.zh: AI 是一项新兴且快速演进的技术，尽管我们相信 AI 对消费者和企业具有重大前景，但其长期影响将取决于 AI 产品和服务在现实应用中在多大程度上被证明具有广泛实用性。无法保证对 AI 解决方案的需求会发展到或维持在我们预期的水平，甚至根本无法保证需求会出现。尽管行业对 AI 的兴趣已大幅增长，但前沿 AI 模型的商业价值主张在很大程度上仍未得到验证，我们的 AI 产品和服务能否获得长期市场认可尚不确定。开发、训练前沿 AI 模型并为其提供推理服务需要大量且不断增长的资本支出，包括对专用计算硬件、数据中心基础设施、能源采购和技术人员的投资，我们预计这些成本在可预见的未来将继续增加。此外，我们计划投入大量资本建设我们的 AI 算力基础设施，我们预计需要多年的投资周期，这些部署才能转化为持续的 AI 分部调整后 EBITDA 正值。我们的 AI 分部自成立以来已产生重大经营亏损，我们可能无法实现该分部的盈利，或者即使实现盈利，也可能无法持续，且无法保证我们对 AI 投资的回报足以证明所投入资本的合理性。此外，AI 模型能力的持续提升在历史上部分依赖于规模定律，即模型性能随算力、数据和模型规模的增加而提升的经验性观察，但这些规模关系能持续多久存在不确定性。由于上述因素，我们的 AI 分部可能无法实现我们预期的增长或回报。

paras.en: **We have a history of net losses and may not achieve profitability in the future.**
paras.zh: **我们有着净亏损的历史，未来可能无法实现盈利。**

paras.en: We incurred net losses of $(4,937) million and $(4,628) million for the years ended December 31, 2025 and 2023, respectively, and a net loss of $(4,276) million for the three months ended March 31, 2026. We may not achieve or, if achieved, sustain profitability in the future. As of March 31, 2026, we had an accumulated deficit of $41,311 million. While we have experienced significant growth in revenue over the last three years, we cannot predict whether we will maintain this level of growth or when we will achieve profitability again. We also expect our capital expenditures and operating expenses to increase in the future, including our general and administrative expenses as a result of increased costs associated with operating as a public company and as we continue to invest for our future growth, including substantial capital expenditures to design, develop, expand, and maintain our technologies and infrastructure to support our operations. Our revenue could decline for a number of reasons, including if we are unable to execute on our growth strategy and as a result of the other risks described in this prospectus. Furthermore, if we fail to maintain or increase our revenue to offset increases in our operating expenses or manage our costs as we invest in our business, including if we do not maintain or improve our operating efficiencies, we may not achieve or sustain profitability. Any failure by us to achieve or sustain profitability on a consistent basis could have a material adverse effect on our business, financial condition and results of operations and cause the market price of our Class A common stock to decline.
paras.zh: 截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日和 2023 年 12 月 31 日止年度，我们分别产生净亏损 $(4,937) 百万和 $(4,628) 百万，截至 2026 年 3 月 31 日止三个月产生净亏损 $(4,276) 百万。我们未来可能无法实现盈利，或即使实现盈利也无法持续。截至 2026 年 3 月 31 日，我们的累计亏损为 $41,311 百万。尽管过去三年我们的收入实现了显著增长，但我们无法预测能否维持这一增长水平，也无法预测何时能再次实现盈利。我们还预计未来资本支出和运营费用将会增加，其中包括因作为上市公司运营相关成本增加而导致的一般及行政费用增加，以及我们持续为未来增长进行投资，包括为设计、开发、扩展和维护我们的技术和基础设施以支持运营而发生的重大资本支出。我们的收入可能因多种原因下降，包括我们无法执行增长战略，以及本招股说明书中描述的其他风险。此外，如果我们在投资业务时未能维持或增加收入以抵消运营费用的增加，或未能管理好成本，包括未能维持或改善运营效率，我们可能无法实现或维持盈利。我们若未能持续实现或维持盈利，可能对我们的业务、财务状况和经营成果产生重大不利影响，并导致我们的 A 类普通股市场价格下跌。

paras.en: **The timing of our revenue and cost recognition may fluctuate due to factors outside of our control, which could cause our periodic results of operations to fluctuate and make our results difficult to predict.**
paras.zh: **我们的收入与成本确认时点可能因我们无法控制的因素而波动，这可能导致我们的期间经营成果波动，并使我们的业绩难以预测。**

paras.en: In our financial results, we recognize revenue and costs for a majority of customer payloads at the launch or deployment of the customer’s payload to its intended orbit. While we plan launches and schedule payloads in advance, the timing of these launches or deployments may vary and can be delayed or otherwise affected by a number of factors outside of our control, including the customer’s delay in delivering their payload for integration onto the launch vehicle, adverse weather, and other operational considerations. As a result, the timing of revenue recognition may shift between reporting periods. For example, if the launch of a customer’s payload was expected to occur near the end of a reporting period but instead occurs shortly thereafter (e.g., on April 1 instead of March 30), the associated revenue would be recognized in the subsequent quarter. In addition, if a significant number of launches or deployments occur within a short period of time, the concentration of those events may result in greater variability in the timing of revenue recognition between reporting periods. These factors may cause our quarterly or annual results of operations to fluctuate and may make our results difficult to predict.
paras.zh: 在我们的财务业绩中，我们针对大多数客户有效载荷的收入和成本是在客户有效载荷发射或部署至其预定轨道时确认的。尽管我们会提前规划发射并安排有效载荷，但这些发射或部署的时点可能发生变化，并可能因我们无法控制的多种因素而延迟或受到其他影响，包括客户延迟交付其有效载荷以集成到运载火箭上、恶劣天气以及其他运营方面的考虑。因此，收入确认的时点可能在报告期之间发生转移。例如，如果某客户有效载荷的发射原预计在报告期末附近发生，但实际在稍后不久发生（例如，在 4 月 1 日而非 3 月 30 日），相关收入将在下一季度确认。此外，如果在短时间内发生大量发射或部署，这些事件的集中可能导致报告期之间收入确认时点的波动性加大。这些因素可能导致我们的季度或年度经营成果波动，并可能使我们的业绩难以预测。

paras.en: **Failure to comply with requirements to design, implement, and maintain effective internal controls could have a material adverse effect on our business and stock price.**
paras.zh: **未能遵守设计、实施和维护有效内部控制的要求，可能对我们的业务和股价产生重大不利影响。**

paras.en: As a privately held company, we were not required to evaluate our internal control over financial reporting in a manner that meets the standards of publicly traded companies required by Section 404(a) of the Sarbanes-Oxley Act (“Section 404”).
paras.zh: 作为一家私营公司，我们此前无需按照《萨班斯-奥克斯利法案》第 404(a) 条（“第 404 条”）所要求的上市公司标准，对我们的财务报告内部控制进行评估。

paras.en: As a public company, we will have significant requirements for enhanced financial reporting and internal controls. The process of designing and implementing effective internal controls is a continuous effort that requires us to anticipate and react to changes in our business and the economic and regulatory environments and to expend significant resources to maintain a system of internal controls that is adequate to satisfy our reporting obligations as a public company. If we are unable to establish or maintain appropriate internal financial reporting controls and procedures, it could cause us to fail to meet our reporting obligations on a timely basis, result in material misstatements in our consolidated financial statements, and harm our results of operations. In addition, we will be required, pursuant to Section 404, to furnish a report by management on, among other things, the effectiveness of our internal control over financial reporting in the second annual report following the completion of this offering. This assessment will need to include disclosure of any material weaknesses identified by our management in our internal control over financial reporting. The rules governing the standards that must be met for our management to assess our internal control over financial reporting are complex and require significant documentation, testing, and possible remediation. Testing and maintaining internal controls may divert our management’s attention from other matters that are important to our business. Additionally, our independent registered public accounting firm will be required to attest to the effectiveness of our internal control over financial reporting on an annual basis, beginning with our second annual report.
paras.zh: 作为一家上市公司，我们将面临加强财务报告和内部控制的重大要求。设计和实施有效内部控制的过程是一项持续的努力，要求我们预见并应对业务以及经济和监管环境的变化，并投入大量资源以维持足以满足我们作为上市公司报告义务的内部控制体系。如果我们无法建立或维持适当的内部财务报告控制与程序，可能导致我们无法及时履行报告义务，导致我们的合并财务报表出现重大错报，并损害我们的经营业绩。此外，根据第 404 条，我们将被要求在本招股说明书完成后的第二份年度报告中，由管理层就我们的财务报告内部控制有效性等事项提供报告。该评估将需要披露我们管理层在财务报告内部控制中识别出的任何重大缺陷。规范管理层评估财务报告内部控制所必须满足标准的规则十分复杂，需要大量文档记录、测试以及可能的整改。测试和维护内部控制可能会分散我们管理层对业务其他重要事项的注意力。此外，我们的独立注册公共会计师事务所将被要求自我们的第二份年度报告起，每年对我们的财务报告内部控制有效性进行鉴证。

paras.en: We are currently in the process of updating our control processes and automating certain of our procedures and systems in anticipation of becoming a public company, but our internal controls over financial reporting currently do not meet all of the standards contemplated by Section 404 that we will eventually be required to meet. Because we currently do not have comprehensive documentation of our internal controls and have not yet tested our internal controls in accordance with Section 404, we cannot conclude in accordance with Section 404 that we do not have a material weakness in our internal controls or a combination of significant deficiencies that could result in the conclusion that we have a material weakness in our internal controls. In connection with updating our control processes and the implementation of the necessary procedures and practices related to internal control over financial reporting, we have identified deficiencies and may identify deficiencies in the future that we may not be able to remediate in time to meet the deadline imposed by the Sarbanes-Oxley Act for compliance with the requirements of Section 404. In addition, we may encounter problems or delays in completing the remediation of any deficiencies identified by our independent registered public accounting firm in connection with the issuance of their attestation report. Our testing, or the subsequent testing (if required) by our independent registered public accounting firm, may reveal deficiencies in our internal controls over financial reporting that are deemed to be material weaknesses. Any material weaknesses could result in a material misstatement of our annual or quarterly consolidated financial statements or disclosures that may not be prevented or detected.
paras.zh: 我们目前正在更新我们的控制流程，并预计在成为上市公司之前实现部分程序和系统的自动化，但我们对财务报告的内部控制目前尚不符合第 404 条所设想的全部标准，而我们最终将被要求达到这些标准。由于我们目前尚未对内部控制形成全面的文档记录，且尚未按照第 404 条对我们的内部控制进行测试，因此我们无法按照第 404 条得出结论，认定我们的内部控制不存在重大缺陷，或不存在可能导致得出我们的内部控制存在重大缺陷结论的多项重大缺陷的组合。在更新我们的控制流程以及实施与财务报告内部控制相关的必要程序和实践的过程中，我们已经识别出缺陷，并且未来可能识别出我们可能无法及时补救以满足《萨班斯-奥克斯利法案》就遵守第 404 条要求所规定期限的缺陷。此外，在完成对我们独立注册公共会计师事务所就出具其鉴证报告所识别的任何缺陷的补救方面，我们可能遇到问题或延误。我们的测试，或我们独立注册公共会计师事务所后续的测试（如要求），可能揭示我们财务报告内部控制中存在被视为重大缺陷的缺陷。任何重大缺陷都可能导致我们的年度或季度合并财务报表或披露出现重大错报，而此类错报可能无法被防止或发现。

paras.en: **Our insurance coverage strategy may not be adequate to protect us from all business risks.**
paras.zh: **我们的保险覆盖策略可能不足以保护我们免受所有业务风险的影响。**

paras.en: We may be subject, in the ordinary course of business, to losses resulting from accidents, acts of God and other claims against us, for which we may have no insurance coverage. As a general matter, we do not maintain as much insurance coverage as many other companies do, and in some cases, we do not maintain any at all, including with respect to our in-orbit satellites, which we currently do not insure and do not expect to insure in the future. Additionally, the policies that we do have may include significant deductibles or self-insured retentions, policy limitations and exclusions, and we cannot be certain that our insurance coverage will be sufficient to cover all future losses or claims against us. A loss that is uninsured or which exceeds policy limits may require us to pay substantial amounts, which may harm our financial condition and operating results.
paras.zh: 在正常经营过程中，我们可能因事故、不可抗力以及其他针对我们的索赔而遭受损失，而我们可能没有相应的保险覆盖。一般而言，我们维持的保险覆盖范围不如许多其他公司那么大，在某些情况下，我们根本不维持任何保险，包括对我们的在轨卫星，我们目前未为其投保，且预计未来也不会投保。此外，我们现有的保单可能包含高额免赔额或自留额、保单限制和除外责任，且我们无法确定我们的保险覆盖是否足以覆盖未来针对我们的所有损失或索赔。未投保或超过保单限额的损失可能要求我们支付大额款项，这可能损害我们的财务状况和经营业绩。

full.sec: Risks Related to Our Corporate Structure, Ownership of our Class A Common Stock and This Offering
full.secZh: 与我们的公司架构、A 类普通股所有权及本次发行相关的风险

paras.en: **Conflicts of interest could arise in the future between us, on the one hand, and Mr. Musk and entities owned by or affiliated with him, on the other hand, concerning among other things, business transactions, potential competitive activities or other business opportunities.**
paras.zh: **未来，本公司与马斯克先生及其拥有或关联的实体之间可能产生利益冲突，涉及（除其他事项外）业务交易、潜在竞争活动或其他商业机会。**

paras.en: Conflicts of interest could arise in the future between us, on the one hand, and Mr. Musk and entities owned by or affiliated with him, on the other hand, concerning among other things, business transactions, potential competitive business activities or other opportunities. In the normal course of business, we have engaged in a variety of transactions with some of these companies. Please refer to “Certain Relationships and Related Person Transactions.” In addition, we have previously engaged, are currently engaged, and expect to continue to engage in the future in a number of strategic collaborations with Tesla, including with respect to Macrohard and Terafab. Certain of these projects, including Macrohard and Terafab, are in the very early stages, as a result of which we and Tesla have not finalized a variety of details relating to our collaboration, including, but not limited to, financial terms, intellectual property rights, and the ultimate term of our collaboration. Furthermore, Mr. Musk and other businesses owned by or affiliated with him may now, or in the future, directly or indirectly, compete with us for investment or business opportunities.
paras.zh: 未来，本公司与马斯克先生及其拥有或关联的实体之间可能产生利益冲突，涉及（除其他事项外）业务交易、潜在竞争性业务活动或其他机会。在日常业务过程中，我们已与其中部分公司进行了各类交易。请参阅“特定关系及关联人士交易”。此外，我们此前已开展、目前正在开展，并预计未来将继续与 Tesla 开展多项战略合作，包括与 Macrohard 和 Terafab 相关的合作。其中部分项目（包括 Macrohard 和 Terafab）尚处于非常早期的阶段，因此本公司与 Tesla 尚未最终确定与我们合作相关的各项细节，包括但不限于财务条款、知识产权以及合作的最终期限。此外，马斯克先生及其拥有或关联的其他企业目前或未来可能直接或间接与我们竞争投资或商业机会。

paras.en: Mr. Musk or his affiliates may become aware, from time to time, of certain business opportunities (such as acquisition opportunities or technological developments) and may direct such opportunities to other businesses in which they have invested, in which case we may not become aware of or otherwise have the ability to pursue such opportunity. In addition, Mr. Musk and his affiliates may dispose of their interests in other companies or other assets in the future, without any obligation to offer us the opportunity to purchase any of those interests or assets.
paras.zh: 马斯克先生或其关联方可能不时知悉某些商业机会（例如收购机会或技术开发），并可能将该等机会导向其已投资的其他企业，在此情况下，我们可能无法知悉该等机会或以其他方式有能力把握该等机会。此外，马斯克先生及其关联方未来可能处置其在其他公司或其他资产中的权益，且无任何义务向我们提供购买任何该等权益或资产的机会。

paras.en: Under our charter, Mr. Musk and his affiliates are not restricted from owning assets or engaging in businesses that compete directly or indirectly with us and will not have any duty to refrain from engaging, directly or indirectly, in the same or similar business activities or lines of business as us, including those business activities or lines of business deemed to be competing with us, or doing business with any of our customers or vendors. Moreover, we have in the past entered into, and may in the future enter into, transactions with entities affiliated with Mr. Musk. We may enter into such transactions in lieu of pursuing other opportunities that some other shareholders may prefer or that may prove to be more accretive than the opportunities we elect to pursue. In any of these matters, the interests of Mr. Musk and entities owned by or affiliated with him may differ or conflict with the interests of our other shareholders. Any actual or perceived conflicts of interest with respect to the foregoing could have an adverse impact on the trading price of our Class A common stock.
paras.zh: 根据我们的公司章程，马斯克先生及其关联方不受限制拥有资产或从事与我们直接或间接竞争的业务，且无任何义务避免直接或间接从事与我们相同或类似的业务活动或业务线，包括被视为与我们竞争的业务活动或业务线，或与我们的任何客户或供应商开展业务。此外，我们过去曾与马斯克先生关联的实体进行交易，未来也可能进行此类交易。我们可能进行此类交易，以替代追求其他股东可能更青睐或可能被证明比我们所选择追求的机会更具增值效应的其他机会。在任何此类事项中，马斯克先生及其拥有或关联的实体的利益可能与我们的其他股东的利益不同或存在冲突。与上述事项相关的任何实际或感知到的利益冲突可能对我们的 A 类普通股交易价格产生不利影响。

paras.en: **Certain of our directors and key employees may have conflicts of interest because they are also employees or directors of affiliates of Mr. Musk or other large shareholders. The resolution of these conflicts of interest may not be in our or your best interests.**
paras.zh: **我们的部分董事和关键员工可能存在利益冲突，因为他们同时担任马斯克先生关联方或其他大股东关联方的员工或董事。此类利益冲突的解决方式可能不符合我们或您的最佳利益。**

paras.en: Certain of our directors and key employees may have conflicts of interest because they are also employees or directors of affiliates of Mr. Musk or other large shareholders. Such directors may have interests in, serve on the boards of, or have financial or other relationships with other companies, ventures, or initiatives that are related to or competitive with our business, including but not limited to other space or AI companies, technology ventures, satellite communications businesses, and government or commercial space contracts. Please refer to “Management.” These relationships and interests could create actual or perceived conflicts of interest, particularly with respect to the allocation of time, resources, business opportunities, or strategic decisions. In addition, our charter provides that, to the fullest extent permitted by applicable law, we renounce certain corporate opportunities that may be presented to Mr. Musk and certain of our directors and their respective affiliates, and such persons may have no duty to present such opportunities to us. Please refer to “Description of Capital Stock—Corporate Opportunities.” Any actual or perceived conflicts of interest could harm our reputation, lead to disputes, divert management attention, or result in decisions that are not in the best interests of us or our shareholders, which could materially and adversely affect our business, financial condition, results of operations, and future prospects.
paras.zh: 我们的部分董事和关键员工可能存在利益冲突，因为他们同时担任马斯克先生关联方或其他大股东关联方的员工或董事。此类董事可能在与我们业务相关或存在竞争关系的其他公司、合资企业或项目中拥有权益、担任董事会成员，或与之存在财务或其他关系，包括但不限于其他航天或 AI 公司、科技合资企业、卫星通信业务以及政府或商业航天合同。请参阅“管理层”。这些关系和权益可能产生实际或潜在的利益冲突，尤其是在时间、资源、商业机会或战略决策的分配方面。此外，我们的章程规定，在适用法律允许的最大范围内，我们放弃可能向马斯克先生及我们的部分董事及其各自关联方提供的某些公司机会，且该等人士可能无义务向我们提供该等机会。请参阅“股本说明——公司机会”。任何实际或潜在的利益冲突都可能损害我们的声誉、引发争议、分散管理层注意力，或导致不符合我们或我们股东最佳利益的决策，从而可能对我们的业务、财务状况、经营业绩和未来前景产生重大不利影响。

paras.en: **We are highly dependent on the continued services of Mr. Musk, our Chief Executive Officer and Chief Technical Officer, and other key personnel, and the loss or reduced involvement of one or more of these individuals could adversely affect our ability to execute our business strategy.**
paras.zh: **我们高度依赖我们的首席执行官兼首席技术官马斯克先生及其他关键人员的持续服务，一名或多名该等人士的流失或参与度降低可能对我们执行业务战略的能力产生不利影响。**

paras.en: We are highly dependent on the continued service and performance of Mr. Musk, whose leadership, vision, and expertise are critical to the development of our technologies and the execution of our business strategy. Mr. Musk has been, and continues to be, a driving force behind our growth, innovation, and operational success. The loss of Mr. Musk, whether due to death, disability, or otherwise, or his inability or unwillingness to continue in his current roles, could significantly disrupt our management structure, adversely affect our ability to execute our strategic plans, and negatively impact our reputation and relationships with customers, partners, and other stakeholders. Our intense, mission-driven, engineering-first culture has been a key driver of our growth and execution, and any erosion of this culture, including as a result of the loss or reduced involvement of Mr. Musk, could have a material adverse effect on our business, financial condition, results of operations, and future prospects. We do not maintain key-person life insurance on Mr. Musk. Further, although Mr. Musk devotes significant time to our businesses and is highly active in our management, he does not devote his full time and attention to our businesses and devotes time and attention to other significant roles (and may in the future serve in additional roles). For instance, Mr. Musk currently serves as Technoking and Chief Executive Officer of Tesla and is involved in other emerging technology ventures, including Neuralink and The Boring Company. Mr. Musk has also previously served as Senior Advisor to the President of the United States. Any such loss or reduced involvement in our business could result in a material adverse effect on our business, financial condition, results of operations, and future prospects. The process of identifying and recruiting a successor with the combination of skills and experience possessed by Mr. Musk, as well as the ability to maintain the confidence of the market, could be lengthy and uncertain, and there can be no assurance that we would be able to attract or retain a suitable replacement in a timely manner or at all.
paras.zh: 我们高度依赖马斯克先生的持续服务和表现，其领导力、愿景和专业能力对我们的技术开发和业务战略执行至关重要。马斯克先生一直并将继续是我们增长、创新和运营成功的推动力量。马斯克先生的流失，无论是因身故、丧失行为能力还是其他原因，或如其无法或不愿继续担任现任职务，都可能严重扰乱我们的管理架构，对我们执行战略计划的能力造成不利影响，并对我们的声誉以及与客户、合作伙伴和其他利益相关方的关系产生负面影响。我们强烈、以使命为驱动、以工程为先的文化是我们增长和执行的关键驱动力，这一文化的任何削弱，包括因马斯克先生的流失或参与度降低所致，都可能对我们的业务、财务状况、经营业绩和未来前景产生重大不利影响。我们未为马斯克先生投保关键人员人寿保险。此外，尽管马斯克先生为我们的业务投入大量时间并在我们的管理中高度活跃，但他并未将全部时间和精力投入我们的业务，而是将时间和精力投入到其他重要职务（且未来可能担任更多职务）。例如，马斯克先生目前担任 Tesla 的 Technoking 兼首席执行官，并参与其他新兴技术企业，包括 Neuralink 和 The Boring Company。马斯克先生此前还曾担任美国总统高级顾问。任何此类流失或对我们业务参与度的降低，都可能对我们的业务、财务状况、经营业绩和未来前景产生重大不利影响。寻找和招募具备马斯克先生所拥有的技能与经验组合、并能够维持市场信心的继任者的过程可能漫长且不确定，且无法保证我们能够及时或最终吸引或留住合适的替代人选。

paras.en: We, Mr. Musk, and other companies Mr. Musk is affiliated with frequently receive an immense amount of media attention. The actions and statements of Mr. Musk and his affiliated ventures, whether or not directly relating to us, may draw significant public attention and scrutiny to us and could potentially have a positive or negative impact on our business, relationships with customers and regulators, or stock price.
paras.zh: 我们、马斯克先生以及马斯克先生关联的其他公司经常受到大量媒体关注。马斯克先生及其关联企业的行为和言论，无论是否与我们直接相关，都可能吸引公众对我们的大量关注和审视，并可能对我们的业务、与客户和监管机构的关系或股价产生正面或负面影响。

paras.en: In addition to Mr. Musk, we have key personnel who are invaluable to our businesses. We rely upon their knowledge, expertise, and leadership to develop, manufacture, launch, sell, and support our products and services. None of our key employees are bound by an employment agreement for any specific term and we may not be able to successfully attract and retain the senior leadership necessary to continue to grow our business. Our compensation arrangements, such as our equity award programs, may not always be successful in attracting new employees and retaining and motivating existing key personnel. Our success depends upon our ability to attract and retain key personnel and any failure to do so could have a material adverse effect on our business, financial condition, results of operations, and future prospects.
paras.zh: 除马斯克先生外，我们还拥有对我们的业务至关重要的关键人员。我们依赖他们的知识、专业能力和领导力来开发、制造、推出、销售和支持我们的产品与服务。我们的关键员工均未签订约定了具体期限的雇佣协议，我们可能无法成功吸引并留住持续发展业务所需的高级领导人才。我们的薪酬安排（例如股权奖励计划）未必总能成功吸引新员工并留住和激励现有核心人员。我们的成功取决于我们吸引和留住关键人员的能力，若未能做到，可能对我们的业务、财务状况、经营业绩和未来前景产生重大不利影响。

paras.en: **A significant reduction by Mr. Musk or other existing shareholders of their ownership interest in us could adversely affect us.**
paras.zh: **马斯克先生或其他现有股东大幅减少其在我们公司的持股权益，可能对我们造成不利影响。**

paras.en: We believe that Mr. Musk’s substantial ownership interest in us provides him with an economic incentive to assist us to be successful. Upon the expiration or earlier waiver of the lock-up restrictions on transfers or sales of our securities following the completion of this offering, Mr. Musk will not be subject to any obligation to maintain his ownership interest in us and may elect at any time thereafter to sell all or a substantial portion of or otherwise reduce his ownership interest in us. If Mr. Musk sells all or a substantial portion of his ownership interest in us, he may have less incentive to assist in our success, which could adversely affect our future prospects. Additionally, future resales of our Class A common stock by Mr. Musk or other existing shareholders, or the perception that such sales may occur, could cause the market price of our Class A common stock to decline significantly, regardless of our actual business performance. In particular, subject to the expiration or waiver of any applicable lock-up period, parties to the Investors’ Rights Agreement described in “Certain Relationships and Related Person Transactions— Investors’ Rights Agreement” will have the right, subject to certain exceptions and conditions, to require us to register approximately 9.2 billion shares of Class A common stock (including shares of Class A common stock issuable upon conversion of Class B common stock) under the Securities Act of 1933, as amended (the “Securities Act”), and they will have the right to participate in certain future registrations of securities by us. Registration of any of such shares would result in such shares becoming freely tradable without compliance with Rule 144 limitations upon effectiveness of the registration statement. In addition, approximately 12.2 billion shares of Class A common stock (including shares of Class A common stock issuable upon conversion of Class B common stock) will generally be available for resale under Rule 144 starting 90 days after this offering, subject to lock-up restrictions described elsewhere in this prospectus. See “Certain Relationships and Related Person Transactions—Investors’ Rights Agreement” and “Shares Eligible for Future Sale—Registration Rights.”
paras.zh: 我们认为，马斯克先生在我们公司持有的大量所有者权益为他提供了经济激励，促使其协助我们取得成功。在本次发行完成后，对我们证券转让或出售的锁定期限制届满或提前豁免后，马斯克先生将不再负有维持其在我们公司所有者权益的任何义务，并可在其后任何时间选择出售其在我们公司全部或大部分所有者权益或以其他方式减少其在我们公司的所有者权益。如果马斯克先生出售其在我们公司全部或大部分所有者权益，他协助我们取得成功的激励可能减少，这可能对我们的未来前景产生不利影响。此外，马斯克先生或其他现有股东未来转售我们的 A 类普通股，或市场认为可能发生此类出售，可能导致我们的 A 类普通股市场价格大幅下跌，无论我们的实际业务表现如何。特别是，在适用锁定期届满或豁免的前提下，“某些关系及相关人士交易——投资者权利协议”中所述的投资者权利协议各方将有权（受某些例外和条件约束）要求我们根据经修订的 1933 年证券法（“证券法”）登记约 9.2 billion 股 A 类普通股（包括 B 类普通股转换后可发行的 A 类普通股），且他们将有权参与我们未来某些证券登记。任何此类股份的登记将导致该等股份在登记声明生效后无需遵守第 144 条限制即可自由交易。此外，约 12.2 billion 股 A 类普通股（包括 B 类普通股转换后可发行的 A 类普通股）通常将在本次发行后 90 天起可根据第 144 条转售，但受本招股说明书其他部分所述锁定期限制的约束。参见“某些关系及相关人士交易——投资者权利协议”和“未来可出售股份——登记权”。

paras.en: **Following the consummation of this offering, we will be a “controlled company” within the meaning of the Nasdaq and Nasdaq Texas listing rules and, as a result, will qualify for and rely on exemptions from certain corporate governance requirements.**
paras.zh: **本次发行完成后，我们将成为纳斯达克和纳斯达克得克萨斯上市规则所指的“受控公司”，因此将有资格并依赖某些公司治理要求的豁免。**

paras.en: Because Mr. Musk will beneficially own 849.5 million shares of Class A common stock and 5,569.1 million shares of Class B common stock (including 350.0 million shares of Class B common stock underlying options), which represents greater than 50% of the voting power of our common stock with respect to director elections and moreover, holders of our Class B common stock, voting separately as a class, will be entitled to elect 51% of the total number of authorized directors constituting our board (rounded up to the nearest whole number), following the completion of this offering, we will be a controlled company under the listing rules of Nasdaq and Nasdaq Texas.
paras.zh: 由于马斯克先生将实益拥有 849.5 million 股 A 类普通股和 5,569.1 million 股 B 类普通股（包括 350.0 million 股 B 类普通股标的期权），占我们普通股在董事选举方面投票权的 50%以上，此外，我们的 B 类普通股持有人作为单独类别投票，将有权选举占我们董事会授权董事总数 51%的董事（向上取整至最接近的整数），本次发行完成后，我们将成为纳斯达克和纳斯达克得克萨斯上市规则下的受控公司。

paras.en: Under the listing rules of Nasdaq and Nasdaq Texas, a company of which more than 50% of the voting power with respect to director elections is held by another person or group of persons acting together is a “controlled company” and may elect not to comply with certain Nasdaq and Nasdaq Texas corporate governance requirements, including the requirements that:
paras.zh: 根据纳斯达克和纳斯达克德克萨斯交易所的上市规则，若某公司董事选举投票权超过 50%由另一人或共同行动的一组人持有，该公司即为“受控公司”，并可以选择不遵守纳斯达克和纳斯达克德克萨斯交易所的某些公司治理要求，包括以下要求：

paras.en: - a majority of such company’s board of directors consist of independent directors as defined under the listing rules of Nasdaq and Nasdaq Texas;
paras.zh: - 该公司董事会多数成员应为纳斯达克和纳斯达克德克萨斯交易所上市规则所定义的独立董事；

paras.en: - director nominees be selected or recommended for board of directors’ selection by a nominating committee composed entirely of independent directors, with a written charter addressing the nominations process as required under the listing rules of Nasdaq and Nasdaq Texas;
paras.zh: - 董事候选人应由完全由独立董事组成的提名委员会遴选或推荐供董事会遴选，并须制定书面章程，按纳斯达克和纳斯达克德克萨斯交易所上市规则的要求载明提名程序；

paras.en: - the compensation committee be composed entirely of independent directors with a written charter addressing the committee’s purpose and responsibilities; and
paras.zh: - 薪酬委员会应完全由独立董事组成，并须制定书面章程载明该委员会的目的和职责；以及

paras.en: - annual performance evaluations of the compensation and nominating committees be conducted.
paras.zh: - 应对薪酬委员会和提名委员会进行年度绩效评估。

paras.en: Following the completion of this offering, we intend to utilize certain of these exemptions. As a result, we do not expect to have a compensation and nominating committee that is composed entirely of independent directors or that has a committee charter that addresses all Nasdaq and Nasdaq Texas requirements applicable to companies that are not controlled companies. Additionally, we may elect to take advantage of certain other exemptions in the future for as long as we remain a “controlled company.” Accordingly, our Class A shareholders will not have the same protections afforded to shareholders of companies that are subject to all of the corporate governance requirements of Nasdaq and Nasdaq Texas. In the event that we cease to be a “controlled company” and our shares continue to be listed on Nasdaq and Nasdaq Texas, we will be required to comply with all of the applicable governance requirements within the applicable transition periods. Please refer to “Management.”
paras.zh: 本次发行完成后，我们拟利用上述部分豁免。因此，我们预计不会设立完全由独立董事组成的薪酬与提名委员会，也不会制定涵盖纳斯达克和纳斯达克德克萨斯交易所对非受控公司适用的全部要求的委员会章程。此外，在我们仍为“受控公司”期间，我们未来可能会选择利用某些其他豁免。因此，我们的 A 类普通股股东将无法享有受纳斯达克和纳斯达克德克萨斯交易所全部公司治理要求约束的公司的股东所享有的同等保护。倘若我们不再属于“受控公司”且我们的股份继续在纳斯达克和纳斯达克德克萨斯交易所上市，我们将被要求在适用的过渡期内遵守所有适用的治理要求。请参阅“管理层”。

paras.en: **Our ability to provide returns to shareholders will depend on appreciation in our share price, as we do not plan to pay dividends for the foreseeable future.**
paras.zh: **我们向股东提供回报的能力将取决于我们股价的升值，因为我们不计划在可预见的未来派发股息。**

paras.en: The ability of investors to realize a return on their investment will depend largely on the appreciation of the price of our Class A common stock, as we do not anticipate paying dividends in the foreseeable future. We have never declared or paid any cash dividends on our common stock, and we currently intend to retain all available funds and any future earnings to support the growth and operation of our business, including investment in new technologies and commercial opportunities. As a result, investors seeking cash returns from their investment will not receive any dividend income, and the only way to realize a return may be through an increase in the market price of our Class A common stock, which may not occur. The trading price of our Class A common stock may be volatile and subject to wide fluctuations in response to various factors, including our financial condition and operating results, changes in our business or future prospects, technological innovations, announcements by us or our competitors, changes in the regulatory environment, harm to our brand and reputation, broader market or economic conditions, and the fact that a number of shares of our Class A common stock are expected to be allocated to retail investors in this offering. Additionally, high retail investor interest in our Class A common stock may occur following this offering, which may lead to increased volatility of the trading price. Some of these factors are outside of our control, and the trading price of our Class A common stock may not reflect our actual operating performance. Accordingly, investors may not be able to realize a gain on their investment and could lose all or part of their investment in our Class A common stock.
paras.zh: 投资者能否实现投资回报，将在很大程度上取决于我们 A 类普通股价格的升值，因为我们预计在可预见的未来不会派发股息。我们从未就普通股宣布或派发过任何现金股息，且我们目前拟保留所有可用资金及任何未来收益，以支持我们业务的增长和运营，包括对新技术和商业机会的投资。因此，寻求现金回报的投资者将不会获得任何股息收入，实现回报的唯一途径可能只有通过我们 A 类普通股市场价格的上涨，而这一上涨未必会发生。我们 A 类普通股的交易价格可能波动较大，并会因各种因素而出现大幅波动，这些因素包括我们的财务状况和经营业绩、我们业务或未来前景的变化、技术创新、我们或竞争对手的公告、监管环境的变化、我们的品牌和声誉受损、更广泛的市场或经济状况，以及本次发行中预计将有相当数量的 A 类普通股配售给散户投资者这一事实。此外，本次发行后，散户投资者对我们 A 类普通股的兴趣可能较高，这可能导致交易价格波动加剧。其中部分因素不在我们的控制范围内，我们 A 类普通股的交易价格可能无法反映我们的实际经营业绩。因此，投资者可能无法实现投资收益，并可能损失其在我们 A 类普通股中的全部或部分投资。

paras.en: **Upon completion of this offering, Mr. Musk will serve as our Chief Executive Officer, Chief Technical Officer, and Chairman of our board and control the election of our directors, and our dual class structure concentrates voting control with Mr. Musk and other holders of our Class B common stock. This will limit or preclude your ability to influence corporate matters and the election of our directors.**
paras.zh: **本次发行完成后，Musk 先生将担任我们的首席执行官、首席技术官及董事会主席，并控制我们董事的选举，且我们的双重股权结构将投票控制权集中于 Musk 先生及我们 B 类普通股的其他持有人。这将限制或妨碍您影响公司事务及选举我们董事的能力。**

paras.en: Our Class B common stock will have ten votes per share; our Class A common stock will have one vote per share; and, except as summarized here, our Class A common stock will vote together with our Class B common stock on any matter submitted to the shareholders for a vote. Under our charter, holders of our Class B common stock, voting separately as a class, will be entitled to elect 51% of the total number of authorized directors constituting our board (rounded up to the nearest whole number) and will have the ability to remove those directors for as long as there is at least one share of Class B common stock outstanding. As a result, holders of our Class B common stock will have control over the composition of our board and significant influence over the outcome of matters requiring shareholder approval. Please refer to “Description of Capital Stock” for certain other actions that will require approval of a majority of the voting power of the outstanding shares of Class B common stock voting separately as a class. This concentration of voting power will limit or preclude the ability of holders of our Class A common stock, including purchasers of Class A common stock in this offering, to influence corporate matters and the election of our directors.
paras.zh: 我们的 B 类普通股每股将拥有十票投票权；我们的 A 类普通股每股将拥有一票投票权；并且，除本招股说明书摘要所述情形外，我们的 A 类普通股将与我们的 B 类普通股就提交股东表决的任何事项共同投票。根据我们的公司章程，B 类普通股持有人作为单独类别单独投票，将有权选举占我们董事会授权董事总数 51%的董事（向上取整至最接近的整数），并且只要至少有一股 B 类普通股流通在外，即有权罢免该等董事。因此，B 类普通股持有人将控制我们董事会的构成，并对需要股东批准的事项的结果产生重大影响。有关需要作为单独类别单独投票的 B 类普通股流通股多数投票权批准的其他特定行动，请参见“股本说明”。这种投票权的集中将限制或排除我们的 A 类普通股持有人（包括本次发行中 A 类普通股的购买者）影响公司事务和我们董事选举的能力。

paras.en: Upon completion of this offering, Mr. Musk will beneficially own a majority of the outstanding shares of our Class B common stock and a majority of the voting power of the common stock (the Class A common stock and the Class B common stock voting together) and therefore will be able to elect all the members of our board. Mr. Musk, who will serve as our Chief Executive Officer and Chairman of our board under our charter and can only be removed from our board or these positions by the vote of Class B holders, as set forth in our charter, will exert significant influence over our business and affairs.
paras.zh: 本次发行完成后，Musk 先生将实益拥有我们 B 类普通股流通股的多数以及普通股（A 类普通股和 B 类普通股共同投票）投票权的多数，因此将能够选举我们董事会的全体成员。Musk 先生将根据我们的公司章程担任我们的首席执行官兼董事会主席，且根据我们的公司章程，只有经 B 类持有人投票方可将其从董事会或上述职位罢免，他将对我们的业务和事务产生重大影响。

paras.en: Class B common stock will continue to have ten votes per share, except that, subject to exceptions for certain inter-family transfers and transfers to certain entities that qualify as “permitted transferees” (as described elsewhere in this prospectus), transfers by holders of our Class B common stock will generally result in those shares converting to Class A common stock. The conversion of Class B common stock to Class A common stock will have the effect, over time, of increasing the relative voting power of those holders of Class B common stock who retain their shares. If Mr. Musk retains a significant portion of his holdings of Class B common stock for an extended period of time, he could continue to control the election and removal of a majority of our board.
paras.zh: B 类普通股将继续每股拥有十票投票权，但除某些家族内部转让以及向符合“获准受让人”资格的某些实体转让的例外情形（如本招股说明书其他部分所述）外，B 类普通股持有人转让股份通常将导致该等股份转换为 A 类普通股。B 类普通股转换为 A 类普通股将随着时间的推移产生增加保留其股份的 B 类普通股持有人相对投票权的效果。如果 Musk 先生在较长时期内保留其持有的 B 类普通股的相当大部分，他可能继续控制我们董事会多数成员的选举和罢免。

paras.en: However, other persons will also hold shares of Class B common stock. If Mr. Musk were to sell, transfer or otherwise dispose of a sufficient number of his shares of Class B common stock such that he no longer holds a majority of the outstanding shares of Class B common stock, another holder or group of holders of Class B common stock could obtain the ability to elect and remove a majority of our board and thereby effectively control the Company. Any such change in control could result in changes to our strategic direction, management, business plans or policies that may not be aligned with the interests of holders of our Class A common stock.
paras.zh: 然而，其他人士也将持有 B 类普通股股份。如果马斯克先生出售、转让或以其他方式处置其足够数量的 B 类普通股股份，以致其不再持有 B 类普通股已发行股份的多数，则 B 类普通股的另一名持有人或持有人集团可能获得选举和罢免我们董事会多数成员的能力，从而有效控制公司。任何此类控制权变更可能导致我们的战略方向、管理层、业务计划或政策发生变化，而这些变化可能与我们的 A 类普通股持有人的利益不一致。

paras.en: In addition, our charter will provide that other than for specified class votes by the Class B common stock or any rights granted to other classes in the future, classes of stock will not be entitled to any separate class votes provided for under the Texas Business Organizations Code (the “TBOC”), including among others (i) the increase or decrease of the aggregate number of authorized shares of a class outstanding, (ii) the exchange, reclassification, or cancellation of all or part of the shares of a class, (iii) a change of shares of a class, with or without par value, into the same or a different number of shares of the same or another class, with or without par value, (iv) the creation of a new class of shares with rights and preferences equal, prior, or superior to the shares of the class and (v) cancellation or other effectuation of the dividends on the shares of the class or series that have accrued but have not been declared.
paras.zh: 此外，我们的章程将规定，除 B 类普通股的特定类别表决或未来授予其他类别的任何权利外，各类股票将无权享有《得克萨斯州商业组织法典》（“TBOC”）所规定的任何单独类别表决权，其中包括（i）增加或减少某一类别已发行股份的授权股份总数，（ii）某一类别全部或部分股份的交换、重新分类或注销，（iii）将某一类别股份（无论是否有面值）变更为同一类别或另一类别的相同或不同数量的股份（无论是否有面值），（iv）创设具有与某一类别股份同等、优先或更优权利和优先权的新类别股份，以及（v）注销或以其他方式实施某一类别或系列股份上已累积但尚未宣派的股息。

paras.en: **The TBOC and our charter include provisions that may limit shareholders’ ability to bring a cause of action against our directors or officers for certain acts or omissions in their capacity as directors or officers of the Company, including minimum share ownership for derivative proceedings and the presumption of the business judgment rule.**
paras.zh: **TBOC 和我们的章程包含的条款可能限制股东就我们的董事或高级管理人员以公司董事或高级管理人员身份作出的某些作为或不作为提起诉讼的能力，包括衍生诉讼的最低持股要求以及商业判断规则的推定。**

paras.en: The TBOC and our governing documents include certain provisions that may limit our shareholders’ ability to bring certain derivative claims against our officers and directors. For example, the TBOC provides that, if a corporation has a class of stock listed on a national securities exchange, the governing documents may provide that the minimum ownership threshold for a shareholder or group of shareholders to institute or maintain a derivative proceeding is up to 3% of the outstanding shares of the corporation. Our bylaws will specify that the required ownership threshold for a shareholder or group of shareholders to institute or maintain a derivative proceeding in the right of the Company will be 3% of the outstanding shares of the Company. Based on the initial public offering price set forth on the cover page of this prospectus, 3% of our outstanding shares has a total dollar value of approximately $53 billion. A similar ownership threshold provision based on this 2025 TBOC provision has already been challenged in court proceedings involving another Texas corporation and, although the federal district court found the provision enforceable in that case, its enforceability or governing documents containing its provisions could be subject to further challenges or interpretation. The TBOC also permits corporations to request a court, at the start of a transaction (including a related party transaction) or inquiry into a derivative claim, to determine the independence and disinterestedness of directors serving on a special committee reviewing the transaction or directors or other individuals on panels reviewing derivative claims. Subsequent challenges to independence or disinterestedness would require new facts. Our bylaws will provide that these TBOC provisions will apply to us.
paras.zh: TBOC 及我们的治理文件包含某些条款，可能限制股东针对我们的高级管理人员和董事提起某些派生诉讼的能力。例如，TBOC 规定，若公司有一类股票在全国性证券交易所上市，治理文件可规定股东或股东集团提起或维持派生诉讼的最低持股门槛最高为公司已发行股份的 3%。我们的章程将规定，股东或股东集团以公司名义提起或维持派生诉讼所需的持股门槛为公司已发行股份的 3%。基于本招股说明书封面所载的首次公开发行价格，我们已发行股份的 3% 总美元价值约为 $53 billion。基于 2025 年 TBOC 该条款的类似持股门槛条款已在涉及另一家得克萨斯州公司的法院程序中受到质疑，尽管联邦地区法院在该案中认定该条款可执行，但其可执行性或包含该条款的治理文件可能面临进一步质疑或解释。TBOC 还允许公司在交易（包括关联方交易）开始或对派生索赔进行调查时，请求法院裁定在审查该交易的特别委员会任职的董事或在审查派生索赔的小组任职的董事或其他个人的独立性和无利害关系性。此后对独立性或无利害关系性的质疑将需要新的事实。我们的章程将规定这些 TBOC 条款适用于我们。

paras.en: In addition, Section 21.419 of the TBOC sets forth certain presumptions concerning compliance by directors and officers with respect to their duties to a corporation, including the duty of care and duty of loyalty. Specifically, in taking or declining to take any action on any matters of a corporation’s business, Section 21.419, which applies to us, provides that a director or officer is presumed to have acted (i) in good faith, (ii) on an informed basis, (iii) in furtherance of the interests of the corporation and (iv) in obedience to the law and the corporation’s governing documents. These provisions are described as codifying the “business judgment rule.” In order to succeed in a cause of action against a director or officer, the Company or a shareholder pursuing such an action must rebut one or more of the foregoing presumptions and prove with particularity the director or officer’s act or omission constituted a breach of duty as a director or officer and that such breach involved fraud, intentional misconduct, an ultra vires act or a knowing violation of law.
paras.zh: 此外，TBOC 第 21.419 条就董事和高级管理人员对公司义务（包括注意义务和忠实义务）的遵守情况设定了某些推定。具体而言，在就公司业务任何事项采取或不采取任何行动时，适用于我们的第 21.419 条规定，董事或高级管理人员被推定 (i) 出于善意、(ii) 在知情基础上、(iii) 为促进公司利益以及 (iv) 遵守法律和公司治理文件行事。这些条款被描述为将“商业判断规则”法典化。要在针对董事或高级管理人员的诉讼中胜诉，公司或提起该诉讼的股东必须推翻上述一项或多项推定，并具体证明该董事或高级管理人员的行为或不作为构成对其作为董事或高级管理人员义务的违反，且该违反涉及欺诈、故意不当行为、越权行为或明知违法。

paras.en: **Our bylaws will impose minimum stock ownership and solicitation requirements on shareholders seeking to submit proposals for shareholder approval, which could limit the ability of our shareholders to bring matters before a meeting of shareholders.**
paras.zh: **我们的章程将对寻求提交供股东批准的提案的股东施加最低持股和征集要求，这可能限制我们的股东将事项提交股东会议的能力。**

paras.en: Upon the completion of this offering, we will qualify as a “nationally listed corporation” under Section 21.373 of the TBOC, and our bylaws will provide that the shareholder proposal requirements permitted by that section will apply immediately upon qualifying as a “nationally listed corporation.” As a result, except with respect to director nominations and procedural resolutions ancillary to the conduct of a shareholders’ meeting, a shareholder or group of shareholders seeking to submit a proposal for approval at a meeting of shareholders will be required to satisfy specified ownership, holding-period and solicitation requirements. Under these provisions, the proposing shareholder or shareholder group must hold an amount of voting shares (determined as of the date of submission of the proposal) equal to at least 3% of our voting shares, must have held that amount continuously for at least six months before the date of the meeting and throughout the entire duration of the meeting, and must solicit holders of shares representing at least 67% of the voting power of shares entitled to vote on the proposal at the shareholder meeting. Based on the initial public offering price set forth on the cover page of this prospectus, 3% of our voting shares has a total dollar value of approximately $53 billion. For purposes of this paragraph, “voting shares” means shares that entitle the holder of the shares to vote on the proposal. These requirements are more restrictive than the requirements that would otherwise apply absent such a bylaw provision and may make it more difficult, or in some cases impracticable, for shareholders to submit proposals for consideration at a shareholders’ meeting. As a result, our shareholders may have fewer opportunities to present proposals for shareholder approval, even on matters they believe are important, which could limit shareholder influence over corporate governance and other matters. Section 21.373 of the TBOC was enacted in 2025 and, while its enforceability has not yet been challenged in court and we do not have any material concerns related to enforceability of Section 21.373 or the related bylaws provision, like many new laws, we expect the enforceability of TBOC Section 21.373 will eventually be challenged.
paras.zh: 本次发行完成后，我们将符合《得克萨斯州商业组织法典》（TBOC）第 21.373 条项下“全国性上市公司”的资格，且我们的章程将规定，该条所允许的股东提案要求将在我们符合“全国性上市公司”资格后立即适用。因此，除董事提名及与股东会议事程序相关的程序性决议外，寻求向股东会议提交提案以供批准的股东或股东集团将被要求满足特定的持股数量、持股期限及征集要求。根据上述规定，提出提案的股东或股东集团必须持有相当于我们至少 3%有表决权股份的股份数量（以提交提案之日确定），必须在会议日期前至少连续六个月持有该等数量股份并在会议整个期间持续持有，且必须征集代表有权在股东会议上对该提案投票的股份至少 67%表决权的股份持有人。基于本招股说明书封面所载的首次公开发行价格，我们 3%的有表决权股份的总美元价值约为$53 billion。就本段而言，“有表决权股份”指赋予其持有人对该提案投票权的股份。该等要求比在无此章程条款的情况下本应适用的要求更为严格，可能使股东更难、或在某些情况下不切实际地在股东会议上提交提案以供审议。因此，我们的股东可能拥有更少的机会提出供股东批准的提案，即使在其认为重要的事项上也是如此，这可能限制股东对公司治理及其他事项的影响力。TBOC 第 21.373 条于 2025 年颁布，尽管其可执行性尚未在法院受到质疑，且我们对第 21.373 条或相关章程条款的可执行性不存在任何重大疑虑，但与许多新法律一样，我们预计 TBOC 第 21.373 条的可执行性最终将受到质疑。

paras.en: **Our bylaws place restrictions on the forum, venue and procedures for legal actions or proceedings initiated by our shareholders, including certain requirements for mandatory arbitration. These provisions could limit our shareholders’ ability to pursue certain claims and/or increase the cost of doing so and could also affect the procedures, rights, and remedies available to our shareholders in such legal actions or proceedings.**
paras.zh: **我们的章程对股东提起的法律诉讼或程序的地点、管辖地和程序施加了限制，包括某些强制仲裁要求。该等条款可能限制我们的股东提起某些索赔的能力和/或增加其提起该等索赔的成本，还可能影响我们的股东在该等法律诉讼或程序中可获得的程序、权利和救济。**

paras.en: Our bylaws will contain a section (the “Forum Selection Bylaw”) that will provide that, unless the Company consents in writing to the selection of an alternative forum, the sole and exclusive forum for the filing, adjudication, and trial of all disputes between (i) one or more shareholders and (ii) the Company or its directors, officers, or controlling persons, or any underwriter of securities issued by the Company (or controlling person thereof) relating to any of the following: (1) any derivative proceeding, meaning a civil dispute brought in the right of the Company; (2) any action based on the governance, governing documents, or internal affairs of the Company; (3) any action based on state or federal securities or trade regulation laws; (4) any action based on the alleged act(s) or omission(s) by a person in its capacity as a shareholder, controlling person, director, officer or other managerial official of the Company; (5) any action based on the alleged breach(es) by one or more shareholders, controlling persons, directors, officers, or other managerial officials of a duty owed, in his or her capacity as such, to the Company or to any shareholder thereof; (6) an action seeking to hold a shareholder, controlling person, director, officer, or other managerial official of the Company liable for an obligation of the Company, other than on account of a written contract signed by the person to be held liable in a capacity other than as a shareholder or managerial official; and (7) any action arising out of the TBOC, will be the Texas Business Court, Eleventh Division (the “Business Court”) (for purposes of this summary, each, an “Internal Dispute”).
paras.zh: 我们的章程将包含一项条款（“管辖地选择章程条款”），规定除非公司书面同意选择替代管辖地，对于以下列各项相关事项引起的、(i) 一名或多名股东与 (ii) 公司或其董事、高级管理人员或控制人，或公司所发行证券的任何承销商（或其控制人）之间的所有争议的提起、裁决和审理，唯一且排他的管辖地为得克萨斯州商业法院第十一庭（“商业法院”）（就本摘要而言，每一项均称为“内部争议”）：(1) 任何派生诉讼，即代表公司权利提起的民事争议；(2) 任何基于公司治理、治理文件或内部事务的诉讼；(3) 任何基于州或联邦证券法或贸易监管法的诉讼；(4) 任何基于某人以其股东、控制人、董事、高级管理人员或其他管理官员身份作出的被指控的作为或不作为的诉讼；(5) 任何基于一名或多名股东、控制人、董事、高级管理人员或其他管理官员被指控违反其以该等身份对公司或其任何股东所负义务的诉讼；(6) 寻求要求公司股东、控制人、董事、高级管理人员或其他管理官员对公司义务承担责任的诉讼，但基于该被要求承担责任之人以非股东或管理官员身份签署的书面合同而产生的责任除外；以及 (7) 任何因《得克萨斯州商业组织法典》（TBOC）引起的诉讼。

paras.en: The selection of the Business Court as the exclusive forum for Internal Disputes may limit a shareholder’s ability to bring a claim in a judicial forum that it finds favorable for disputes with us or our directors, officers, other managerial officials, or other employees, which may discourage lawsuits against us and our directors, officers, other managerial officials, and other employees. Except to the extent that the Company consents in writing, or a court of competent jurisdiction determines in a final and unappealable judgment, that an Internal Dispute is not subject to the sole and exclusive venue and forum or jurisdiction of the Business Court or arbitration (as described further below), a shareholder will not be permitted to litigate an Internal Dispute in federal court or in any state court other than the Business Court, and will not be able to avail itself of any potential advantages or procedural protections of such other forums (subject to the provisions of Section 27 of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, as amended (the “Exchange Act”) discussed below). Any person or entity purchasing or otherwise acquiring any interest in our shares of capital stock will be deemed to have notice of and to have consented to these provisions. For more information, please refer to “Description of Capital Stock—Exclusive Forum and Venue and Arbitration, Jury Trial Waiver.”
paras.zh: 选择商业法院作为内部争议的排他管辖地，可能会限制股东就其与公司或我们的董事、高级管理人员、其他管理官员或其他员工之间的争议向其认为有利的司法管辖地提起诉讼的能力，这可能会抑制针对公司及我们的董事、高级管理人员、其他管理官员和其他员工的诉讼。除非公司书面同意，或有管辖权的法院在终局且不可上诉的判决中认定某项内部争议不受商业法院或仲裁（如下文进一步所述）的唯一排他管辖地和管辖地或管辖权的约束，否则股东不得在联邦法院或除商业法院以外的任何州法院就内部争议进行诉讼，也无法利用该等其他管辖地的任何潜在优势或程序性保护（受下文讨论的经修订的《1934 年证券交易法》（“《交易法》”）第 27 条规定的约束）。任何购买或以其他方式取得我们股本股份任何权益的个人或实体，将被视为已注意到并同意这些条款。有关更多信息，请参阅“股本说明——排他管辖地与管辖地及仲裁、陪审团审判豁免”。

paras.en: Section 27 of the Exchange Act creates exclusive federal jurisdiction over all suits brought to enforce any duty or liability created by the Exchange Act or the rules and regulations thereunder, and under Section 29 of the Exchange Act, investors cannot be required to waive compliance with the substantive obligations of the federal securities laws and the rules and regulations thereunder. Nonetheless, we believe federal case law interpreting the Exchange Act provides that the requirement under Section 27 of exclusive jurisdiction in federal court may be waived under certain circumstances. The Company’s position is that the Business Court can exercise jurisdiction over claims arising under the Exchange Act, because Texas law by statutory authority expressly gives the Business Court jurisdiction over such claims. Accordingly, we believe that under our Bylaws a shareholder bringing a claim under the Exchange Act, whether directly or on a derivative basis, must bring such a claim in the Business Court (and will not have available to them federal court).
paras.zh: 《交易法》第 27 条赋予联邦法院对所有为执行《交易法》或其项下规则和条例所创设的任何义务或责任而提起的诉讼的专属管辖权，且根据《交易法》第 29 条，不得要求投资者放弃遵守联邦证券法及其项下规则和条例的实质性义务。尽管如此，我们认为，解释《交易法》的联邦判例法规定，第 27 条项下的联邦法院专属管辖权要求在某些情况下可以放弃。公司的立场是，商业法院可以对依据《交易法》提起的索赔行使管辖权，因为德克萨斯州法律通过成文法授权明确赋予商业法院对此类索赔的管辖权。因此，我们认为，根据我们的章程，依据《交易法》提起索赔的股东，无论是直接提起还是以派生方式提起，均必须在商业法院提起该等索赔（且无法诉诸联邦法院）。

paras.en: The company’s position regarding the law governing the ability to consent to the selection of a state tribunal where there is explicit exclusive federal jurisdiction for certain actions brought under the federal securities laws (including the Exchange Act) is untested, and there is risk that, if an Internal Dispute were filed under the Exchange Act or the rules and regulations thereunder in a court other than the Business Court, that court could deny a motion by the Company to transfer the action to the Business Court pursuant to the Forum Selection Bylaw. In such a case, we and/or plaintiffs may incur additional expense and uncertainty of trying a case in a different forum or the forum might be arbitration (as further discussed below).
paras.zh: 公司关于在联邦证券法（包括《交易法》）项下某些诉讼存在明确联邦专属管辖权的情况下，同意选择州法院的适用法律立场尚未经过检验，且存在风险：如果依据《交易法》或其项下规则和条例在商业法院以外的法院提起内部争议，该法院可能驳回公司依据法院选择章程要求将诉讼移送至商业法院的动议。在此情况下，我们和/或原告可能因在不同法院审理案件而承担额外费用和不确定性，或者法院可能为仲裁（如下文进一步讨论）。

paras.en: Accordingly, the bylaws provide that to the extent that a court of competent jurisdiction (which is a court that possesses personal and subject matter jurisdiction) were to decline, in a final and unappealable judgment, to transfer an Internal Dispute to the Business Court (such Internal Dispute, an “Other Dispute”), such Other Dispute would be exclusively and finally settled by arbitration, pursuant to the Texas Arbitration Act, under the Expedited Procedure Provisions of the Rules of the International Chamber of Commerce, pursuant to Article 30 thereof. To be clear, absent Company consent, a shareholder would not be able to file an arbitration demand pursuant to the Dispute Resolution Clause without first obtaining a final and unappealable judgment declining to transfer that shareholder’s Internal Dispute to the Business Court. The governing law of such Other Dispute would be the federal law of the United States or the law of the State of Texas, as applicable to the issues raised in the Other Dispute, including without limitation the pleading and discovery limitations of the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act. If a court declines to transfer an Internal Dispute to the Business Court, but such court is later held not to have personal or subject matter jurisdiction with respect to such Internal Dispute, the arbitration provision would not be triggered because such action would be required to be dismissed and subsequently brought in a court of competent jurisdiction.
paras.zh: 因此，章程规定，若具有管辖权的法院（即同时具备属人管辖权和属事管辖权的法院）以终局且不可上诉的判决拒绝将内部争议移交商事法院（该等内部争议称为“其他争议”），则该等其他争议应依据《得克萨斯州仲裁法》，按照《国际商会仲裁规则》的快速程序条款并根据其第 30 条，通过仲裁排他且终局地解决。需明确的是，未经公司同意，股东不得在未首先取得拒绝将其内部争议移交商事法院的终局且不可上诉判决之前，依据争议解决条款提出仲裁请求。该等其他争议的准据法为美国联邦法律或得克萨斯州法律，视其他争议所涉问题而定，包括但不限于《私人证券诉讼改革法》关于诉答和证据开示的限制。若法院拒绝将内部争议移交商事法院，但该法院随后被认定对该内部争议不具有属人管辖权或属事管辖权，则仲裁条款将不会被触发，因为该诉讼应予驳回并随后向具有管辖权的法院提起。

paras.en: Given the unsettled nature of the law in this area, there is some risk that a court that has denied a motion to transfer an Internal Dispute to the Business Court pursuant to the Forum Selection Bylaw would also deny a motion to compel arbitration of such Other Dispute pursuant to the Forum Selection Bylaw. Accordingly, the Forum Selection Bylaw further provides that to the extent that a court of competent jurisdiction determines in a final and unappealable judgment that such Other Dispute cannot be compelled to arbitration pursuant to the Forum Selection Bylaw, the sole and exclusive forum for the adjudication and trial of such Other Dispute will be the United States District Court for the Southern District of Texas, Houston Division (the “Federal Court”).
paras.zh: 鉴于该领域法律尚不确定，存在一定风险：已依据法院选择章程驳回将内部争议移交商事法院动议的法院，也可能依据法院选择章程驳回强制将其他争议提交仲裁的动议。因此，法院选择章程进一步规定，若具有管辖权的法院以终局且不可上诉的判决认定该等其他争议不能依据法院选择章程强制提交仲裁，则该等其他争议的审理和审判的唯一排他性法院为美国得克萨斯州南区联邦地区法院休斯敦分院（“联邦法院”）。

paras.en: Finally, the Forum Selection Bylaw provides that to the extent that a court of competent jurisdiction determines in a final and unappealable judgment that the Federal Court lacks jurisdiction over any such Other Dispute, the sole and exclusive forum and venue for such Other Dispute will be the state district courts of Harris County, Texas.
paras.zh: 最后，法院选择章程规定，若具有管辖权的法院以终局且不可上诉的判决认定联邦法院对任何该等其他争议不具有管辖权，则该等其他争议的唯一排他性法院和审判地为得克萨斯州哈里斯县的州地区法院。

paras.en: Regardless of the forum, venue, or procedures selected for an Internal Dispute or Other Dispute, our bylaws shall require that any Internal Dispute or Other Disputes be brought only as an individual action or derivative proceeding, and, to the fullest extent permitted by law, shall prohibit shareholders from bringing such an Internal Dispute or Other Dispute as a class action, mass action, or other form of collective action or from being consolidated or joined, in whole or in part, consistent with the Arbitration Rules. However, the Company, at its sole option, may elect to seek consolidation or joinder of matters as consistent with the Arbitration Rules.
paras.zh: 无论为内部争议或其他争议选择何种论坛、管辖地或程序，我们的章程均应要求任何内部争议或其他争议仅以个人诉讼或派生诉讼的形式提起，并且在法律允许的最大范围内，应禁止股东以集体诉讼、大规模诉讼或其他形式的集体诉讼方式提起该等内部争议或其他争议，或禁止其全部或部分地被合并或并入，以符合仲裁规则。但是，公司可自行选择，按照仲裁规则寻求事项的合并或并入。
