However, we expect these dynamics to be offset by increased scale and technological advancement in our launch, satellite, and user terminal operations, ultimately supporting overall revenue growth and cost reduction. Our Starlink Subscriber monthly ARPU decreased from $86 per month for the three months ended March 31, 2025 to $66 per month for the three months ended March 31, 2026 and from $91 per month in 2024 to $81 per month in 2025. These decreases were driven primarily by international expansion and the addition of lower priced service plans.
paras.zh: Starlink 订阅用户 ARPU：我们将 ARPU 计算为该期间 Starlink 订阅用户产生的服务收入除以 (i) 该期间 Starlink 订阅用户的平均数，并除以 (ii) 该期间的月数。我们的战略侧重于通过运营效率和技术进步推动可持续的收入增长并扩大利润率，而非优先提高 ARPU。这一方针与我们扩大全球连接和市场准入的长期愿景相一致。我们预计，随着北美以外地区订阅用户群占比持续增长、我们新增较低价位的服务计划，以及我们调整宽带产品的月度服务计划费用，Starlink 订阅用户 ARPU 在未来几年总体上将继续下降。然而，我们预计这些动态将被我们发射、卫星和用户终端运营中规模扩大和技术进步所抵消，最终支撑整体收入增长和成本降低。我们的 Starlink 订阅用户月度 ARPU 从截至 2025 年 3 月 31 日止三个月的每月 $86 下降至截至 2026 年 3 月 31 日止三个月的每月 $66，并从 2024 年的每月 $91 下降至 2025 年的每月 $81。这些下降主要由国际扩张和新增较低价位的服务计划所驱动。

paras.en: Nameplate Compute Draw : We calculate Nameplate Compute Draw for a period as the number of GPUs installed in our data centers at the end of the period multiplied by their respective all-in power draw. Nameplate Compute Draw reflects installed capacity and does not represent actual power consumption or utilization. It does not include power we install and use for our supporting infrastructure such as cooling systems, power distribution losses, lighting, security systems, or facility-level overhead. Our Nameplate Compute Draw increased to 1.0 gigawatt as of March 31, 2026 as we brought COLOSSUS and COLOSSUS II online. We use this metric to assess our ability to deploy and scale compute capacity.
paras.zh: 名义算力功耗：我们将某一期间的名义算力功耗计算为该期间末我们数据中心内已安装的 GPU 数量乘以其各自的全部功耗。名义算力功耗反映的是已安装容量，并不代表实际电力消耗或利用率。它不包括我们为配套基础设施（如冷却系统、配电损耗、照明、安防系统或设施级管理费用）安装和使用的电力。随着我们将 COLOSSUS 和 COLOSSUS II 投入运行，截至 2026 年 3 月 31 日，我们的名义算力功耗增至 1.0 吉瓦。我们使用该指标来评估我们部署和扩展算力容量的能力。

paras.en: #### Segment Income (Loss) from Operations
paras.zh: #### 分部经营利润（亏损）

paras.en: Space Income (Loss) from Operations
paras.zh: 太空业务经营利润（亏损）

paras.en: Space loss from operations for the three months ended March 31, 2026 increased by $592 million to $(662) million compared to $(70) million for the three months ended March 31, 2025, primarily driven by an accelerated investment in development of the Starship vehicle as well as launch facilities to support future Starship launches, and a decrease in revenue from customer launches, partially offset by a decrease in cost of revenue, selling, general, and administrative expenses and impairment.
paras.zh: 截至 2026 年 3 月 31 日止三个月的太空业务经营亏损较截至 2025 年 3 月 31 日止三个月的 $(70) million 增加 $592 million，至 $(662) million，主要由于加速投资于 Starship 飞行器及发射设施的开发以支持未来的 Starship 发射，以及客户发射收入减少，部分被收入成本、销售、一般及行政费用和减值减少所抵消。

paras.en: Space income (loss) from operations for the year ended December 31, 2025 decreased by $678 million to $(657) million compared to $21 million for the year ended December 31, 2024, while Space income (loss) from operations for the year ended December 31, 2024 increased by $22 million to $21 million for the year ended December 31, 2024 compared to $(1) million for the year ended December 31, 2023. The year-over-year decrease in 2025 was primarily driven by an accelerated investment in development of the Starship vehicle as well as launch facilities to support future Starship launches, partially offset by an increase in revenue and decrease in cost of revenue.
paras.zh: 截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日止年度，太空业务经营收入（亏损）较截至 2024 年 12 月 31 日止年度的$21 million 减少$678 million 至$(657) million；而截至 2024 年 12 月 31 日止年度的太空业务经营收入（亏损）较截至 2023 年 12 月 31 日止年度的$(1) million 增加$22 million 至$21 million。2025 年的同比减少主要由于对 Starship 飞行器开发以及支持未来 Starship 发射的发射设施的投资加速，部分被收入增加和收入成本下降所抵消。

paras.en: Connectivity Income (Loss) from Operations
paras.zh: 连接业务经营利润（亏损）

paras.en: Connectivity income from operations for the three months ended March 31, 2026 increased by $155 million to $1,188 million compared to $1,033 million for the three months ended March 31, 2025, primarily driven by increased revenue from our consumer subscribers (composed of 104.7% growth in Starlink Subscribers, offset by a 22.9% decline in Starlink Subscriber ARPU, primarily due to international expansion and the addition of lower priced service plans) and enterprise business, partially offset by higher depreciation of capitalized launch and satellite costs due to the increase in Starlink flights, as well as higher operating expenses including ground operating costs and international expansion costs to support and drive subscriber growth.
paras.zh: 截至 2026 年 3 月 31 日止三个月的连接业务经营利润较截至 2025 年 3 月 31 日止三个月的 $1,033 million 增加 $155 million，至 $1,188 million，主要由于我们的消费者用户（由 Starlink 用户数增长 104.7% 构成，部分被 Starlink 用户 ARPU 下降 22.9% 所抵消，后者主要由于国际扩张及新增低价服务套餐）和企业业务收入增加，部分被因 Starlink 飞行次数增加导致的资本化发射及卫星成本折旧增加，以及包括地面运营成本和支持并推动用户增长的国际扩张成本在内的运营费用增加所抵消。

paras.en: Connectivity income from operations for 2025 increased by $2,417 million to $4,423 million compared to $2,006 million for the year ended December 31, 2024 while Connectivity income from operations for the year ended December 31, 2024 increased by $1,537 million to $2,006 million compared to $469 million for the year ended December 31, 2023. The year-over-year increase in 2025 was primarily driven by increased revenue from growth of our consumer and enterprise customers by $2,378 million and $1,410 million, respectively, partially offset by higher depreciation of capitalized launch and satellite costs due to the increase in Starlink flights, as well as higher marketing and international expansion costs to drive subscriber growth.
paras.zh: 2025 年连接业务经营利润较截至 2024 年 12 月 31 日止年度的 $2,006 增加 $2,417 至 $4,423，而截至 2024 年 12 月 31 日止年度的连接业务经营利润较截至 2023 年 12 月 31 日止年度的 $469 增加 $1,537 至 $2,006。2025 年的同比增长主要得益于我们消费类和企业类客户增长带来的收入分别增加 $2,378 和 $1,410，部分被因 Starlink 发射次数增加导致的资本化发射及卫星成本折旧增加，以及为推动订户增长而增加的营销和国际扩张成本所抵消。

paras.en: AI Income (Loss) from Operations
paras.zh: AI 经营利润（亏损）

paras.en: AI loss from operations for the three months ended March 31, 2026 increased by $1,533 million to $(2,469) million compared to $(936) million for the three months ended March 31, 2025, primarily driven by higher cloud computing and GPU depreciation costs, data center infrastructure and employee expenses, partially offset by higher revenue.
paras.zh: 截至 2026 年 3 月 31 日止三个月的 AI 经营亏损较截至 2025 年 3 月 31 日止三个月的 $(936) 增加 $1,533 至 $(2,469)，主要受云计算和 GPU 折旧成本、数据中心基础设施及员工费用增加推动，部分被收入增加所抵消。

paras.en: AI loss from operations for 2025 increased by $4,794 million to $(6,355) million compared to $(1,561) million for the year ended December 31, 2024, while AI loss from operations for the year ended December 31, 2024 decreased by $2,412 million to $(1,561) million compared to $(3,973) million for the year ended December 31, 2023. The increase in 2025 was primarily driven by higher cloud computing costs, facilities-related costs and employee expenses, partially offset by higher revenue.
paras.zh: 2025 年 AI 经营亏损较截至 2024 年 12 月 31 日止年度的 $(1,561) 增加 $4,794 至 $(6,355)，而截至 2024 年 12 月 31 日止年度的 AI 经营亏损较截至 2023 年 12 月 31 日止年度的 $(3,973) 减少 $2,412 至 $(1,561)。2025 年的增加主要受云计算成本、设施相关成本及员工费用增加推动，部分被收入增加所抵消。

paras.en: #### Segment Adjusted EBITDA
paras.zh: #### 分部调整后 EBITDA

paras.en: Segment Adjusted EBITDA is defined as segment income (loss) from operations excluding (i) depreciation and amortization, (ii) share-based compensation, (iii) restructuring charges and (iv) impairment.
paras.zh: 分部调整后 EBITDA 定义为分部经营利润（亏损）剔除(i)折旧及摊销、(ii)股份支付费用、(iii)重组费用及(iv)减值。

paras.en: Space Segment Adjusted EBITDA
paras.zh: 太空分部调整后 EBITDA

paras.en: Space Segment Adjusted EBITDA for the three months ended March 31, 2026 decreased by $575 million to $(351) million compared to $224 million for the three months ended March 31, 2025, primarily driven by an accelerated investment in development of the Starship vehicle as well as launch facilities to support future Starship launches, and a decrease in revenue from customer launches, partially offset by a decrease in cost of revenue, selling, general, and administrative expenses.
paras.zh: 截至 2026 年 3 月 31 日止三个月的太空分部调整后 EBITDA 较截至 2025 年 3 月 31 日止三个月的 $224 减少 $575 至 $(351)，主要受加速投资开发 Starship 运载工具及支持未来 Starship 发射的发射设施，以及客户发射收入减少推动，部分被收入成本、销售、一般及管理费用减少所抵消。

paras.en: Space Segment Adjusted EBITDA for 2025 decreased by $501 million to $653 million compared to $1,154 million in 2024, while Space Segment Adjusted EBITDA for 2024 increased by $157 million to $1,154 million compared to $997 million in 2023. The year-over-year decrease in 2025 was primarily driven by an accelerated investment in development of the Starship vehicle, as well as launch facilities to support future Starship launches, partially offset by an increase in NASA Cargo Resupply Services (CRS) for additional missions to the International Space Station, along with increased revenue from a U.S. Department of War contract. Our Space Segment Adjusted EBITDA is also driven by the reusability and efficiency of our rockets, which boosts cadence and reliability and supports a diversified base of commercial and government customers. These efforts have created a strong foundation for our Space Segment Adjusted EBITDA, and we believe position us to unlock further high-value opportunities in the expanding space economy.
paras.zh: 2025 年太空板块调整后 EBITDA 减少 $501 million 至 $653 million，而 2024 年为 $1,154 million；2024 年太空板块调整后 EBITDA 较 2023 年的 $997 million 增加 $157 million 至 $1,154 million。2025 年的同比减少主要由于对 Starship 飞行器开发以及支持未来 Starship 发射的发射设施的投资加速，部分被 NASA 货物补给服务（CRS）因向国际空间站执行更多任务而增加的收入以及来自美国战争部合同收入的增加所抵消。我们的太空板块调整后 EBITDA 还受益于火箭的可重复使用性和效率，这提升了发射频次和可靠性，并支撑了多元化的商业和政府客户基础。这些努力为我们的太空板块调整后 EBITDA 奠定了坚实基础，我们相信这使我们能够在不断扩大的太空经济中释放更多高价值机会。

paras.en: Connectivity Segment Adjusted EBITDA
paras.zh: 连接板块调整后 EBITDA

paras.en: Connectivity Segment Adjusted EBITDA for the three months ended March 31, 2026 increased by $469 million to $2,087 million compared to $1,618 million for the three months ended March 31, 2025, primarily driven by higher revenue from growth in consumer and enterprise revenue. Consumer revenue was composed of 104.7% growth in Starlink Subscribers, offset by a 22.9%decline in Starlink Subscriber ARPU, primarily due to international expansion and the addition of lower priced service plans. Enterprise and government revenue had an increase primarily driven by the growth in our aviation, maritime, mobility, and other enterprise business, partially offset by a decrease in our government business. These increases in revenue were offset by higher operating expenses for international expansion, and higher research and development costs.
paras.zh: 截至 2026 年 3 月 31 日止三个月的连接板块调整后 EBITDA 增加 $469 million 至 $2,087 million，而截至 2025 年 3 月 31 日止三个月为 $1,618 million，主要由于消费者和企业收入增长带来的收入增加。消费者收入由 Starlink 订户增长 104.7% 构成，但被 Starlink 订户 ARPU 下降 22.9% 所抵消，主要由于国际扩张以及新增低价服务套餐。企业和政府收入增长主要由于我们的航空、海事、移动及其他企业业务的增长，部分被政府业务下降所抵消。上述收入增长被国际扩张带来的更高运营费用以及更高的研发成本所抵消。

paras.en: Connectivity Segment Adjusted EBITDA for 2025 increased by $3,319 million to $7,168 million compared to $3,849 million in 2024 while Connectivity Segment Adjusted EBITDA for 2024 increased by $2,247 million to $3,849 million compared to $1,602 million in 2023. The year-over-year increase in 2025 was primarily driven by higher revenue from growth in our consumer and enterprise customers, partially offset by higher marketing and international expansion costs to grow our subscribers, as well as higher research and development costs for our next-generation product development. We have driven our strong sequential Connectivity Segment Adjusted EBITDA growth by expanding the scale and efficiency of our LEO satellite constellations and our highly verticalized supply chain, which has delivered major cost reductions in user terminal production.
paras.zh: 2025 年连接板块调整后 EBITDA 增加 $3,319 million 至 $7,168 million，而 2024 年为 $3,849 million；2024 年连接板块调整后 EBITDA 较 2023 年的 $1,602 million 增加 $2,247 million 至 $3,849 million。2025 年的同比增加主要由于消费者和企业客户增长带来的收入增加，部分被为增长订户而增加的营销和国际扩张成本以及下一代产品开发带来的更高研发成本所抵消。我们通过扩大 LEO 卫星星座的规模和效率以及高度垂直整合的供应链，推动了连接板块调整后 EBITDA 的强劲环比增长，这大幅降低了用户终端生产成本。

paras.en: AI Segment Adjusted EBITDA
paras.zh: AI 板块调整后 EBITDA

paras.en: AI Segment Adjusted EBITDA for the three months ended March 31, 2026 decreased by $497 million to $(609) million compared to $(112) million for the three months ended March 31, 2025, primarily driven by higher cloud compute and data center infrastructure and operating costs, and employee compensation expenses, partially offset by higher revenue.
paras.zh: 截至 2026 年 3 月 31 日止三个月的 AI 板块调整后 EBITDA 减少 $497 million 至 $(609) million，而截至 2025 年 3 月 31 日止三个月为 $(112) million，主要由于云算力和数据中心基础设施及运营成本以及员工薪酬费用增加，部分被收入增加所抵消。

paras.en: AI Segment Adjusted EBITDA for 2025 decreased by $1,584 million to $(1,237) million compared to $347 million in 2024 while AI Segment Adjusted EBITDA for 2024 decreased by $875 million to $347 million, compared to $1,222 million in 2023. The decrease in 2025 was primarily driven by higher cloud computing costs, facilities-related costs and employee expenses, partially offset by higher revenue. AI Segment Adjusted EBITDA is primarily driven by our strategy to rapidly and cost-effectively scale compute infrastructure. We expect to continue to expand our terrestrial data centers, and to launch orbital data centers, and we expect a multi-year investment horizon before these deployments translate into sustained positive Segment Adjusted EBITDA for our AI segment.
paras.zh: 2025 年 AI 板块调整后 EBITDA 减少 $1,584 百万至 $(1,237) 百万，而 2024 年为 $347 百万；2024 年 AI 板块调整后 EBITDA 减少 $875 百万至 $347 百万，而 2023 年为 $1,222 百万。2025 年的减少主要由于云计算成本、设施相关成本及员工费用上升，部分被收入增长所抵消。AI 板块调整后 EBITDA 主要受我们快速且具成本效益地扩展算力基础设施的战略所驱动。我们预计将继续扩建地面数据中心，并推出轨道数据中心，且预计在这些部署转化为 AI 板块持续正的板块调整后 EBITDA 之前，将经历多年的投资期。

paras.en: Segment Adjusted EBITDA is a non-GAAP measure. Please refer to the section titled “—Non-GAAP Financial Measures” for additional information on our non-GAAP financial measures, including reconciliations of Segment Adjusted EBITDA to segment income (loss) from operations, the most directly comparable GAAP measure.
paras.zh: 板块调整后 EBITDA 是一项非 GAAP 指标。有关我们非 GAAP 财务指标的更多信息，包括板块调整后 EBITDA 与经营分部收入（亏损）（最直接可比的 GAAP 指标）的对账，请参阅标题为“—非 GAAP 财务指标”的章节。

paras.zh: 2025 年太空资本支出增加 $1,800 百万至 $3,832 百万，而 2024 年为 $2,032 百万；2024 年太空资本支出增加 $535 百万至 $2,032 百万，而 2023 年为 $1,497 百万。各同比期间的增加主要由于我们对 Starship 发射场基础设施的投资增加。

paras.zh: 2025 年连接资本支出增加 $680 百万至 $4,178 百万，而 2024 年为 $3,498 百万；2024 年连接资本支出增加 $1,043 百万至 $3,498 百万，而 2023 年为 $2,455 百万。各同比期间的增加主要由于在我们持续增加卫星数量并扩展卫星网络的过程中，卫星及地面设备成本上升。

paras.en: AI Capital Expenditures
paras.zh: AI 资本支出

paras.en: AI capital expenditures for the three months ended March 31, 2026 increased $5,156 million to $7,723 million compared to $2,567 million for the three months ended March 31, 2025. The increase was primarily driven by investments in the rapid expansion of our terrestrial data centers, including the development, construction, and equipping of new facilities and supporting infrastructure.
paras.zh: 截至 2026 年 3 月 31 日止三个月的 AI 资本支出增加 $5,156 百万至 $7,723 百万，而截至 2025 年 3 月 31 日止三个月为 $2,567 百万。该增加主要由于对我们地面数据中心快速扩张的投资，包括新设施及配套基础设施的开发、建设和设备配置。

paras.en: AI capital expenditures for 2025 increased $7,094 million to $12,727 million compared to $5,633 million in 2024, while AI capital expenditures for 2024 increased $5,170 million to $5,633 million compared to $463 million in 2023. This increase was primarily driven by significant investments in the rapid expansion of our terrestrial data centers, including the development, construction, and equipping of new facilities and supporting infrastructure.
paras.zh: 2025 年的 AI 资本支出增加 $7,094 百万至 $12,727 百万，而 2024 年为 $5,633 百万；2024 年的 AI 资本支出增加 $5,170 百万至 $5,633 百万，而 2023 年为 $463 百万。该增加主要由于对我们地面数据中心快速扩张的重大投资，包括新设施及配套基础设施的开发、建设和设备配置。

paras.en: Developing Starship. Starship is our next-generation vehicle that we expect will dramatically expand our launch capability through full and rapid reusability combined with unprecedented mass to orbit capability. As the most powerful launch system ever developed, we expect that Starship V3 will be able to carry a payload of 100 metric tons, and that future generations could reach 200 metric tons, potentially as soon as Starship V4. Starship is central to our goal of unlocking growth through our unique vertically integrated business model. Starship is expected to be the only vehicle with fully reusable first and second stages, which is critical to reducing launch costs and increasing launch cadence. We believe that Starship can eventually reduce the cost to reach orbit by 99% or more relative to the historical average launch cost per kilogram according to NASA of $18,500, establishing a scalable path to creating the infrastructure of the future, such as orbital AI compute.
paras.zh: 研发星舰。星舰是我们的下一代运载工具，我们预计它将通过完全且快速的重复使用能力，结合前所未有的入轨质量能力，大幅扩展我们的发射能力。作为有史以来研发的最强大发射系统，我们预计星舰 V3 将能够运载 100 公吨的有效载荷，而未来版本可能达到 200 公吨，最早可能在星舰 V4 实现。星舰对于我们通过独特的垂直一体化商业模式实现增长的目标至关重要。星舰预计将成为唯一拥有完全可重复使用一级和二级的运载工具，这对于降低发射成本和提高发射频次至关重要。我们相信，根据 NASA 的数据，星舰最终能够将入轨成本相对于每公斤 18,500 美元的历史平均发射成本降低 99% 或更多，从而开辟一条可扩展的路径，以构建未来的基础设施，例如轨道 AI 算力。

paras.en: We have already demonstrated catching and reusing the first stage booster for Starship through our innovative “chopsticks” method to catch the booster. To date, we have executed 12 Starship flight tests, with our 12th flight test in May 2026 debuting the next generation Starship vehicle and Super Heavy booster. This next-generation Starship introduces major changes for better orbital performance and reusability. We plan to demonstrate key development milestones of catching the upper stage and demonstrating in-orbit propellant transfer capabilities. These milestones will be the key unlocks for a rapidly reusable rocket that we expect will take hundreds of thousand s of tons of mass to orbit to drive growth in our Connectivity and AI segments, and allow us to develop the lunar economy and eventually to reach Mars. We expect Starship to commence payload delivery to orbit in the second half of 2026 following additional flight tests. For additional information about this risk, please refer to “Risk Factors—Risks Related to Our Business—Any failure or delay in the development of Starship at scale or in achieving the required launch cadence, reusability and capabilities thereafter would delay or limit our ability to execute our growth strategy, including the deployment of next-generation satellites, global satellite-to-mobile connectivity, and orbital AI compute, which could materially adversely affect our business, financial condition, results of operations, and future prospects” in this prospectus.
paras.zh: 我们已经通过创新的“筷子”方法捕获助推器，展示了捕获并重复使用星舰一级助推器的能力。迄今为止，我们已执行 12 次星舰飞行测试，其中 2026 年 5 月的第 12 次飞行测试首次亮相了下一代星舰运载工具和超重型助推器。这一下一代星舰引入了重大变更，以实现更好的轨道性能和可重复使用性。我们计划展示捕获上面级和展示在轨推进剂转移能力的关键研发里程碑。这些里程碑将是实现快速可重复使用火箭的关键突破，我们预计该火箭将把数十万吨质量送入轨道，以推动我们互联和 AI 板块的增长，并使我们能够发展月球经济，最终抵达火星。我们预计星舰将在额外的飞行测试之后，于 2026 年下半年开始向轨道运送有效载荷。有关此风险的更多信息，请参阅本招股说明书中的“风险因素——与我们业务相关的风险——星舰规模化研发的任何失败或延迟，或此后未能实现所需的发射频次、可重复使用性和能力，都将延迟或限制我们执行增长战略的能力，包括部署下一代卫星、全球卫星到移动连接和轨道 AI 算力，这可能对我们的业务、财务状况、经营业绩和未来前景产生重大不利影响”。

paras.en: Launch Costs and Cadence. Our launch costs and cadence underpin the foundational competitive advantage that enables the performance of each of our segments. The reusability of our launch vehicles meaningfully reduces the cost per kilogram to orbit by eliminating or limiting the need to manufacture new vehicles for every mission.
paras.zh: 发射成本与频次。我们的发射成本和频次构成了基础性竞争优势，支撑着我们每个板块的业绩表现。我们运载工具的可重复使用性通过消除或减少为每次任务制造新运载工具的需求，显著降低了每公斤入轨成本。

paras.en: Reusability also enables higher launch cadence by shortening the time between flights, as vehicles can be rapidly reflown after their return. These factors enable performance in our Connectivity segment by supporting faster and more cost‑effective deployment of our satellite constellations. We expect they will support our AI segment as we aim to deploy a large fleet of orbital AI compute. We expect continued enhancements to our launch infrastructure and launch vehicles, including Starship, to drive cost down and throughput up, extending these benefits to our businesses, as well as to our third‑party customers who rely on our launch capabilities. As we continue to reduce launch costs and increase launch cadence, we expect to transform the rocket launch industry into airline-like operations, enabling continuous and affordable access to space. Period-to-period comparisons of launch costs and cadence are impacted by factors out of our control, including timing of delivery of customer payloads which impacts the mix of customer and internal payloads and related financial reporting, or weather which can delay a launch from one period to another.
paras.zh: 可重复使用性还通过缩短飞行之间的时间间隔实现了更高的发射频率，因为飞行器在返回后可以快速再次飞行。这些因素通过支持更快、更具成本效益地部署我们的卫星星座，使我们互联业务板块的性能得以实现。我们预计它们将支持我们的 AI 业务板块，因为我们旨在部署大规模轨道 AI 算力集群。我们预计，包括 Starship 在内的发射基础设施和运载火箭的持续改进将推动成本下降、吞吐量提升，从而将这些益处延伸至我们的各项业务，以及依赖我们发射能力的第三方客户。随着我们持续降低发射成本并提高发射频率，我们预计将把火箭发射行业转变为类似航空公司的运营模式，实现持续且可负担的太空准入。发射成本和发射频率的期间对比会受到我们无法控制的因素影响，包括客户有效载荷交付时间（这会影响客户与内部有效载荷的组合及相关财务报告），或可能将发射从一个期间推迟到另一个期间的天气因素。

paras.en: Increasing Satellite Capacity. The scale, reliability, and capacity of our LEO broadband and mobile satellite constellations drive our Connectivity segment’s growth and operating performance. In 2025, launching and operating higher-throughput satellites supported Starlink’s service quality and customer reach by increasing available network capacity and improving service consistency during peak usage periods. As of March 31, 2026, we operated over 9,600 Starlink broadband and mobile satellites in Low-Earth Orbit, with the majority composed of our second-generation, V2 Mini satellites. We expect to commence deploying our next-generation V3 satellites, designed to offer one Tbps of downlink capacity per satellite, using Starship in the second half of 2026 and expect that a single Starship launch will be capable of deploying up to 60 V3 satellites to LEO, representing a twenty-fold increase in Starlink downlink capacity deployed relative to a Falcon 9 launch.
paras.zh: 提升卫星容量。我们低地球轨道（LEO）宽带和移动卫星星座的规模、可靠性和容量驱动着我们互联业务板块的增长和经营表现。2025 年，发射和运营更高吞吐量的卫星通过增加可用网络容量并改善高峰使用期间的服务一致性，支持了 Starlink 的服务质量和客户覆盖。截至 2026 年 3 月 31 日，我们在低地球轨道运营着超过 9,600 颗 Starlink 宽带和移动卫星，其中大部分为我们的第二代 V2 Mini 卫星。我们预计将于 2026 年下半年开始使用 Starship 部署我们的下一代 V3 卫星，该卫星设计为每颗提供 1 Tbps 的下行容量，并预计单次 Starship 发射将能够向 LEO 部署最多 60 颗 V3 卫星，相当于相对于 Falcon 9 发射所部署的 Starlink 下行容量增加二十倍。

paras.en: We also provide satellite-to-mobile connectivity, supplementing terrestrial networks and substantially reducing mobile “dead zones” in approximately 30 countries. Since January 2025, we have grown our constellation from approximately 360 V1 Mobile satellites to approximately 650 V1 Mobile satellites. Through this constellation and in partnership with more than 30 mobile network operators, we provided data, over-the-top voice, and messaging services to approximately 7.4 million monthly unique devices across approximately 30 countries. During 2025, we also entered into agreements to acquire 65 MHz of spectrum in the United States as well as certain global Mobile Satellite Service spectrum licenses from EchoStar for $19.6 billion of equity and cash consideration, as described below under “—Liquidity and Capital Resources—Material Cash Commitments.” We expect the spectrum acquisition to close in November 2027, subject to required regulatory approvals and other closing conditions. We expect the wider bandwidth operations enabled by this spectrum purchase, together with our authorization to deploy 7,500 satellites including with the 2GHz spectrum band, will provide stronger support for current performance and potential future services, including broadband data and IoT connectivity, and is expected to enable 5G connectivity.
paras.zh: 我们还提供卫星到移动设备的连接服务，作为地面网络的补充，并在约 30 个国家大幅减少移动网络“盲区”。自 2025 年 1 月以来，我们的星座已从约 360 颗 V1 Mobile 卫星增长至约 650 颗 V1 Mobile 卫星。通过该星座，并与 30 多家移动网络运营商合作，我们为约 30 个国家约 740 万台月度唯一设备提供了数据、OTT 语音和消息服务。2025 年期间，我们还签订了协议，以 196 亿美元的股权和现金对价收购美国 65 MHz 频谱以及 EchoStar 的某些全球移动卫星服务频谱许可证，详见下文“——流动性与资本资源——重大现金承诺”。我们预计该频谱收购将于 2027 年 11 月完成，但须获得所需的监管批准及其他交割条件。我们预计，此次频谱购买所支持的更宽带宽运营，连同我们部署 7,500 颗卫星（包括使用 2GHz 频段）的授权，将为当前业绩和潜在未来服务（包括宽带数据和 IoT 连接）提供更强支持，并预计将实现 5G 连接。

paras.en: These investments in satellite scale, per-satellite capacity, and expanded capabilities are instrumental to the growth and operating performance of our Connectivity segment, enabling us to onboard new users while improving service quality.
paras.zh: 这些对卫星规模、单星容量和扩展能力的投资，对我们连接业务的增长和经营业绩至关重要，使我们能够吸纳新用户，同时提升服务质量。

paras.en: Increasing Starlink Brand Awareness and Acquiring New Subscribers. Our growth is driven in part by increased global awareness of Starlink’s capabilities and our ability to convert that awareness into customer adoption. Trust, visibility, and demonstrated reliability are central to customer acquisition, particularly for those in remote and infrastructure-limited regions. Proven performance in rural, remote, and disaster-affected areas, along with strong brand awareness, reinforces Starlink’s reputation as essential infrastructure, leading to higher adoption in new markets.
paras.zh: 提升 Starlink 品牌知名度并获取新用户。我们的增长部分得益于全球对 Starlink 能力的认知提升，以及我们将这种认知转化为客户采用的能力。信任、可见度和经证实的可靠性是客户获取的核心，尤其是对于偏远和基础设施有限地区的客户。在农村、偏远和受灾地区经过验证的表现，加上强大的品牌知名度，巩固了 Starlink 作为关键基础设施的声誉，从而推动新市场的更高采用率。

paras.en: As of March 31, 2026, we had over 9,600 Starlink broadband and mobile satellites in Low-Earth Orbit, operating the world’s most advanced broadband constellation providing internet connectivity to approximately 10.3 million Starlink Subscribers across 164 countries, territories, and other markets, collectively home to more than 3.3 billion people. We are focused on growing the number of Starlink Subscribers by expanding our consumer distribution network across thousand s of authorized retail stores globally, and executing region-specific marketing campaigns to increase brand awareness. By clearly demonstrating Starlink’s superior speed, low-latency, and ease of installation, we expect to drive meaningful subscriber growth.
paras.zh: 截至 2026 年 3 月 31 日，我们在低地球轨道拥有超过 9,600 颗 Starlink 宽带和移动卫星，运营着全球最先进的宽带星座，为遍布 164 个国家、地区及其他市场的约 10.3 百万 Starlink 用户提供互联网连接，这些市场合计居住着超过 3.3 十亿人口。我们专注于通过在全球数千家授权零售门店扩展消费者分销网络，并执行针对特定区域的营销活动以提升品牌知名度，从而增加 Starlink 用户数量。通过清晰展示 Starlink 卓越的速度、低延迟和易于安装的特点，我们预计将推动用户数量实现显著增长。

paras.en: Increasing Enterprise Customer Adoption. As we continue to grow our Starlink constellation and bandwidth, we see a large opportunity to grow the enterprise connectivity market by providing solutions that had not previously been available. Our network is global and can provide primary connectivity for on-the-move applications as well as a resilient backup option for enterprises serviced by land-based connectivity. We plan to deepen our penetration with enterprise and government customers through direct, vertical-specific acquisition strategies. In recent years, we have assembled dedicated sales and engineering teams to market and support fleet-wide conversions in aviation and maritime, customized deployments for land mobility, which we expect to continue to grow as consumers who experience Starlink begin to expect high-performance connectivity when traveling. We expect to enable more customized deployments for land mobility across existing use cases such as commercial trucking fleets, and new applications enabled by more connected devices. We also continue to develop specialized networks for secure government applications via Starshield. By leveraging proven performance in mission-critical environments and expanding through channel partners in select geographies, we expect to drive increased adoption among high-value enterprise and government accounts.
paras.zh: 企业客户采用率不断提升。随着我们持续扩大 Starlink 星座规模与带宽，我们看到通过提供此前无法获得的解决方案来拓展企业连接市场的巨大机遇。我们的网络覆盖全球，可为移动中的应用提供主用连接，也可为依赖地面连接的企业提供具备韧性的备用选项。我们计划通过针对特定垂直行业的直销策略，深化在企业及政府客户中的渗透。近年来，我们组建了专门的销售与工程团队，以推广并支持航空和海事领域的整机队改造，以及陆地移动场景的定制化部署；我们预计，随着体验过 Starlink 的消费者开始期望在出行时获得高性能连接，这一业务将继续增长。我们预计将在商用卡车车队等现有用例以及由更多联网设备催生的新应用中，实现更多陆地移动场景的定制化部署。我们还将继续通过 Starshield 为安全政府应用开发专用网络。凭借在关键任务环境中经过验证的性能，并通过特定地区的渠道合作伙伴进行拓展，我们预计将推动高价值企业及政府客户的采用率进一步提升。

paras.en: Accelerating Investment in Growth and Innovation. We are simultaneously developing and scaling a wide range of complex, capital‑intensive projects, including Starship and terrestrial and orbital AI compute. We believe speed is a competitive advantage, and periodically we decide to increase and accelerate our investments. For example, in 2025 we accelerated our timeline for Starship development, increasing R&D in our Space segment to $3,004 million, compared to $1,835 million in 2024. In our AI segment, in 2025 we successfully accelerated deployment of compute for the development of Grok, increasing R&D in our AI segment to $5,064 million, compared to $1,176 million in 2024. We believe pursuing multiple ambitious programs in parallel enables us to compound advantages across our vertically integrated innovation engine and unlock new large addressable markets over time. The timing of our investments is not fixed and may accelerate based on technical progress, market opportunity, or resource availability. As a result, our operating results, margins and profitability may fluctuate from period to period as we continue to prioritize execution speed, capacity expansion, and technological leadership over near‑term margin optimization. We believe that this approach maximizes long‑term value creation by allowing us to move faster than competitors, scale earlier in emerging markets, and reinforce durable competitive advantages that we expect to benefit our business over time.
paras.zh: 加快对增长与创新的投资。我们同时在开发和扩展一系列复杂且资本密集的项目，包括 Starship 以及地面和轨道 AI 算力。我们认为速度是一种竞争优势，并会定期决定增加和加快我们的投资。例如，2025 年我们加快了 Starship 的开发时间表，将太空板块的研发费用增至 $3,004 million，而 2024 年为 $1,835 million。在 AI 板块，2025 年我们成功加快了用于 Grok 开发的算力部署，将 AI 板块的研发费用增至 $5,064 million，而 2024 年为 $1,176 million。我们相信，并行推进多个雄心勃勃的项目，使我们能够在垂直整合的创新引擎上实现优势叠加，并随着时间推移解锁新的大型可寻址市场。我们的投资时点并非固定不变，并可能根据技术进展、市场机遇或资源可用性而加快。因此，由于我们继续将执行速度、产能扩张和技术领先置于近期利润率优化之上，我们的经营业绩、利润率和盈利能力可能逐期波动。我们相信，这一策略使我们能够比竞争对手行动更快、在新兴市场更早实现规模化，并强化持久的竞争优势，从而最大化长期价值创造，我们预计这将随着时间推移为我们的业务带来裨益。

paras.en: Supply Chain and Manufacturing Efficiency for User Terminals. The operating performance of our Connectivity segment depends in part on the cost and availability of user terminals at scale. We are vertically integrated across terminal design, production, and support, including silicon, hardware, software, manufacturing, fulfillment, and operations, which enables us to control our means of production as well as rapidly iterate to continuously improve the performance of our user terminals and optimize product cost. Since our initial launch of our user terminal, we have optimized the design of our phased-array antennas, our self-aligning antenna responsible for connecting user equipment to our LEO satellite network, for manufacturability and high-volume scale. Over the past five years, we have significantly lowered production costs and have scaled terminal output to approximately 200,000 terminals per week. We plan to continue to further scale production significantly and make gains that improve margins, lower customer barriers, and broaden addressable markets.
paras.zh: 用户终端的供应链与制造效率。我们互联业务板块的经营业绩部分取决于用户终端规模化供应的成本与可获得性。我们在终端设计、生产和支持方面实现垂直整合，涵盖芯片、硬件、软件、制造、履约和运营，这使我们能够掌控自身的生产方式，并快速迭代，以持续提升用户终端性能并优化产品成本。自用户终端首次推出以来，我们已针对可制造性和大批量规模化，优化了相控阵天线（即负责将用户设备连接至我们 LEO 卫星网络的自对准天线）的设计。过去五年间，我们大幅降低了生产成本，并将终端产量提升至每周约 200,000 台。我们计划继续大幅扩大生产规模，并取得提升利润率、降低客户门槛和拓宽可服务市场的进展。

paras.en: Scaling our AI Compute Rapidly and Efficiently. Our ability to rapidly and cost-effectively scale AI compute is a significant driver of our competitiveness. We view scaling of compute capacity through a simple lens: power availability and the powered shell together determine how quickly we can deploy compute, and our model and serving stack in that powered shell determines how efficiently we convert that compute into useful tokens. In order to scale our AI segment rapidly and efficiently, our strategy is extreme vertical integration, “from shovels to tokens.”
paras.zh: 快速高效地扩展我们的 AI 算力。我们快速且高性价比地扩展 AI 算力的能力，是我们竞争力的重要驱动因素。我们以简单的视角看待算力容量的扩展：电力可用性与通电外壳共同决定了我们部署算力的速度，而我们在该通电外壳中的模型与服务栈则决定了我们将该算力转化为有用 token 的效率。为了快速高效地扩展我们的 AI 业务板块，我们的战略是极致的垂直整合，即“从铲子到 token”。

paras.en: Power Availability and Powered Shells. We have demonstrated an industry-leading ability to rapidly deploy large-scale data center infrastructure at unprecedented speed and cost efficiency. Our COLOSSUS and COLOSSUS II data centers collectively provide approximately 1.0 gigawatt of compute power, with additional power capacity available for data center operations. We brought the first cluster of COLOSSUS online in 122 days, repurposing the shell of an existing factory, and the first cluster of COLOSSUS II online even faster in 91 days. As an illustrative comparison, an industry benchmark to bring online a 100 megawatt greenfield data center is approximately two years. We also demonstrated a significant improvement in cost efficiency, achieving data center construction costs for COLOSSUS II that are considerably lower than industry benchmarks on a per megawatt basis.
paras.zh: 电力可用性与通电外壳。我们已展现出行业领先的能力，能够以前所未有的速度和成本效率快速部署大规模数据中心基础设施。我们的 COLOSSUS 和 COLOSSUS II 数据中心合计提供约 1.0 吉瓦的算力功率，并另有可用电力容量用于数据中心运营。我们在 122 天内使 COLOSSUS 的第一个集群上线，复用了现有工厂的外壳；并使 COLOSSUS II 的第一个集群以更快的 91 天上线。作为说明性对比，使一个 100 兆瓦的新建数据中心上线的行业基准约为两年。我们还在成本效率方面展现出显著改善，COLOSSUS II 的数据中心建设成本按每兆瓦计算大幅低于行业基准。

paras.en: COLOSSUS and COLOSSUS II were brought online almost entirely through on-site power generation capabilities that we designed, built, and deployed ourselves. We view our proven ability to construct power infrastructure at this scale and speed as a significant competitive advantage. We partner closely with local utilities to fund grid infrastructure expansions and access excess capacity, while proactively curtailing our grid usage whenever required to prioritize community needs. Megapacks—utility-scale battery storage systems— deliver critical redundancy and help stabilize operations during peak demand. Going forward, COLOSSUS II is expected to be primarily powered by a dedicated natural gas power plant, supplemented over time by additional grid capacity that we are directly funding through our local utility partners. Our comprehensive expertise across the full infrastructure stack—from power procurement and on-site generation to distribution and advanced cooling systems—enables us to translate available power into usable compute capacity with exceptional efficiency. As we continue to scale and optimize, we expect to drive further improvements in Power Usage Effectiveness. We expect these gains to accelerate the path from buildout to monetization.
paras.zh: COLOSSUS 和 COLOSSUS II 几乎完全依靠我们自行设计、建造和部署的现场发电能力实现上线。我们认为，我们在大规模、高速度建设电力基础设施方面经实践验证的能力是一项显著的竞争优势。我们与当地公用事业公司紧密合作，为电网基础设施扩建提供资金并获取富余容量，同时在需要时主动削减我们的电网用电量，以优先满足社区需求。Megapack——公用事业级电池储能系统——提供关键的冗余保障，并有助于在用电高峰期间稳定运营。展望未来，COLOSSUS II 预计将主要由一座专用天然气发电厂供电，并随着时间推移，由我们通过当地公用事业合作伙伴直接出资建设的额外电网容量作为补充。我们在整个基础设施栈——从电力采购、现场发电到配电和先进冷却系统——的全面专业能力，使我们能够以卓越的效率将可用电力转化为可用的算力容量。随着我们持续扩大规模和优化，我们预计将推动电能利用效率（Power Usage Effectiveness）的进一步提升。我们预计这些改善将加快从建设到变现的进程。

paras.en: AI Token Generation Efficiency. We are highly vertically integrated. We design, own or lease, and install all of our powered shells and dedicated processor capacity. This full-stack ownership enables us to efficiently convert power capacity into usable compute, precisely control cluster configuration, and operate a true end-to-end system spanning infrastructure through to model deployment. Our operating performance depends on how effectively we utilize deployed compute once capacity comes online—specifically, our ability to convert raw infrastructure into reliable, high-throughput token generation at scale. Achieving this requires tight coordination across model training and inference workflows, hardware configuration, and data center operations so that utilization and throughput ramp efficiently as we expand. We believe we hold a meaningful efficiency advantage by tightly integrating the model layer directly with the compute layer. Unlike third-party environments that impose multiple abstraction layers, we run our serving stack close to the processors and optimize serving, networking, and cluster configuration as a single unified system. This “model-to-compute” integration reduces overhead, improves hardware utilization, and increases the proportion of available compute that is converted into delivered output tokens. Output tokens represent the final generated response delivered to the user, while total processing can be substantially higher when a request triggers additional inference-time reasoning steps. Because we control workload scheduling and serving logic, we can prioritize high token efficiency—intelligently balancing compute allocated to reasoning with strong final output to maintain or improve response quality. This end-to-end control, combined with our sourcing relationships with leading compute providers, gives us a performance-per-watt advantage and enables us to adopt new processor generations at scale more rapidly through a repeatable playbook for reconfiguration and recommissioning.
paras.zh: AI Token 生成效率。我们高度垂直整合。我们设计、拥有或租赁并安装所有带电力供应的机房外壳及专用处理器算力。这种全栈自有模式使我们能够高效地将电力容量转化为可用算力，精确控制集群配置，并运营一套从基础设施到模型部署的真正端到端系统。我们的经营表现取决于算力容量上线后我们对已部署算力的利用效率——具体而言，即我们将原始基础设施大规模转化为可靠、高吞吐量 token 生成的能力。实现这一目标需要在模型训练与推理工作流、硬件配置以及数据中心运营之间紧密协同，以便在我们扩张过程中高效提升利用率和吞吐量。我们相信，通过将模型层与算力层直接紧密整合，我们拥有显著的效率优势。与施加多层抽象层的第三方环境不同，我们的服务栈运行在贴近处理器的位置，并将服务、网络和集群配置作为单一统一系统进行优化。这种“模型到算力”的整合降低了开销，提高了硬件利用率，并提升了可用算力中转化为实际交付输出 token 的比例。输出 token 代表最终交付给用户的生成响应，而当一次请求触发额外的推理时推理步骤时，总处理量可能大幅更高。由于我们控制工作负载调度和服务逻辑，我们能够优先追求高 token 效率——智能地平衡分配给推理的算力与强劲的最终输出，以维持或提升响应质量。这种端到端控制，结合我们与领先算力供应商的采购关系，赋予我们每瓦性能优势，并使我们能够通过可复制的重新配置与重新投用操作手册，更快速、大规模地采用新一代处理器。

paras.en: **Orbital AI Compute Has the Potential to Massively Increase Our Ability to Scale Our AI Compute,**
paras.zh: **轨道 AI 算力有可能大幅提升我们扩展 AI 算力的能力，**

paras.en: Accelerate Our Pace, and to Be More Cost Effective Relative to Terrestrial Options. We believe we are the only company with a commercially viable path to building orbital AI compute at scale. This is underpinned by our unique ability to launch substantial mass into orbit cost efficiently through reusable rockets and manufacture secure, reliable, and high performance satellites at low cost and high volume. We plan to develop orbital data centers to enable scaling of compute capacity for us and our customers that is independent of terrestrial power infrastructure constraints. Space offers the potential to access virtually limitless power and an operating environment that supports sustained high‑density compute, including structural advantages for power generation, cooling, and uninterrupted operations as capacity grows. We plan to employ a modular shell approach built around our scalable satellite constellation, which enables compute capacity to be deployed and expanded efficiently as capacity requirements grow. The architecture also supports shorter refresh cycles at the token layer, as we can upgrade compute as successive chip generations arrive, increasing token output per unit of installed capacity. Our goal over time is to launch 100 gigawatts of compute to space each year. If operated continuously, the generation resources used to support 100 gigawatts of compute could generate approximately one-fifth of the annual power production in the United States, which was 4.4 thousand terawatt hours in 2025, according to the U.S. Energy Information Administration (EIA). We expect space‑based compute to massively increase AI compute scale, while also improving token economics.
paras.zh: 加快我们的步伐，并相对于地面方案更具成本效益。我们相信，我们是唯一一家拥有在规模化建设轨道 AI 算力方面具备商业可行路径的公司。这得益于我们独特的能力：通过可重复使用火箭以低成本将大量载荷送入轨道，并以低成本、高产量制造安全、可靠且高性能的卫星。我们计划开发轨道数据中心，使我们和我们的客户能够在不受地面电力基础设施制约的情况下扩展算力容量。太空有潜力提供几乎无限的电力以及支持持续高密度算力的运行环境，包括随着容量增长在发电、冷却和不间断运行方面的结构性优势。我们计划采用围绕可扩展卫星星座构建的模块化外壳方案，使算力容量能够随着容量需求的增长而高效部署和扩展。该架构还支持在 token 层面实现更短的更新周期，因为随着 successive 芯片世代的到来，我们可以升级算力，从而提高单位已装机容量对应的 token 产出。我们的长期目标是每年向太空发射 100 吉瓦的算力。据美国能源信息管理局（EIA）数据，若持续运行，用于支持 100 吉瓦算力的发电资源可产生约相当于美国年发电量的五分之一，美国 2025 年发电量为 4.4 千太瓦时。我们预计天基算力将大幅提升 AI 算力规模，同时改善 token 经济性。

paras.en: Ability to Increase Revenue from our Consumer User Base. Our performance depends in part on our ability to effectively increase revenue from our over 1.3 billion accounts active in the last twelve months ended March 2026, including approximately 550 million monthly active AI users across Grok and X through multiple complementary monetization channels:
paras.zh: 提升来自我们消费用户群的收入的能力。我们的业绩部分取决于我们能否通过多个互补的变现渠道，有效提升来自截至 2026 年 3 月的过去十二个月内活跃的超过 13 亿个账户的收入，其中包括 Grok 和 X 上约 5.5 亿月活跃 AI 用户：

paras.en: Growing our Advertising Platform. Advertising remains a core monetization channel for our AI segment, with revenue driven by our ability to deliver highly relevant ads. We aim to grow advertising revenue per user by strengthening performance advertising, expanding AI‑driven targeting and measurement, and introducing richer ad formats and creative tools. A central focus of ours is making ads feel like content—contextually relevant, aligned with user interests, and integrated into real‑time conversations. Grok increasingly supports this strategy by helping advertisers with campaign creation, creative optimization, and alignment with trending topics and user intent. While these factors help us drive advertising revenue, the pricing of our advertising products is also affected by other factors, including the global economy and the highly competitive nature of our industry. We believe continued investment in AI‑powered advertising will further improve advertiser ROI while further enhancing user experience.
paras.zh: 发展我们的广告平台。广告仍是我们 AI 板块的核心变现渠道，收入取决于我们投放高度相关广告的能力。我们旨在通过强化效果广告、扩展 AI 驱动的定向和衡量，以及引入更丰富的广告形式和创意工具，提升每用户广告收入。我们的一个核心重点是让广告感觉像内容——在语境上相关、与用户兴趣一致，并融入实时对话。Grok 日益支持这一战略，帮助广告主进行广告活动创建、创意优化，以及与热门话题和用户意图保持一致。尽管这些因素有助于我们推动广告收入，但我们广告产品的定价也受到其他因素的影响，包括全球经济和我们所处行业的高度竞争性。我们相信，持续投资于 AI 驱动的广告将进一步提升广告主 ROI，同时进一步改善用户体验。

paras.en: Conversion of Users to Paid Subscribers. In parallel, we are focused on converting a greater portion of our user base into paying subscribers through our X subscription (Premium and Premium+) and Grok subscription offerings. Subscribers benefit from enhanced functionality, exclusive features, and access to our latest AI models. As of December 31, 2025, we reached approximately 4.9 million active paid subscribers, which was comprised of approximately 4.1 million X Premium Basic, X Premium and Premium+ paid subscribers and approximately 0.9 million SuperGrok and SuperGrok Heavy paid subscribers. As of March 31, 2026, we reached approximately 6.3 million active paid subscribers, which was comprised of approximately 4.4 million X Premium Basic, X Premium and Premium+ paid subscribers and approximately 1.9 million SuperGrok, SuperGrok Heavy and SuperGrok Lite paid subscribers. We plan to continue adding new features and functionality while releasing increasingly capable Grok models to increase the penetration rate of our subscriber base. Our AI segment has demonstrated exceptional model velocity: since launching Grok, we have developed leading frontier models at a far faster rate of innovation than others. We believe this pace of innovation strengthens the value proposition of our subscription offerings and supports long‑term subscriber growth.
paras.zh: 用户转化为付费订阅用户。与此同时，我们专注于通过我们的 X 订阅（Premium 和 Premium+）以及 Grok 订阅产品，将更大比例的用户群体转化为付费订阅用户。订阅用户可受益于增强的功能、专属特性以及对我们最新 AI 模型的访问权限。截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，我们的活跃付费订阅用户达到约 4.9 百万，其中包括约 4.1 百万 X Premium Basic、X Premium 和 Premium+ 付费订阅用户，以及约 0.9 百万 SuperGrok 和 SuperGrok Heavy 付费订阅用户。截至 2026 年 3 月 31 日，我们的活跃付费订阅用户达到约 6.3 百万，其中包括约 4.4 百万 X Premium Basic、X Premium 和 Premium+ 付费订阅用户，以及约 1.9 百万 SuperGrok、SuperGrok Heavy 和 SuperGrok Lite 付费订阅用户。我们计划继续增加新特性和功能，同时发布能力日益增强的 Grok 模型，以提高我们订阅用户群的渗透率。我们的 AI 板块展现了卓越的模型迭代速度：自推出 Grok 以来，我们以远快于其他方的创新速度开发出了领先的前沿模型。我们相信，这一创新步伐增强了我们订阅产品的价值主张，并支撑长期订阅用户增长。

paras.en: Progress Toward the Everything App and New Monetization Channels. We aim to evolve X into an “Everything App,” integrating real-time information, communications, media, payments, banking, commerce and more within one consumer experience. This can increase the usefulness of X, and therefore increase the usage and monetization potential of X. We have rapid product launch velocity, with a frequent cadence of new features and products launched since 2023, including features such as long‑form video, improved group interactions, and creator tools. We plan to further broaden the value proposition of X through offerings like Money, a product we launched in beta in November 2025, which aims to expand platform utility by enabling payments and other financial services. We released X Chat in November 2025, which features end-to-end encryption and has no connection to advertising, unlike other services. We intend to further embed Grok throughout the platform to enhance discovery, analysis of posts, user support, and personalization, making core workflows more useful and reducing friction for users to adopt paid features.
paras.zh: 迈向万能应用及新变现渠道的进展。我们旨在将 X 演进为一款“万能应用”，将实时信息、通信、媒体、支付、银行、商务等整合于一体化的消费者体验之中。这可以提升 X 的实用性，从而提升 X 的使用量和变现潜力。我们拥有快速的产品发布速度，自 2023 年以来以频繁的节奏推出了新特性和产品，包括长视频、改进的群组互动以及创作者工具等特性。我们计划通过诸如 Money 等产品进一步拓宽 X 的价值主张，该产品于 2025 年 11 月推出测试版，旨在通过支持支付及其他金融服务来扩展平台效用。我们于 2025 年 11 月发布了 X Chat，其具备端到端加密功能，且与其他服务不同，与广告没有任何关联。我们打算进一步将 Grok 嵌入整个平台，以增强发现、帖子分析、用户支持和个性化，使核心工作流程更加有用，并降低用户采用付费功能的阻力。

paras.en: Growing Enterprise and Government Adoption of Our AI Offerings. Our future growth and financial performance depend in part on our ability to increase adoption and usage of our AI offerings among enterprise and government customers. We have launched Grok Business, Grok Enterprise, Grok API, and xAI Gov, products that we believe will be attractive to enterprises and governments, and we expect substantial opportunities to acquire new customers. We are also partnering with Cursor to advance Grok and potentially to create jointly-owned coding and knowledge work AI models, trained on our compute infrastructure. Over time, we also believe enterprises and governments will present significant opportunities for revenue expansion as they deploy our models more broadly across their organizations, adopt new capabilities, and build and operate solutions using our API. We also intend to continue to offer our compute infrastructure to third-party customers. Our ability to realize these expansion opportunities depends on continued innovation, reliable performance, and meeting evolving technical, security, and compliance requirements.
paras.zh: 企业及政府客户对我们 AI 产品的采用持续增长。我们未来的增长和财务表现部分取决于我们能否提高企业及政府客户对我们 AI 产品的采用率和使用量。我们已推出 Grok Business、Grok Enterprise、Grok API 和 xAI Gov，我们认为这些产品将对企业及政府客户具有吸引力，并预计将迎来获取新客户的重大机遇。我们还正与 Cursor 合作推进 Grok，并可能共同创建编码与知识工作 AI 模型，基于我们的算力基础设施进行训练。随着时间推移，我们还认为，随着企业及政府客户在其组织内更广泛地部署我们的模型、采用新能力，以及使用我们的 API 构建和运营解决方案，它们将带来显著的收入扩张机遇。我们还打算继续向第三方客户提供我们的算力基础设施。我们能否实现这些扩张机遇，取决于持续创新、可靠性能，以及满足不断演变的技术、安全和合规要求。

paras.en: #### Description of Our Segments
paras.zh: #### 我们的业务分部说明

paras.en: Revenue - Space
paras.zh: 收入 - 太空

paras.en: Space segment generates revenue primarily through (i) Launch Services for the deployment of payloads to their intended orbits for both commercial and government customers utilizing Falcon 9 and Falcon Heavy, and (ii) Launch and Development for the development of spacecraft and provision of launch and mission services for government agency space programs utilizing Falcon 9, Falcon Heavy, Starship, and Dragon. Launch Services revenue is derived from fixed-price contracts that range from one to five years. Launch and Development revenue is derived from fixed-price contracts that can range from one to fourteen years.
paras.zh: 太空板块主要通过以下方式产生收入：(i) 发射服务，即利用 Falcon 9 和 Falcon Heavy 为商业和政府客户将有效载荷部署至其预定轨道；(ii) 发射与开发，即利用 Falcon 9、Falcon Heavy、Starship 和 Dragon 为政府机构太空项目开发航天器并提供发射及任务服务。发射服务收入来自期限为一至五年的固定价格合同。发射与开发收入来自期限可为一至十四年的固定价格合同。

paras.en: The Company recognizes Launch Services revenue at a point in time, due to the interchangeability of flight hardware and minimal unique engineering costs. Revenue and costs are deferred and not recognized until upon the launch or deployment of the customer’s payload to their intended orbit.
paras.zh: 由于飞行硬件可互换且独特工程成本极低，公司在某一时点确认发射服务收入。收入和成本予以递延，直至客户有效载荷发射或部署至其预定轨道时才予以确认。

paras.en: The Company recognizes Launch and Development revenue over time as the Company’s performance on the contract creates an asset with no alternative use and the Company has an enforceable right to payment for performance to date. The Company measures progress on these contracts using the cost-to-cost input method, which the Company believes represents the most appropriate measure towards satisfaction of its performance obligation.
paras.zh: 由于公司在合同上的履约行为创造了无替代用途的资产，且公司对迄今已履约部分享有可强制执行的收款权利，公司在一段时间内确认发射与开发收入。公司采用成本比成本投入法计量这些合同的履约进度，公司认为该方法最能反映其履约义务的履行情况。

paras.en: For launches of our Starlink satellites, the Company does not recognize any inter-segment revenue, rather those launch costs are capitalized in satellites in Property, plant, and equipment, net. We allocate a significant amount of launch capacity to our Connectivity segment, and expect to allocate a significant amount to our AI segment in the future. Our Space segment revenue only reflects our customer launches and customer activities.
paras.zh: 对于我们的 Starlink 卫星发射，公司不确认任何分部间收入，相关发射成本资本化计入物业、厂房及设备净额中的卫星项下。我们将大量发射能力分配给我们的互联板块，并预计未来将向我们的 AI 板块分配大量发射能力。我们的太空板块收入仅反映客户发射和客户活动。

paras.en: Revenue from Launch Services recognized at point in time and revenue from Launch and Development recognized over time as a percentage of total Space segment revenue are as follows:
paras.zh: 按某一时点确认的发射服务收入与在一段时间内确认的发射与开发收入占太空板块总收入的比例列示如下：

paras.en: **Three Months Ended March 31,**
paras.zh: **截至 3 月 31 日的三个月，**

paras.en: We expect Space revenue growth to continue to be lower than total company revenue growth as our internal business continues to absorb most of the growth in our launch capacity. In addition, we expect Launch and Development to represent a larger portion of our Space revenue as we continue to serve our long-term contracts for our government customers. From period to period, Space revenue will vary based on the mix of launches used for customers and our own businesses.
paras.zh: 我们预计太空收入的增长将继续低于公司总收入的增长，因为我们的内部业务将继续吸收我们发射能力增长的大部分。此外，随着我们继续履行政府客户的长期合同，我们预计发射与开发将占我们太空收入的更大比例。在不同期间，太空收入将因用于客户和我们自身业务的发射组合不同而有所变化。

paras.en: Expenses - Space
paras.zh: 费用 - 太空

paras.en: Cost of Revenue
paras.zh: 收入成本

paras.en: The Company’s Falcon 9 and Falcon Heavy are composed of boosters (also known as first stages), second stages, Merlin engines, and fairings. Boosters, fairings, and Merlin engines are reusable and are classified as property, plant, and equipment and are depreciated to cost of revenue. The second stages are not reusable and are recorded to cost of revenue when they are launched for Launch Services revenue transactions or assigned for Launch and Development revenue transactions. Dragon is comprised of a fully reusable capsule that is classified asProperty, plant, and equipment, net and is depreciated to cost of revenue. Starship is comprised of a booster, ship, and Raptor engines and is currently in the development stage. A majority of Starship costs are currently expensed to Research and development as incurred. Raptor engines are expensed when used in test flights.
paras.zh: 公司的 Falcon 9 和 Falcon Heavy 由助推器（亦称一级）、二级、Merlin 发动机和整流罩组成。助推器、整流罩和 Merlin 发动机可重复使用，归类为不动产、厂房及设备，并折旧计入收入成本。二级不可重复使用，在用于发射服务收入交易而发射时，或用于发射与开发收入交易而分配时，计入收入成本。Dragon 由一个完全可重复使用的太空舱组成，归类为不动产、厂房及设备净额，并折旧计入收入成本。Starship 由助推器、飞船和 Raptor 发动机组成，目前处于开发阶段。Starship 的大部分成本目前在实际发生时计入研发费用。Raptor 发动机在用于试飞时计入费用。

paras.en: Space segment’s cost of revenue includes second stages flown related to the Company’s Falcon 9 and Falcon Heavy launches, launch operations and overhead, depreciation (inclusive of booster, Merlin engine, and fairing depreciation), employee compensation costs (including salaries, benefits, and share-based compensation) for our operations teams, launch testing and overhead, engineering costs, inventory excess and obsolescence, shared costs incurred in the production of launch hardware, and ongoing product support.
paras.zh: 太空板块的收入成本包括与公司 Falcon 9 和 Falcon Heavy 发射相关的已飞行二级、发射运营及间接费用、折旧（包括助推器、Merlin 发动机和整流罩折旧）、运营团队员工薪酬成本（包括工资、福利和股权激励费用）、发射测试及间接费用、工程成本、存货超额及陈旧、发射硬件生产过程中发生的共享成本，以及持续的产品支持。

paras.en: We expect Space cost of revenue to increase both in absolute dollars and as a percentage of revenue based on our expected mix of Launch Services and Launch and Development. From period to period, Space segment cost of revenue will vary based on the mix of customer and internal launches.
paras.zh: 我们预计，基于我们对发射服务与发射和开发的预期组合，太空板块收入成本在绝对美元金额和占收入百分比两方面均将增加。逐期而言，太空板块收入成本将因客户发射与内部发射的组合而变动。

paras.en: Research and Development
paras.zh: 研发

paras.en: Space segment’s research and development (“R&D”) expenses mainly relate to the development, build, and testing of Starship. Starship costs consist of test flight hardware, Raptor engines, employee compensation costs (including salaries, benefits, and share-based compensation), tooling and equipment expenses, depreciation for R&D equipment, and allocated overhead. R&D also includes certain expenses related to the development of features and modules created through engineering services for the Company’s Falcon vehicles, where the Company retains the associated intellectual property.
paras.zh: 太空板块的研发（“R&D”）费用主要与 Starship 的开发、建造和测试相关。Starship 成本包括试飞硬件、Raptor 发动机、员工薪酬成本（包括工资、福利和股权激励费用）、工装及设备费用、研发设备折旧以及分摊的间接费用。研发还包括与通过工程服务为公司 Falcon 运载工具开发的功能和模块相关的某些费用，公司保留相关知识产权。

paras.en: We expect Space research and development to increase both in absolute dollars and as a percentage of revenue in 2026, as we invest in the development and commercialization of Starship, and to moderate both in absolute dollars and as a percentage of revenue once Starship is commercialized by delivering payload to orbit. At commercialization, Starship costs generally will be capitalized and then depreciated in cost of revenue of the segment associated with the payload delivered.
paras.zh: 我们预计，随着我们投资于 Starship 的开发和商业化，2026 年太空板块研发在绝对美元金额和占收入百分比两方面均将增加；一旦 Starship 通过向轨道运送有效载荷实现商业化，其在绝对美元金额和占收入百分比两方面均将趋于平缓。商业化后，Starship 成本一般将予以资本化，随后在与所运送有效载荷相关的板块收入成本中折旧。

paras.en: Selling, General, and Administrative
paras.zh: 销售、一般及行政

paras.en: Space segment’s selling, general, and administrative (“SG&A”) expenses include allocated employee compensation costs (including salaries, benefits, and share-based compensation) for our sales, facilities, legal, finance, information technology, human resources, and other administrative employees, depreciation, and corporate aircraft costs.
paras.zh: 太空板块的销售、一般及行政（“SG&A”）费用包括分摊的销售、设施、法务、财务、信息技术、人力资源及其他行政员工的员工薪酬成本（包括工资、福利和股权激励费用）、折旧以及公司飞机成本。

paras.en: We expect Space segment's SG&A to increase in absolute dollars to support growth of our business, and to decrease as a percentage of revenue as we continue to work to reduce operating costs as a percentage of revenue.
paras.zh: 我们预计太空业务板块的销售、一般及行政费用（SG&A）绝对金额将增加，以支持我们业务的增长；同时，随着我们持续努力降低运营成本占收入的百分比，该费用占收入的百分比将下降。

paras.en: Impairment
paras.zh: 减值

paras.en: Space impairment includes impairment losses on fixed assets due to anomalies on the Company’s flight vehicles and launch sites, which occur outside our normal business operations.
paras.zh: 太空业务减值包括因公司飞行器和发射场出现异常而导致的固定资产减值损失，该等异常发生在我们的正常业务运营之外。

paras.en: Revenue - Connectivity
paras.zh: 收入 - 连接业务

paras.en: Connectivity segment generates revenue from (i) the broadband and mobile connectivity services provided through Starlink and (ii) the sale of the Starlink Kit (inclusive of the terminal). The Company provides connectivity services and Starlink Kits to consumers or enterprise and government customers.
paras.zh: 连接业务分部的收入来自(i)通过 Starlink 提供的宽带和移动连接服务，以及(ii)Starlink Kit（含终端）的销售。公司向消费者或企业与政府客户提供连接服务和 Starlink Kit。

paras.en: The Company recognizes revenue from broadband and mobile connectivity services over time as the customer simultaneously receives and consumes the benefits provided. The Company generates service revenue from (i) fixed-price services that require advance or recurring monthly payments by the customer or (ii) variable-priced services based on actual data consumption. The amounts received from customers for advanced payments for broadband and mobile connectivity services are recognized either ratably over the subscription term or based on actual data consumption. The Company’s broadband contracts are generally month-to-month and the revenue recognized for these recurring consumer customers is equal to the amount billed in that month. The Company’s mobile connectivity agreements are generally multi-year contractual obligations that range from one to five years, although the customer can generally terminate at any time.
paras.zh: 公司在客户同时获得并消耗所提供服务带来的利益的过程中，随时间确认宽带和移动连接服务的收入。公司的服务收入来自(i)要求客户预付或按月定期付款的固定价格服务，或(ii)基于实际数据使用量的可变价格服务。公司就宽带和移动连接服务向客户收取的预付款，在订阅期内按比例确认，或基于实际数据使用量确认。公司的宽带合同通常为按月合同，针对此类经常性消费者客户确认的收入等于该月开票金额。公司的移动连接协议通常为一年至五年的多年期合同义务，但客户通常可随时终止。

paras.en: The Company recognizes revenue over time for certain contracts related to our Starshield business that are multi-year in nature. For revenue that is recognized over time, we use the cost-to-cost input method. The Company records revenue based upon costs (such as materials and labor hours) incurred to date relative to the total estimated cost at completion.
paras.zh: 对于与 Starshield 业务相关的某些多年期合同，公司随时间确认收入。对于随时间确认的收入，公司采用成本比成本投入法。公司根据迄今发生的成本（如材料和人工工时）相对于完工时估计总成本的比例确认收入。

paras.en: The Company records revenue for the Starlink Kit upon delivery to the customer, or in the instance of certain enterprise customers, when it is installed. Starlink Kit revenue is reported net of sales returns, credits, and chargebacks.
paras.zh: 公司在 Starlink Kit 交付给客户时确认收入，对于某些企业客户，则在安装完成时确认。Starlink Kit 收入按扣除销售退货、折让和拒付后的净额列报。

paras.en: Expenses - Connectivity
paras.zh: 费用 - 连接业务

paras.en: Cost of Revenue
paras.zh: 收入成本

paras.en: Connectivity segment’s cost of revenue includes depreciation (inclusive of launch, satellite, and ground infrastructure costs), Starlink Kit costs, shipping and handling costs, ground operating expenses, employee compensation costs (including salaries, benefits, and share-based compensation) for our engineering and operations teams, payment processor fees, warranty expense, inventory excess and obsolescence, and customs and duties.
paras.zh: 连接业务分部的收入成本包括折旧（含发射、卫星和地面基础设施成本）、Starlink Kit 成本、运输及装卸成本、地面运营费用、工程与运营团队员工薪酬成本（包括工资、福利和股份支付薪酬）、支付处理费、保修费用、存货超额及陈旧、以及关税和税费。

paras.en: We expect Connectivity cost of revenue to increase in absolute dollars as we grow our revenue, and to decrease as a percentage of revenue as we continue to drive efficiencies in our next-generation satellites, Starlink Kits, and ground infrastructure.
paras.zh: 我们预计，随着收入增长，连接业务收入成本将以绝对美元计增加；随着我们持续提升下一代卫星、Starlink Kit 和地面基础设施的效率，其占收入的百分比将下降。

paras.en: Research and Development
paras.zh: 研发

paras.en: Connectivity segment’s R&D expenses mainly relate to the development, build, and testing of our next-generation satellites, Starlink Kits, and ground infrastructure. These costs include employee compensation costs (including salaries, benefits, and share-based compensation), contractor compensation expenses, equipment lease expenses, depreciation for R&D equipment, and allocated overhead.
paras.zh: 连接业务分部的研发费用主要与下一代卫星、Starlink Kit 和地面基础设施的开发、建造和测试相关。这些成本包括员工薪酬成本（包括工资、福利和股份支付薪酬）、承包商薪酬费用、设备租赁费用、研发设备折旧以及分摊的管理费用。

paras.en: We expect Connectivity research and development to increase in absolute dollars as we grow our revenue, and to decrease as a percentage of revenue as we scale our business.
paras.zh: 我们预计，随着收入增长，连接业务研发费用将以绝对美元计增加；随着业务规模扩大，其占收入的百分比将下降。

paras.en: Selling, General, and Administrative
paras.zh: 销售、一般及行政费用

paras.en: Connectivity segment’s SG&A expenses include allocated employee compensation costs (including salaries, benefits, and share-based compensation) for our sales, facilities, legal, finance, information technology, human resources, and other administrative employees, licensing and regulatory fees, marketing expenses, depreciation, and bad debt expense.
paras.zh: Connectivity 分部的销售、一般及行政费用包括分摊的销售、设施、法务、财务、信息技术、人力资源及其他行政员工的员工薪酬成本（含工资、福利及股份支付费用）、许可及监管费用、营销费用、折旧以及坏账费用。

paras.en: We expect Connectivity SG&A to increase in absolute dollars and as a percentage of revenue in 2026 as we introduce marketing spend to support growth of our business, and to decrease as a percentage of revenue over time as we continue to work to reduce operating costs as a percentage of revenue.
paras.zh: 我们预计，2026 年 Connectivity 的销售、一般及行政费用在绝对金额和占收入的比例上均将上升，原因是我们将投入营销支出以支持业务增长；随着我们持续努力降低运营成本占收入的比例，该费用占收入的比例预计将随时间推移而下降。

paras.en: Impairment
paras.zh: 减值

paras.en: Connectivity impairment includes costs related to discontinuation of a product line for Starlink Kits that is non-recurring.
paras.zh: Connectivity 减值包括与停止 Starlink Kits 某产品线相关的成本，该成本为非经常性项目。

paras.en: Revenue - AI
paras.zh: 收入 - AI

paras.en: AI segment generates revenue from (i) the sale of ad products displayed on its X platform, and (ii) providing AI solutions and infrastructure, which includes subscription-related offerings, data licensing arrangements, and API access to Grok models. Both services are offered to consumer and enterprise customers.
paras.zh: AI 分部通过以下方式产生收入：(i) 在其 X 平台上销售所展示的广告产品，以及 (ii) 提供 AI 解决方案和基础设施，包括订阅相关产品、数据许可安排以及 Grok 模型的 API 访问。这两类服务均面向消费者和企业客户提供。

paras.en: Revenue for advertising services is recognized in the period when advertising is delivered as evidenced by a person engaging with an ad on the Company’s platforms in a manner satisfying the types of engagement selected by the advertisers. The Company’s contract terms for advertising services are typically cancellable short-term arrangements. We experience seasonality in our advertising revenues. Overall advertising spend tends to be highest in the fourth quarter of each year due in large part to end-of-year advertiser spending and lowest in the first quarter of each year.
paras.zh: 广告服务收入在广告投放期间确认，其依据是个人以符合广告主所选互动类型的方式与公司平台上的广告进行互动。公司广告服务的合同条款通常为可取消的短期安排。我们的广告收入存在季节性。整体广告支出通常在每年第四季度最高，这在很大程度上归因于广告主的年末支出，并在每年第一季度最低。

paras.en: Revenue for AI solutions and infrastructure includes: (i) premium subscriptions on X and Grok which is recognized ratably over the period of the subscription term (ranging from month-to-month to one year), (ii) data licensing revenue which is generally recognized ratably over the period (from month-to-month to two years) in which the Company provides data as the customer consumes and benefits from the use of the licensed data, and (iii) revenue from providing API access to Grok models recognized ratably over the contract term (typically month-to-month or up to one year) for stand-ready access or as services are consumed for usage based arrangements.
paras.zh: AI 解决方案和基础设施收入包括：(i) X 和 Grok 上的高级订阅，在订阅期内（从按月到一年不等）按比例确认；(ii) 数据许可收入，通常在公司提供数据、客户消耗并受益于所许可数据的使用期间（从按月到两年不等）按比例确认；以及 (iii) 提供 Grok 模型 API 访问的收入，对于随时可用访问，在合同期内（通常为按月或最长一年）按比例确认，对于基于用量的安排，则在服务被消耗时确认。

paras.en: Expenses - AI
paras.zh: 费用 - AI

paras.en: Cost of Revenue
paras.zh: 收入成本

paras.en: AI segment’s cost of revenue includes infrastructure costs, revenue share expenses, payment processor fees, payments to creators, amortization of acquired intangible assets, and allocated labor and overhead costs. Infrastructure costs consist primarily of costs related to data center facilities, including lease and hosting costs, related support, maintenance, energy, and bandwidth costs, depreciation of servers and networking equipment, public cloud hosting costs, and employee compensation costs (including salaries, benefits, and share-based compensation) for our operations teams.
paras.zh: AI 分部的收入成本包括基础设施成本、收入分成费用、支付处理商费用、向创作者支付的款项、收购的无形资产摊销以及分摊的劳动力和间接费用。基础设施成本主要包括与数据中心设施相关的成本，包括租赁和托管成本、相关支持、维护、能源和带宽成本、服务器和网络设备的折旧、公有云托管成本，以及我们运营团队的人员薪酬成本（包括工资、福利和股份支付薪酬）。

paras.en: We expect AI cost of revenue to increase in absolute dollars as we grow our revenue, and to decrease as a percentage of revenue as we monetize our products and as we expand our service offerings for AI solutions.
paras.zh: 我们预计，随着收入增长，AI 收入成本以绝对美元计将增加，而随着我们将产品变现以及扩展 AI 解决方案的服务产品，其占收入的百分比将下降。

paras.en: Research and Development
paras.zh: 研究与开发

paras.en: AI segment’s R&D expenses mainly relate to the training of Grok, our leading frontier model, development, build, and testing of our next-generation AI-enabled products and data center costs to train AI-enabled products. These costs include cloud computing expenses, employee compensation expenses (including salaries, benefits, and share-based compensation), power generation costs, and depreciation of data center assets, including processors, equipment lease expenses, and networking equipment.
paras.zh: AI 分部的研发费用主要涉及我们领先的前沿模型 Grok 的训练、下一代 AI 赋能产品的开发、构建和测试，以及用于训练 AI 赋能产品的数据中心成本。这些成本包括云计算费用、人员薪酬费用（包括工资、福利和股份支付薪酬）、发电成本以及数据中心资产折旧，包括处理器、设备租赁费用和网络设备。

paras.en: We expect AI R&D expenses to increase, both in absolute dollars and as a percentage of revenue, as we invest in compute infrastructure for Grok. Additionally, AI R&D expenses may increase as a result of the compute agreement with Cursor.
paras.zh: 我们预计，随着我们投资于 Grok 的算力基础设施，AI 研发费用以绝对美元计及占收入的百分比均将增加。此外，AI 研发费用可能因与 Cursor 的算力协议而增加。

paras.en: Selling, General, and Administrative
paras.zh: 销售、一般及行政

paras.en: AI segment’s SG&A expenses consist primarily of employee compensation expenses (including salaries, benefits, and share-based compensation) for our sales, sales support, marketing, finance, legal, information technology, human resources and other administrative employees. In addition, SG&A expenses include fees and costs for professional services, including consulting, content moderation, third-party legal and accounting services and facilities costs and other supporting overhead costs that are not allocated to other departments.
paras.zh: AI 分部的销售、一般及管理费用主要由我们销售、销售支持、市场营销、财务、法务、信息技术、人力资源及其他行政员工的员工薪酬费用（包括工资、福利和股份支付薪酬）构成。此外，销售、一般及管理费用还包括专业服务费用和成本，包括咨询、内容审核、第三方法律和会计服务，以及设施成本和其他未分配至其他部门的相关间接费用。

paras.en: We expect AI SG&A to increase in absolute dollars to support growth of our business, and to decrease as a percentage of revenue as we continue to work to reduce operating costs as a percentage of revenue. Additionally, AI SG&A may increase as a result of the compute agreement with Cursor.
paras.zh: 我们预计 AI 销售、一般及管理费用按绝对金额计算将增加，以支持我们业务的增长；同时，随着我们持续努力降低运营成本占收入的百分比，该费用占收入的百分比将下降。此外，由于与 Cursor 签订的算力协议，AI 销售、一般及管理费用可能增加。

paras.en: Restructuring Charges
paras.zh: 重组费用

paras.en: AI restructuring charges are the result of the acquisition of Twitter in October 2022 by X Holdings. The charges include workforce restructuring for former Twitter employees, as well as impairment and early termination penalties as a result of consolidation of Twitter’s various office leases.
paras.zh: AI 重组费用源于 X Holdings 于 2022 年 10 月收购 Twitter。该费用包括前 Twitter 员工的劳动力重组，以及因整合 Twitter 多项办公租赁而产生的减值及提前终止罚金。

paras.en: Impairment
paras.zh: 减值

paras.en: AI impairment includes a one-time impairment of the Twitter brand when Twitter was rebranded to X in July 2023.
paras.zh: AI 减值包括 2023 年 7 月 Twitter 品牌更名为 X 时对 Twitter 品牌进行的一次性减值。

paras.en: Other Corporate Expenses
paras.zh: 其他公司费用

paras.en: Interest Expense
paras.zh: 利息费用

paras.en: Interest expense includes interest expense related to our borrowings, amortization of associated debt issuance costs, undrawn fees, and finance leases. Interest expense is reflected net of capitalized interest.
paras.zh: 利息费用包括与我们借款相关的利息费用、相关债务发行成本的摊销、未提取费用以及融资租赁。利息费用以扣除资本化利息后的净额列示。

paras.en: Interest Income
paras.zh: 利息收入

paras.en: Interest income includes interest income earned on cash and cash equivalents and marketable securities, and dividend income from our investments in mutual funds.
paras.zh: 利息收入包括现金及现金等价物和有价证券所赚取的利息收入，以及我们共同基金投资产生的股息收入。

paras.en: Other Income (Expense), Net
paras.zh: 其他收入（费用）净额

paras.en: Other income (expense), net consists of gain or loss on digital assets, gain or loss on foreign currency transactions, and loss on extinguishment of debt.
paras.zh: 其他收入（费用）净额由数字资产收益或亏损、外币交易收益或亏损以及债务清偿损失构成。

paras.en: Provision for (Benefit from) Income Taxes
paras.zh: 所得税费用（收益）

paras.en: The provision for (benefit from) income taxes consists primarily of income taxes in certain federal, state, local and foreign jurisdictions in which we conduct business. Foreign jurisdictions typically have different statutory tax rates from those in the United States. Accordingly, our effective tax rates may vary depending on the impact of the valuation allowance as well as the relative proportion of foreign income to domestic income, generation of tax credits, changes in the valuation of our deferred tax assets and liabilities, and changes in tax laws.
paras.zh: 所得税费用（收益）主要由我们在开展业务的某些联邦、州、地方及外国司法管辖区缴纳的所得税构成。外国司法管辖区的法定税率通常与美国不同。因此，我们的实际税率可能因估值备抵的影响以及境外收入与境内收入的相对比例、税收抵免的产生、递延所得税资产和负债估值的变化以及税法的变化而有所不同。

paras.en: #### Comparison of the three months ended March 31, 2026 and 2025
paras.zh: #### 2026 年与 2025 年截至 3 月 31 日止三个月的比较

paras.en: Consolidated Results of Operations
paras.zh: 合并经营业绩

paras.en: The following table sets forth our consolidated financial statements data for the periods indicated:
paras.zh: 下表列示了所示期间的合并财务报表数据：

paras.zh: **截至 3 月 31 日止三个月，**

paras.en: Revenue
paras.zh: 收入

paras.en: Revenue for the three months endedMarch 31, 2026 increased by $627 million, or 15.4%, compared to thethree months endedMarch 31, 2025. This increase was primarily due to an increase in revenue from our Connectivity segment of $782 million as our Starlink Subscriber base continued to grow as well as an increase in revenue from our AI segment of $91 million from higher X and Grok subscriptions, partially offset by a decrease in revenue from our Space segment of $246 million due to lower Launch Services missions and timing of work for government contracts.
paras.zh: 截至 2026 年 3 月 31 日止三个月的收入较截至 2025 年 3 月 31 日止三个月增加$627 million，增幅 15.4%。该增加主要由于随着我们的 Starlink 订户基础持续增长，我们的连接业务分部收入增加$782 million，以及由于 X 和 Grok 订阅量增加，我们的 AI 业务分部收入增加$91 million，部分被我们的太空业务分部收入减少$246 million 所抵消，后者是由于发射服务任务减少以及政府合同工作的时间安排所致。

paras.en: Cost of Revenue
paras.zh: 收入成本

paras.en: Cost of revenue for the three months endedMarch 31, 2026 increased by $426 million, or 21.7%, compared to the prior three months endedMarch 31, 2025. This increase was primarily due to an increase in costs in our Connectivity segment of $437 million driven by an increase in depreciation related to the number of satellites placed into orbit and higher operating costs of $5 million in our AI segment, partially offset by a decrease in cost of revenue from our Space segment of $16 million due to less customer launches.
paras.zh: 截至 2026 年 3 月 31 日止三个月的收入成本较上一期间（截至 2025 年 3 月 31 日止三个月）增加 $426 million，增幅 21.7%。该增加主要由于我们互联业务板块的成本增加 $437 million，其驱动因素是入轨卫星数量增加导致的折旧增加；以及我们 AI 业务板块运营成本增加 $5 million；部分被我们太空业务板块因客户发射次数减少而带来的收入成本减少 $16 million 所抵消。

paras.en: Research and Development
paras.zh: 研发费用

paras.en: Research and development expense for the three months endedMarch 31, 2026 increased by $1,957 million, or 125.7%, compared to the prior three months endedMarch 31, 2025. This increase was primarily due to higher costs in our AI segment of $1,471 million driven by depreciation of GPU hardware, and the cost of cloud computing and data center infrastructure expenses as a result of our AI data center expansions and higher costs from our Space segment of $404 million driven by accelerated investment in our Starship vehicle and related facilities.
paras.zh: 截至 2026 年 3 月 31 日止三个月的研发费用较上一期间（截至 2025 年 3 月 31 日止三个月）增加 $1,957 million，增幅 125.7%。该增加主要由于我们 AI 业务板块成本增加 $1,471 million，其驱动因素是 GPU 硬件折旧，以及因 AI 数据中心扩建而产生的云计算和数据中心基础设施费用；以及我们太空业务板块成本增加 $404 million，其驱动因素是对 Starship 运载工具及相关设施的加速投资。

paras.en: Selling, General, and Administrative
paras.zh: 销售、一般及管理费用

paras.en: Selling, general, and administrative expense for the three months endedMarch 31, 2026 increased by $253 million, or 51.3%, compared to the prior three months endedMarch 31, 2025. This increase was primarily due to higher employee-related costs and professional fees for our AI segment of $163 million as our AI business grew rapidly, higher marketing and international expansion costs of $79 million and $23 million, respectively, for our Connectivity segment. These increases were partially offset by lower expenses of $18 million in our Space segment.
paras.zh: 截至 2026 年 3 月 31 日止三个月的销售、一般及管理费用较上一期间（截至 2025 年 3 月 31 日止三个月）增加 $253 million，增幅 51.3%。该增加主要由于随着我们 AI 业务快速增长，AI 业务板块的员工相关成本及专业服务费增加 $163 million；以及我们互联业务板块的营销成本和国际扩张成本分别增加 $79 million 和 $23 million。上述增加部分被我们太空业务板块费用减少 $18 million 所抵消。

paras.en: Restructuring Charges (Credits)
paras.zh: 重组费用（收益）

paras.en: Restructuring charges (credits) for the three months endedMarch 31, 2026 decreased by $15 million compared to the prior three months endedMarch 31, 2025. This decrease was primarily due to change in estimated settlement amounts for former Twitter employees as part of the workforce reduction program implemented in 2022.
paras.zh: 截至 2026 年 3 月 31 日止三个月的重组费用（收益）较上一期间（截至 2025 年 3 月 31 日止三个月）减少 $15 million。该减少主要由于 2022 年实施的裁员计划中前 Twitter 员工预计和解金额的估计发生变化。

paras.en: Impairment
paras.zh: 减值

paras.en: Impairment for the three months endedMarch 31, 2026 decreased by $24 million compared to the prior three months endedMarch 31, 2025. The impairment in the three months endedMarch 31, 2025 was related to a post-landing anomaly in our Space segment. There was no impairment for the three months ended March 31, 2026.
paras.zh: 截至 2026 年 3 月 31 日止三个月的减值较上一期间（截至 2025 年 3 月 31 日止三个月）减少 $24 million。截至 2025 年 3 月 31 日止三个月的减值与我们太空业务板块的一次着陆后异常有关。截至 2026 年 3 月 31 日止三个月未发生减值。

paras.en: Income (Loss) from Operations
paras.zh: 经营利润（亏损）

paras.en: Income (loss) from operations for the three months endedMarch 31, 2026 decreased by $1,970 million compared to the prior three months endedMarch 31, 2025 driven by the factors described above.
paras.zh: 截至 2026 年 3 月 31 日止三个月的经营利润（亏损）较上一期间（截至 2025 年 3 月 31 日止三个月）减少 $1,970 million，其驱动因素为上述各项因素。

paras.en: Interest Expense
paras.zh: 利息费用

paras.en: Interest expense for the three months endedMarch 31, 2026 increased by $217 million, or 48.5%, compared to the prior three months endedMarch 31, 2025. This increase was primarily due to additional debt raised by the Company and other financing arrangements entered into during the period by our AI segment.

paras.en: Cost of revenue for the year ended December 31, 2025 increased by $1,455 million, or 18.2%, compared to the prior year ended December 31, 2024. This increase was primarily due to an increase in costs in our Connectivity segment of $1,153 million driven by higher depreciation as the number of satellites placed into orbit grew and higher operating expenses, and higher infrastructure and cloud computing costs of $491 million in our AI segment, partially offset by a decrease in cost of revenue from our Space segment of $189 million due to the increased reusability of our Falcon launch vehicles resulting in lower depreciation.
paras.zh: 截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日止年度的收入成本较上一截至 2024 年 12 月 31 日止年度增加$1,455 百万，增幅 18.2%。该增加主要由于随着入轨卫星数量增长带来的折旧增加及运营费用上升，我们连接业务的成本增加$1,153 百万，以及我们 AI 业务的基础设施和云计算成本增加$491 百万，部分被我们太空业务收入成本的减少$189 百万所抵消，该减少是由于我们的 Falcon 运载火箭可重复使用性提高导致折旧降低。

paras.en: Research and Development
paras.zh: 研发

paras.en: Research and development expense for the year ended December 31, 2025 increased by $5,179 million, or 149.5%, compared to the prior year ended December 31, 2024. This increase was primarily due to higher R&D costs in our AI segment of $3,888 million driven by the depreciation of GPU hardware and the cost of cloud computing as a result of our AI data center expansions and higher R&D costs from our Space segment of $1,169 million driven by accelerated investment in our Starship vehicle.
paras.zh: 截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日止年度的研发费用较上一截至 2024 年 12 月 31 日止年度增加$5,179 百万，增幅 149.5%。该增加主要由于我们 AI 业务的研发成本增加$3,888 百万，其驱动因素为 GPU 硬件折旧以及因 AI 数据中心扩建而产生的云计算成本，以及我们太空业务的研发成本增加$1,169 百万，其驱动因素为对 Starship 飞行器的加速投资。

paras.en: Selling, General, and Administrative
paras.zh: 销售、一般及行政

paras.en: Selling, general, and administrative expense for the year ended December 31, 2025 increased by $831 million, or 45.8%, compared to the prior year ended December 31, 2024. This increase was primarily due to higher employee and facilities-related costs and higher legal expenses for our AI segment of $722 million as our AI business grew rapidly, and higher marketing and international expansion costs of $40 million and $37 million, respectively, for our Connectivity segment. These increases were partially offset by lower allocated general and administrative overhead in our Space segment.
paras.zh: 截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日止年度的销售、一般及管理费用较上一截至 2024 年 12 月 31 日止年度增加 $831 million，增幅 45.8%。该增加主要由于随着我们 AI 业务的快速增长，员工及设施相关成本上升，以及我们 AI 分部法律费用增加 $722 million，同时我们 Connectivity 分部的营销及国际扩张成本分别增加 $40 million 和 $37 million。上述增加部分被我们 Space 分部分摊的一般及行政管理间接费用下降所抵消。

paras.en: Restructuring Charges
paras.zh: 重组费用

paras.en: Restructuring charges for the year ended December 31, 2025 increased by $274 million, or 128.6%, compared to the prior year ended December 31, 2024. This increase was primarily due to additional expense related to the settlement to former Twitter employees as part of the workforce reduction program implemented in 2022.
paras.zh: 截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日止年度的重组费用较上一截至 2024 年 12 月 31 日止年度增加 $274 million，增幅 128.6%。该增加主要由于与 2022 年实施的裁员计划相关的、就向前 Twitter 员工支付和解款项而产生的额外费用。

paras.en: Impairment
paras.zh: 减值

paras.en: Impairment for the year ended December 31, 2025 decreased by $25 million, or 39.7%, compared to the prior year ended December 31, 2024. The decrease was primarily related to a discontinuation of a Starlink Kit production line in our Connectivity segment that occurred during the year ended December 31, 2024 with no impairment in 2025, partially offset by an increase in impairment in our Space Segment during the year ended December 31, 2025 primarily related to a post-landing anomaly.
paras.zh: 截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日止年度的减值较上一截至 2024 年 12 月 31 日止年度减少 $25 million，降幅 39.7%。该减少主要与我们 Connectivity 分部于截至 2024 年 12 月 31 日止年度停产一条 Starlink Kit 生产线有关，2025 年未发生减值，部分被我们 Space 分部于截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日止年度主要因一次着陆后异常而增加的减值所抵消。

paras.en: Income (Loss) from Operations
