paras.en: Income (loss) from operations for the year ended December 31, 2025 decreased by $3,055 million compared to the prior year ended December 31, 2024 driven by the factors described above.
paras.zh: 截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日止年度的经营利润（亏损）较上一截至 2024 年 12 月 31 日止年度减少 $3,055 million，主要受上述因素驱动。

paras.en: Interest Expense
paras.zh: 利息费用

paras.en: Interest expense for the year ended December 31, 2025 increased by $365 million, or 23.1%, compared to the prior year ended December 31, 2024. This increase was primarily due to new term loans and senior notes entered into by the Company and other financing arrangements for GPUs entered into during the year by our AI segment.
paras.zh: 截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日止年度的利息费用较上一截至 2024 年 12 月 31 日止年度增加 $365 million，增幅 23.1%。该增加主要由于本公司新订立的定期贷款和优先票据，以及我们 AI 分部于本年度内就 GPU 订立的其他融资安排。

paras.en: Interest Income
paras.zh: 利息收入

paras.en: Interest income for the year ended December 31, 2025 increased by $121 million, or 32.6%, compared to the prior year ended December 31, 2024. This increase was primarily due to an increase in dividend income earned from marketable securities and cash equivalents.
paras.zh: 截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日止年度的利息收入较上一截至 2024 年 12 月 31 日止年度增加 $121 million，增幅 32.6%。该增加主要由于从有价证券及现金等价物赚取的股息收入增加。

paras.en: Other Income (Expense), Net
paras.zh: 其他收入（费用），净额

paras.en: Other income (expense), net for the year ended December 31, 2025 decreased by $1,162 million, compared to the prior year ended December 31, 2024. This decrease was primarily due to an unrealized loss on digital assets.
paras.zh: 截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日止年度的其他收入（费用）净额较上一截至 2024 年 12 月 31 日止年度减少 $1,162 百万。该减少主要由于数字资产的未实现亏损。

paras.en: Provision for (Benefit from) Income Taxes
paras.zh: 所得税费用（收益）

paras.en: Provision for income taxes for the year ended December 31, 2025 increased by $1,267 million compared to the prior year ended December 31, 2024. The increase was primarily due to a partial valuation allowance release in 2024 and the establishment of a valuation allowance in 2025. For the year ended December 31, 2024, the Company released a partial valuation allowance on the Company’s U.S. deferred tax assets. As of December 31, 2024, the Company forecasted $659 million of deferred tax assets related to U.S. R&D credits would be utilized in the future. For the year ended December 31, 2025, we assessed the realizability of our deferred tax assets and reversed the benefit that was recognized for the year ended December 31, 2024 based on cumulative pretax losses adjusted for permanent differences and other negative evidence.
paras.zh: 截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日止年度的所得税费用较上一截至 2024 年 12 月 31 日止年度增加 $1,267 百万。该增加主要由于 2024 年部分估值备抵的释放以及 2025 年估值备抵的计提。截至 2024 年 12 月 31 日止年度，公司释放了公司美国递延税项资产的部分估值备抵。截至 2024 年 12 月 31 日，公司预计与研发税收抵免相关的 $659 百万递延税项资产将在未来被使用。截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日止年度，我们评估了递延税项资产的可实现性，并基于经永久性差异调整后的累计税前亏损及其他负面证据，冲回了截至 2024 年 12 月 31 日止年度确认的收益。

paras.zh: 净利润（亏损）

paras.en: Net income (loss) for the year ended December 31, 2025 decreased by $5,728 million compared to the prior year ended December 31, 2024 driven by the factors described above.
paras.zh: 截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日止年度的净利润（亏损）较上一截至 2024 年 12 月 31 日止年度减少 $5,728 百万，主要受上述因素驱动。

paras.en: Revenue
paras.zh: 收入

paras.en: Revenue for the year ended December 31, 2025 increased by $290 million,or 7.6%, compared to the prior year ended December 31, 2024. Launch Services revenue remained relatively flat year over year, while Launch and Development revenue increased by $298 million. The Launch and Development revenue increase was primarily driven by increased revenue for an extended contract with NASA for additional Cargo Resupply Services (CRS) missions to the International Space Station and increased revenue from a U.S. Department of War contract. While total Falcon launches increased by 31 from 134 in 2024 to 165 in 2025, Space customer launches and average price per launch remained relatively flat year over year.
paras.zh: 截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日止年度的收入较上一截至 2024 年 12 月 31 日止年度增加 $290 million，即 7.6%。发射服务收入同比基本持平，而发射与开发收入增加 $298 million。发射与开发收入的增长主要得益于与 NASA 就国际空间站额外货运补给服务（CRS）任务签订的扩展合同收入增加，以及来自美国战争部一份合同的收入增加。尽管 Falcon 总发射次数从 2024 年的 134 次增加 31 次至 2025 年的 165 次，但太空客户发射次数及每次发射平均价格同比基本持平。

paras.en: Cost of Revenue
paras.zh: 收入成本

paras.en: Cost of revenue for the year ended December 31, 2025 decreased by $189 million,or 12.2%, compared to the prior year ended December 31, 2024. This decrease was primarily due increased reusability of our Falcon launch vehicles resulting in lower deprecation of $240 million, lowering the cost of each launch, and lower overhead costs of $11 million. The decrease is also due to the relative increase in Starlink satellite launches from 89 launches in 2024 to 122 launches in 2025, resulting in relatively more of our launch operations and overhead costs capitalized in our Connectivity segment of $14 million. This decrease was partially offset by an increase in inventory excess and obsolescence reserves of $51 million mainly due to less demand on rocket vehicle and spacecraft parts as reusability has increased.
paras.zh: 截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日止年度的收入成本较上一截至 2024 年 12 月 31 日止年度减少 $189 million，即 12.2%。该减少主要由于我们 Falcon 运载火箭可重复使用性提高，使折旧减少 $240 million，降低了每次发射的成本，以及间接费用减少 $11 million。该减少还由于 Starlink 卫星发射次数相对增加，从 2024 年的 89 次增至 2025 年的 122 次，使相对更多的发射运营及间接费用资本化计入我们的互联业务分部，金额为 $14 million。该减少被存货超额及陈旧储备增加 $51 million 部分抵消，主要由于可重复使用性提高导致对火箭运载器及航天器部件的需求减少。

paras.en: Research and Development
paras.zh: 研发

paras.en: Research and development for the year ended December 31, 2025 increased by $1,169 million,or 63.7%, compared to the prior year ended December 31, 2024. This increase was primarily driven by higher production costs of $779 million, higher launch costs of $218 million, and higher engineering costs of $185 million, due to the accelerated investment in development of the Starship vehicle and continued development of production and launch facilities to support future Starship launches.
paras.zh: 截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日止年度的研发费用较上一截至 2024 年 12 月 31 日止年度增加 $1,169 million，即 63.7%。该增加主要由于生产成本增加 $779 million、发射成本增加 $218 million 及工程成本增加 $185 million，原因是加速投资于 Starship 运载器的开发，以及持续开发生产和发射设施以支持未来的 Starship 发射。

paras.en: Selling, general, and administrative for the year ended December 31, 2025 decreased by $26 million,or 6.9%, compared to the prior year ended December 31, 2024. This decrease was primarily due to lower allocated general and administrative overhead of $52 million, partially offset by higher employee compensation expenses (including salaries, benefits, and share-based compensation) of $16 million.
paras.zh: 截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日止年度的销售、一般及行政费用较上一截至 2024 年 12 月 31 日止年度减少 $26 million，即 6.9%。该减少主要由于分摊的一般及行政间接费用减少 $52 million，被员工薪酬费用（包括工资、福利及股份支付薪酬）增加 $16 million 部分抵消。

paras.zh: 截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日止年度的减值较上一截至 2024 年 12 月 31 日止年度增加 $14 million，即 61.5%。该增加主要由于年内一枚 Falcon 9 助推器因着陆后异常而产生的一次性减值损失。

paras.en: Cost of Revenue
paras.zh: 收入成本

paras.en: Cost of revenue for the year ended December 31, 2025 increased by $491 million,or 29.1%, compared to the prior year ended December 31, 2024. This increase was primarily due to higher infrastructure and cloud computing costs of $412 million attributable to increased subscriber revenue, higher employee compensation expenses (including salaries, benefits, and share-based compensation) of $90 million, higher revenue share and content creator fees of $45 million, and higher payment processor fees of $28 million, partially offset by a decrease in depreciation and amortization expense of $97 million driven by a decrease in amortization expense for intangible assets that were fully amortized during 2025.
paras.zh: 截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日止年度的收入成本较上一截至 2024 年 12 月 31 日止年度增加 $491 million，即 29.1%。该增加主要归因于：因订阅收入增长而增加的基础设施及云计算成本 $412 million、员工薪酬费用（包括工资、福利及股权激励费用）增加 $90 million、收入分成及内容创作者费用增加 $45 million，以及支付处理费增加 $28 million，部分被折旧及摊销费用减少 $97 million 所抵销，该减少系因于 2025 年已全部摊销完毕的无形资产摊销费用减少所致。

paras.en: Research and Development
paras.zh: 研发费用

paras.en: Research and development for the year ended December 31, 2025 increased by $3,888 million,or 330.8%, compared to the prior year ended December 31, 2024. This increase was primarily due to higher GPU depreciation expense of $1,673 million, higher infrastructure and cloud computing expenses of $1,440 million associated with the build out of our compute infrastructure, and higher employee compensation expenses (including salaries, benefits, and share-based compensation) and allocated overhead costs of $775 million.
paras.zh: 截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日止年度的研发费用较上一截至 2024 年 12 月 31 日止年度增加 $3,888 million，即 330.8%。该增加主要归因于：GPU 折旧费用增加 $1,673 million、与算力基础设施建设相关的基础设施及云计算费用增加 $1,440 million，以及员工薪酬费用（包括工资、福利及股权激励费用）及分摊间接费用增加 $775 million。

paras.en: Selling, General, and Administrative
paras.zh: 销售、一般及行政费用

paras.en: Selling, general, and administrative for the year ended December 31, 2025 increased by $722 million,or 65.4%, compared to the prior year ended December 31, 2024. This increase was primarily due to higher employee compensation expenses (including salaries, benefits, and share-based compensation) of $519 million as we continue to expand our AI business, higher legal expenses of $189 million, and higher facilities and general and administrative costs of $14 million.
paras.zh: 截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日止年度的销售、一般及行政费用较上一截至 2024 年 12 月 31 日止年度增加 $722 million，即 65.4%。该增加主要归因于：随着我们持续扩展 AI 业务，员工薪酬费用（包括工资、福利及股权激励费用）增加 $519 million、法律费用增加 $189 million，以及设施及一般和行政成本增加 $14 million。

paras.en: Restructuring Charges
paras.zh: 重组费用

paras.en: Restructuring charges for the year ended December 31, 2025 increased by $274 million or 129.1%, compared to the prior year ended December 31, 2024. This increase was primarily due to additional expense recorded to settle with former Twitter employees as part of the workforce reduction program implemented in 2022.
paras.zh: 截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日止年度的重组费用较上一截至 2024 年 12 月 31 日止年度增加 $274 million，即 129.1%。该增加主要归因于作为 2022 年实施的裁员计划的一部分，与前 Twitter 员工达成和解所记录的额外费用。

paras.en: Loss from Operations
paras.zh: 经营亏损

paras.en: AI loss from operations for the year ended December 31, 2025 increased by $4,794 million, or 307.1%, compared to the prior year ended December 31, 2024 driven by the factors described above.
paras.zh: 截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日止年度的 AI 经营亏损较上一截至 2024 年 12 月 31 日止年度增加 $4,794 million，即 307.1%，系由上述因素所致。

paras.en: Revenue

paras.en: Cost of Revenue
paras.zh: 收入成本

paras.en: Cost of revenue for the year ended December 31, 2024 increased by $1,886 million, or 30.9%, compared to the prior year ended December 31, 2023. This increase was primarily due to a higher cost of revenue from the Connectivity segment of $1,982 million as a result of the higher volume spend on Starlink Kits as deliveries increased and higher depreciation of launch costs driven by an increase in the number of satellites placed into orbit, partially offset by cost efficiency from increased reusability of our Falcon launch vehicles in our Space segment of $128 million.
paras.zh: 截至 2024 年 12 月 31 日止年度的收入成本较上一截至 2023 年 12 月 31 日止年度增加 $1,886 百万，增幅 30.9%。该增加主要归因于互联业务分部的收入成本增加 $1,982 百万，原因是随着交付量增加，Starlink Kits 的支出量增加，以及因入轨卫星数量增加导致发射成本折旧增加，部分被我们太空业务分部因 Falcon 运载火箭可重复使用性提高带来的成本效率 $128 百万所抵消。

paras.en: Research and Development
paras.zh: 研发

paras.en: Research and development for the year ended December 31, 2024 increased by $1,359 million, or 64.6%, compared to the prior year ended December 31, 2023. This increase was primarily due to higher cost in our AI segment of $990 million related to advancing our AI technologies and higher costs of $297 million in our Space segment for investment in Starship production, launch and engineering costs, and related facilities.
paras.zh: 截至 2024 年 12 月 31 日止年度的研发较上一截至 2023 年 12 月 31 日止年度增加 $1,359 百万，增幅 64.6%。该增加主要归因于我们 AI 业务分部与推进 AI 技术相关的成本增加 $990 百万，以及我们太空业务分部对 Starship 生产、发射和工程成本及相关设施的投资成本增加 $297 百万。

paras.en: Selling, general, and administrative for the year ended December 31, 2024 increased by $148 million, or 8.9%, compared to the prior year ended December 31, 2023. This increase was primarily due to: (i) higher international expansion costs of $18 million, higher employee compensation expenses (including salaries, benefits, and share-based compensation) of $11 million, and higher allocated general and administrative overhead of $54 million in our Connectivity segment, and (ii) higher employee compensation expenses (including salaries, benefits, and share-based compensation) and professional fees of $25 million in our Space segment.
paras.zh: 截至 2024 年 12 月 31 日止年度的销售、一般及管理费用较上一截至 2023 年 12 月 31 日止年度增加 $148 million，增幅 8.9%。该增加主要由于：(i) 国际扩张成本增加 $18 million、员工薪酬费用（包括工资、福利及股份支付薪酬）增加 $11 million，以及我们 Connectivity 板块分摊的一般及管理费用增加 $54 million；以及 (ii) 我们 Space 板块的员工薪酬费用（包括工资、福利及股份支付薪酬）及专业服务费增加 $25 million。

paras.en: Restructuring charges for the year ended December 31, 2024 decreased by $24 million, or 10.1%, compared to the prior year ended December 31, 2023. This decrease was due to the impairment on office leases assumed as part of the Twitter acquisition that occurred during the year ended December 31, 2023, partially offset by an increase in workforce-related restructuring charges.

paras.zh: 截至 2024 年 12 月 31 日止年度的减值较上一截至 2023 年 12 月 31 日止年度减少 $3,712 million，降幅 98.3%。截至 2023 年 12 月 31 日止年度的减值主要与 Twitter 品牌在更名为 X 后发生的减值有关。

paras.en: Cost of Revenue

paras.en: Cost of revenue for the year ended December 31, 2024 decreased by $128 million,or 7.6%, compared to the prior year ended December 31, 2023. This decrease was primarily due to increased reusability of our Falcon launch vehicles resulting in lower depreciation of $80 million, lowering the cost of each launch. The decrease was also due to the relative increase in Starlink satellite launches from 63 launches in 2023 to 89 launches in 2024, resulting in relatively more of our launch operations and overhead costs capitalized in our Connectivity segment of $99 million. This decrease was offset by an increase in launch overhead costs of $77 million due to the increase in Falcon launches.
paras.zh: 截至 2024 年 12 月 31 日止年度的收入成本较上一截至 2023 年 12 月 31 日止年度减少 $128 million，降幅 7.6%。该减少主要由于我们 Falcon 运载火箭可重复使用性提高，使折旧减少 $80 million，从而降低了每次发射的成本。该减少还由于 Starlink 卫星发射次数相对增加，从 2023 年的 63 次发射增至 2024 年的 89 次发射，使相对更多的发射运营和间接费用 $99 million 资本化计入我们的 Connectivity 分部。该减少被发射间接费用增加 $77 million 所部分抵消，该增加系因 Falcon 发射次数增加所致。

This increase was primarily driven by an increase of$2,013 million in revenue from our consumer subscribers, composed of96.5% growth in Starlink Subscribers offset by a 8.1% decline in Starlink Subscriber ARPU primarily due to international expansion. In addition, Connectivity revenue had an increase of $1,717 million from our enterprise and government customers, primarily driven by the growth in our enterprise connectivity business of $466 million and growth in our government connectivity business of $1,250 million.
paras.zh: 截至 2024 年 12 月 31 日止年度的收入较上一截至 2023 年 12 月 31 日止年度增加 $3,730 百万，即 96.4%。该增加主要受我们消费者订阅用户收入增加 $2,013 百万所推动，其中 Starlink 订阅用户增长 96.5%，但被 Starlink 订阅用户 ARPU 下降 8.1% 所部分抵消，后者主要由于国际扩张。此外，来自企业及政府客户的连接业务收入增加 $1,717 百万，主要受我们企业连接业务增长 $466 百万及政府连接业务增长 $1,250 百万所推动。

paras.en: Cost of Revenue
paras.zh: 收入成本

paras.en: Cost of revenue for the year ended December 31, 2024 increased by $1,982 million,or 71.1%, compared to the prior year ended December 31, 2023. This increase was primarily due to higher volume spend on Starlink Kits of $907 million driven by higher kit deliveries and higher depreciation of $555 million from capitalized launch and satellite costs driven by an increase in the number of launches and satellites placed into orbit.
paras.zh: 截至 2024 年 12 月 31 日止年度的收入成本较上一截至 2023 年 12 月 31 日止年度增加 $1,982 百万，即 71.1%。该增加主要由于 Starlink Kits 的销量支出增加 $907 百万（受套件交付量增加推动），以及资本化发射及卫星成本折旧增加 $555 百万（受发射次数及入轨卫星数量增加推动）。

paras.en: Research and Development
paras.zh: 研发

paras.en: Research and development for the year ended December 31, 2024 increased by $72 million,or 18.8%, compared to the prior year ended December 31, 2023. This increase was primarily due to higher costs for the next-generation production development of satellites of $73 million, ground equipment of $4 million, offset by lower costs of $4 million for Starlink Kits.
paras.zh: 截至 2024 年 12 月 31 日止年度的研发费用较上一截至 2023 年 12 月 31 日止年度增加 $72 百万，即 18.8%。该增加主要由于下一代卫星生产开发成本增加 $73 百万、地面设备成本增加 $4 百万，但被 Starlink Kits 成本减少 $4 百万所部分抵消。

paras.en: Selling, General, and Administrative
paras.zh: 销售、一般及行政

paras.en: Selling, general, and administrative for the year ended December 31, 2024 increased by $100 million,or 43.0%, compared to the prior year ended December 31, 2023. This increase was primarily due to higher international expansion costs of $18 million, higher employee compensation expenses (including salaries, benefits, and share-based compensation) of $11 million, and higher allocated general and administrative overhead of $54 million.
paras.zh: 截至 2024 年 12 月 31 日止年度的销售、一般及行政费用较上一截至 2023 年 12 月 31 日止年度增加 $100 百万，即 43.0%。该增加主要由于国际扩张成本增加 $18 百万、员工薪酬费用（包括工资、福利及股份支付薪酬）增加 $11 百万，以及分摊的一般及行政间接费用增加 $54 百万。

paras.en: Impairment
paras.zh: 减值

paras.en: Impairment for the year ended December 31, 2024 increased by $39 million compared to the prior year ended December 31, 2023. This increase was due to a discontinuation of a certain Starlink Kit production line.
paras.zh: 截至 2024 年 12 月 31 日止年度的减值较上一截至 2023 年 12 月 31 日止年度增加 $39 million。该增加是由于某条 Starlink Kit 生产线停产所致。

paras.en: Income from operations for the year ended December 31, 2024 increased by $1,537 million, or 327.4%, compared to the prior year ended December 31, 2023 driven by the factors described above.

paras.en: Revenue

paras.en: Revenue for the year ended December 31, 2024 decreased by $341 million,or 11.5%, compared to the prior year ended December 31, 2023. This decrease was due to a decrease in advertising revenue of $595 million, partially offset by an increase in AI solutions and infrastructure revenue of $254 million. The decrease in advertising revenue was due to the loss of advertising partners for X. The increase in AI solutions and infrastructure was due to an increase in X subscription revenue of $157 million and an increase in data licensing arrangements of $90 million. In 2023 and 2024, substantially all of our AI segment revenue consisted of advertising, subscriptions, and data licensing revenue generated from X, formerly known as Twitter.
paras.zh: 截至 2024 年 12 月 31 日止年度的收入较上一截至 2023 年 12 月 31 日止年度减少 $341 million，即 11.5%。该减少是由于广告收入减少 $595 million，部分被 AI 解决方案及基础设施收入增加 $254 million 所抵消。广告收入减少是由于 X 失去广告合作伙伴。AI 解决方案及基础设施收入增加是由于 X 订阅收入增加 $157 million 以及数据许可安排增加 $90 million。2023 年和 2024 年，我们 AI 分部的绝大部分收入由来自 X（前称 Twitter）的广告、订阅及数据许可收入构成。

paras.en: Cost of Revenue
paras.zh: 收入成本

paras.en: Cost of revenue for the year ended December 31, 2024 increased by $32 million,or 1.9%, compared to the prior year ended December 31, 2023. This increase was primarily due to higher server depreciation of $97 million, partially offset by lower infrastructure and revenue share expenses of $46 million, and lower employee and facilities-related expenses of $18 million resulting from the Company’s restructuring and cost reduction efforts.
paras.zh: 截至 2024 年 12 月 31 日止年度的收入成本较上一截至 2023 年 12 月 31 日止年度增加 $32 million，即 1.9%。该增加主要由于服务器折旧增加 $97 million，部分被基础设施及收入分成费用减少 $46 million 以及因公司重组及降本举措导致的员工及设施相关费用减少 $18 million 所抵消。

paras.en: Research and Development
paras.zh: 研发

paras.en: Research and development for the year ended December 31, 2024 increased by $990 million,or 531.5%, compared to the prior year ended December 31, 2023. This increase was primarily due to increased investments made in advancing our AI technologies, including employee compensation expenses (including salaries, benefits, and share-based compensation) and infrastructure services of $703 million and higher depreciation of $321 million for our equipment hardware.
paras.zh: 截至 2024 年 12 月 31 日止年度的研发费用较上一年的截至 2023 年 12 月 31 日止年度增加 $990 million，即 531.5%。该增加主要归因于为推进我们 AI 技术而增加的投资，包括员工薪酬费用（含工资、福利及股份支付薪酬）及基础设施服务 $703 million，以及设备硬件折旧增加 $321 million。

paras.en: Selling, General, and Administrative
paras.zh: 销售、一般及行政

paras.en: Selling, general, and administrative for the year ended December 31, 2024 increased by $24 million,or 2.3%, compared to the prior year ended December 31, 2023. This increase was primarily due to an increase in our amortization expense of $107 million related to the Twitter brand becoming a finite-lived intangible asset and higher legal costs of $65 million, partially offset by lower employee and facilities related costs of $125 million and lower professional fees of $23 million resulting from the Company’s restructuring and cost reduction efforts.
paras.zh: 截至 2024 年 12 月 31 日止年度的销售、一般及行政费用较上一年的截至 2023 年 12 月 31 日止年度增加 $24 million，即 2.3%。该增加主要归因于与 Twitter 品牌成为有限寿命无形资产相关的摊销费用增加 $107 million 以及法律费用增加 $65 million，部分被因公司重组及降本举措导致的员工及设施相关成本减少 $125 million 和专业费用减少 $23 million 所抵消。

paras.en: Restructuring charges
paras.zh: 重组费用

paras.en: Restructuring charges for the year ended December 31, 2024 decreased by $24 million,or 10.2%, compared to the prior year ended December 31, 2023. This decrease was due to the impairment on the office leases assumed as part of the Twitter acquisition that primarily occurred during the year ended December 31, 2023, partially offset by an increase in workforce-related restructuring charges.
paras.zh: 截至 2024 年 12 月 31 日止年度的重组费用较上一年的截至 2023 年 12 月 31 日止年度减少 $24 million，即 10.2%。该减少归因于作为 Twitter 收购一部分而承接的办公租赁减值（主要发生于截至 2023 年 12 月 31 日止年度），部分被劳动力相关重组费用增加所抵消。

paras.zh: 截至 2024 年 12 月 31 日止年度的减值较上一年的截至 2023 年 12 月 31 日止年度减少 $3,775 million。截至 2023 年 12 月 31 日止年度的减值与 Twitter 品牌无形资产在其更名为 X 后的减值相关。

paras.en: Management believes that certain financial measures that are not presented in accordance with GAAP provide management and investors with useful supplemental information that provides a meaningful view of our financial condition and results of operations across periods by removing the impact of items that management believes do not directly reflect our ongoing operating performance. Adjusted EBITDA and Segment Adjusted EBITDA are supplemental measures that are not required by or presented in accordance with GAAP. In evaluating our performance as measured by Adjusted EBITDA and Segment Adjusted EBITDA, management recognizes and considers the limitations of these measures. Other companies in our industry may calculate Adjusted EBITDA and Segment Adjusted EBITDA differently than we do or may not calculate them at all, limiting their usefulness as comparative measures. Because of these limitations, Adjusted EBITDA and Segment Adjusted EBITDA should not be considered in isolation or as a substitute for net income (loss), income (loss) from operations, or any other measure calculated in accordance with GAAP, and should be considered together with our GAAP financial measures and the reconciliations to the corresponding most directly comparable GAAP financial measures set forth in this prospectus.
paras.zh: 管理层认为，某些未按照 GAAP 列报的财务指标为管理层和投资者提供了有用的补充信息，通过剔除管理层认为不直接反映我们持续经营业绩的项目，使各方能够有意义地了解我们在各期间的财务状况和经营成果。调整后 EBITDA 和分部调整后 EBITDA 是补充指标，并非 GAAP 所要求或按照 GAAP 列报。在评估以调整后 EBITDA 和分部调整后 EBITDA 衡量的业绩时，管理层认识到并考虑了这些指标的局限性。我们行业中的其他公司对调整后 EBITDA 和分部调整后 EBITDA 的计算方式可能与我们不同，或者可能根本不计算这些指标，从而限制了其作为可比指标的有用性。由于存在这些局限性，调整后 EBITDA 和分部调整后 EBITDA 不应被孤立地看待，也不应被视为净利润（亏损）、经营利润（亏损）或任何其他按照 GAAP 计算的指标的替代，而应与我们的 GAAP 财务指标以及本招股说明书中列示的与最直接可比的相应 GAAP 财务指标的对账一并考虑。

paras.en: Adjusted EBITDA is defined as net income (loss) excluding (i) depreciation and amortization, (ii) share-based compensation, (iii) impairment, (iv) restructuring charges, (v) interest expense, (vi) interest income, (vii) other income (expense), net and (viii) provision for income taxes. Segment Adjusted EBITDA is defined as segment income (loss) from operations excluding (i) depreciation and amortization, (ii) share-based compensation, (iii) restructuring charges, and (iv) impairment. Adjusted EBITDA and Segment Adjusted EBITDA are key performance measures that our management uses to assess our financial performance as well as for internal planning and forecasting purposes. We consider Adjusted EBITDA and Segment Adjusted EBITDA to be meaningful performance measures for investors to evaluate our operating performance and to compare the financial results between periods.
paras.zh: 调整后 EBITDA 定义为净利润（亏损）剔除 (i) 折旧和摊销、(ii) 股份支付、(iii) 减值、(iv) 重组费用、(v) 利息费用、(vi) 利息收入、(vii) 其他收入（费用）净额及 (viii) 所得税费用（收益）。分部调整后 EBITDA 定义为分部经营利润（亏损）剔除 (i) 折旧和摊销、(ii) 股份支付、(iii) 重组费用及 (iv) 减值。调整后 EBITDA 和分部调整后 EBITDA 是管理层用于评估财务业绩以及内部规划和预测目的的关键业绩指标。我们认为，调整后 EBITDA 和分部调整后 EBITDA 是有意义的业绩指标，可供投资者评估我们的经营业绩并比较各期间的财务结果。

Our primary sources of liquidity are cash flows generated from operations, our total cash and cash equivalents of $15,852 million as of March 31, 2026, short-term marketable securities of $7,823 million as of March 31, 2026, and borrowings under our credit facilities. As of March 31, 2026, we have $1,500 million available to borrow under the SpaceX Credit Facility. The cash we generate from our core operations also enables us to fund our research and development projects including our Starship rocket and next-generation satellites, the construction of future data centers, and the continued expansion of our AI-enabled products.
paras.zh: 我们的主要流动性来源为经营活动产生的现金流、截至 2026 年 3 月 31 日的现金及现金等价物总额 15,852 百万美元、截至 2026 年 3 月 31 日的短期有价证券 7,823 百万美元，以及我们信贷额度项下的借款。截至 2026 年 3 月 31 日，我们在 SpaceX 信贷额度项下尚有 1,500 百万美元可供借入。我们核心业务产生的现金也使我们能够为研发项目提供资金，包括我们的 Starship 火箭和下一代卫星、未来数据中心的建设，以及我们 AI 赋能产品的持续扩张。

paras.en: In addition, because we expect a significant portion of our future expenditures to fund growth initiatives, we retain flexibility to adjust spending across segments. For example, if our near-term data center needs decrease in scale or ramp more slowly than expected, including due to global economic, tax, trade or business conditions, we may reduce future capital expenditures in this segment and reallocate those expenditures to other segments based on business priorities and growth opportunities. In addition, we continually evaluate our cash needs and may decide it is best to raise additional capital or seek alternative financing sources to fund the rapid growth of our business, including through drawdowns on existing or new debt facilities. We may seek to refinance the SpaceX Bridge Loan, including with the proceeds from notes offerings, bank borrowings, or other financial arrangements. We may also from time to time determine that it is in our best interests to voluntarily repay certain indebtedness early.
paras.zh: 此外，由于我们预计未来支出的很大一部分将用于为增长计划提供资金，我们保留在各分部之间调整支出的灵活性。例如，如果我们的近期数据中心需求规模下降或爬坡速度慢于预期（包括由于全球经济、税收、贸易或商业状况所致），我们可能减少该分部未来的资本支出，并根据业务优先级和增长机会将这些支出重新分配至其他分部。此外，我们持续评估我们的现金需求，并可能决定最好通过现有或新增债务融资项下提款等方式筹集额外资本或寻求替代融资来源，以为我们业务的快速增长提供资金。我们可能寻求对 SpaceX 过桥贷款进行再融资，包括使用票据发行所得款项、银行借款或其他财务安排。我们还可能不时认定提前自愿偿还某些债务符合我们的最佳利益。

paras.en: Accordingly, we believe we have sufficient sources of funding to meet our business requirements for at least the next twelve months from the issuance of the consolidated financial statements.
paras.zh: 因此，我们认为我们拥有充足的资金来源，可满足自合并财务报表发布之日起至少未来十二个月的业务需求。

paras.en: #### Debt Agreements
paras.zh: #### 债务协议

paras.en: SpaceX Credit Facility
paras.zh: SpaceX 信贷额度

paras.en: In February 2025, SpaceX entered into a five-year senior unsecured revolving credit agreement with a syndicate of banks, under which the Company may borrow up to $1,500 million (“SpaceX Credit Facility”). The SpaceX Credit Facility is subject to certain customary representations, warranties, covenants, and events of default, including a maximum financial covenant requiring the Company to maintain a Consolidated Leverage Ratio (as defined in the SpaceX Credit Facility) of no greater than 3.75 to 1.0 as of the end of each fiscal quarter (subject to temporary increases to 4.25 to 1.0 following certain qualified acquisitions) and other customary reporting requirements. The SpaceX Credit Facility also includes sublimits of up to $150 million for financial letters of credit and up to $1,000 million for performance letters of credit. The SpaceX Credit Facility terminates, and all outstanding loans become due and payable, on February 7, 2030, unless the parties agree to an extension in accordance with the terms of the SpaceX Credit Facility. As of March 31, 2026 and December 31, 2025, no amounts were outstanding under the SpaceX Credit Facility.
paras.zh: 2025 年 2 月，SpaceX 与一个银行银团签订了为期五年的高级无抵押循环信贷协议，根据该协议，公司可借入最高 1,500 百万美元（“SpaceX 信贷额度”）。SpaceX 信贷额度受若干惯常陈述、保证、契约和违约事件约束，其中包括一项最高财务契约，要求公司在每个财季末维持不高于 3.75 比 1.0 的合并杠杆率（SpaceX 信贷额度中定义）（在发生某些合格收购后可临时提高至 4.25 比 1.0），以及其他惯常报告要求。SpaceX 信贷额度还包括最高 150 百万美元的财务信用证分限额和最高 1,000 百万美元的履约信用证分限额。除非各方按照 SpaceX 信贷额度条款约定展期，SpaceX 信贷额度将于 2030 年 2 月 7 日终止，届时所有未偿还贷款到期应付。截至 2026 年 3 月 31 日和 2025 年 12 月 31 日，SpaceX 信贷额度项下无未偿还金额。

paras.en: Borrowings under the SpaceX Credit Facility bear interest, at the Company’s option, at a rate per annum equal to (i) a forward-looking term rate based on SOFR (“Term SOFR”) plus an applicable margin ranging from 0.75% and 1.25% (depending on the Company’s debt rating), or (ii) a base rate equal to the highest of (a) Federal Funds Rate plus 0.5%, (b) the Prime Rate, (c) Term SOFR plus 1.00%, and (d) 1.00% plus an applicable margin ranging from 0.0% and 0.25% (depending on the Company’s debt rating). The Company may also borrow in various alternative currencies, with interest calculated at rates based on SONIA for Pound Sterling-denominated loans and EURIBOR for Euro-denominated loans, plus an applicable margin. In addition, the Company pays a commitment fee on the unused portion of the SpaceX Credit Facility, which ranges from 0.07% (amended to 0.06% under the Amended SpaceX Credit Facility described below) to 0.11% per annum based on the Company’s debt rating. As of March 31, 2026, the Company was in compliance with all covenants under the SpaceX Credit Facility.
paras.zh: SpaceX 信贷融资项下的借款按公司选择，以年利率计息，利率等于 (i) 基于 SOFR 的前瞻性期限利率（“Term SOFR”）加上 0.75% 至 1.25% 的适用利差（取决于公司的债务评级），或 (ii) 基准利率，即以下各项中的最高者：(a) 联邦基金利率加 0.5%，(b) 最优惠利率，(c) Term SOFR 加 1.00%，以及 (d) 1.00% 加上 0.0% 至 0.25% 的适用利差（取决于公司的债务评级）。公司还可以多种替代货币借款，英镑计价贷款的利息按基于 SONIA 的利率计算，欧元计价贷款的利息按基于 EURIBOR 的利率计算，另加适用利差。此外，公司就 SpaceX 信贷融资的未使用部分支付承诺费，根据公司债务评级，年费率为 0.07%（根据下文所述经修订的 SpaceX 信贷融资，修订为 0.06%）至 0.11%。截至 2026 年 3 月 31 日，公司遵守了 SpaceX 信贷融资项下的所有契约。

paras.en: In March 2026, the Company entered into a First Amendment to Credit Agreement and Waiver (the “First Amendment”) with its lenders, in connection with the Company’s entry into the SpaceX Bridge Loan (as defined below). The First Amendment, among other things, (i) waived certain specified defaults and (ii) amended certain definitions and covenants under the SpaceX Credit Facility to conform to the terms of the SpaceX Bridge Loan.
paras.zh: 2026 年 3 月，就公司订立 SpaceX 过桥贷款（定义见下文）事宜，公司与贷款方订立了《信贷协议第一修正案及豁免》（“第一修正案”）。第一修正案除其他事项外，(i) 豁免了某些特定违约，并 (ii) 修订了 SpaceX 信贷融资项下的某些定义和契约，以与 SpaceX 过桥贷款的条款保持一致。

paras.en: In May 2026, SpaceX amended the SpaceX Credit Facility to increase the borrowing capacity up to $5,000 million (“Amended SpaceX Credit Facility”). As part of the Amended SpaceX Credit Facility, the sublimit for performance letters of credit was increased to $2,000 million. The Amended SpaceX Credit Facility terminates, and all outstanding loans become due and payable, on May 19, 2031, unless the parties agree to an extension in accordance with the terms of the Amended SpaceX Credit Facility. All other terms were consistent with the terms of the SpaceX Credit Facility.
paras.zh: 2026 年 5 月，SpaceX 修订了 SpaceX 信贷融资，将借款能力提高至最高 $5,000 million（“经修订的 SpaceX 信贷融资”）。作为经修订的 SpaceX 信贷融资的一部分，履约信用证的子限额提高至 $2,000 million。除非各方按照经修订的 SpaceX 信贷融资的条款同意展期，否则经修订的 SpaceX 信贷融资于 2031 年 5 月 19 日终止，所有未偿还贷款届时到期应付。所有其他条款与 SpaceX 信贷融资的条款一致。

paras.en: SpaceX Bridge Loan
paras.zh: SpaceX 过桥贷款

paras.en: In March 2026, SpaceX entered into a new bridge loan credit agreement (the “SpaceX Bridge Loan”) with a syndicate of lenders, providing for an unsecured bridge term loan facility in an aggregate principal amount of $20,000 million. The SpaceX Bridge Loan matures on September 2, 2027, with two three-month extensions at the Company’s option, subject to the absence of a continuing default and the payment of an extension fee of 0.25% of the aggregate outstanding principal per extension, resulting in a final extended maturity date of March 2028.
paras.zh: 2026 年 3 月，SpaceX 与一个贷款方银团订立了一项新的过桥贷款信贷协议（“SpaceX 过桥贷款”），提供本金总额为 $20,000 million 的无担保过桥定期贷款融资。SpaceX 过桥贷款于 2027 年 9 月 2 日到期，公司可选择进行两次三个月的展期，前提是不存在持续违约，且每次展期须支付相当于未偿还本金总额 0.25% 的展期费，最终展期到期日为 2028 年 3 月。

paras.en: The proceeds of the SpaceX Bridge Loan were used to repay the X B-1 Term Loan, the X B-3 Term Loan, the xAI Fixed Rate Loan, the xAI Floating Rate Loan and the xAI 12.5% Senior Secured Notes (as defined and described in Note 10, Debt, to the consolidated financial statements included elsewhere in this prospectus). The Company may also use the remaining proceeds for general corporate purposes.
paras.zh: SpaceX 过桥贷款的所得款项用于偿还 X B-1 定期贷款、X B-3 定期贷款、xAI 固定利率贷款、xAI 浮动利率贷款及 xAI 12.5% 优先担保票据（定义及描述见本招股说明书其他部分所载合并财务报表附注 10“债务”）。公司还可将剩余所得款项用于一般公司用途。

paras.en: The SpaceX Bridge Loan bears interest, at the Company’s election, at a rate per annum equal to (i) Term SOFR plus an applicable margin ranging from 0.75%-1.75% (depending on the Company’s debt rating), or (ii) a base rate equal to the highest of (a) the Federal Funds Rate plus 0.5%, (b) the Prime Rate, (c) Term SOFR plus 1.0% and (d) 1.00%, plus an applicable margin ranging from 0.00% to 0.75% (depending on the Company’s debt rating). In addition, the Company is obligated to pay duration fees equal to 0.125% of outstanding principal on the first anniversary of closing and 0.25% of outstanding principal on the fifteen-month anniversary of closing. As of March 31, 2026, the Company was in compliance with all covenants under the SpaceX Bridge Loan.
paras.zh: SpaceX 过桥贷款按公司选择计息，年利率等于 (i) Term SOFR 加适用利差 0.75%-1.75%（取决于公司债务评级），或 (ii) 基准利率（等于以下最高者：(a) 联邦基金利率加 0.5%，(b) 最优惠利率，(c) Term SOFR 加 1.0%，及 (d) 1.00%）加适用利差 0.00% 至 0.75%（取决于公司债务评级）。此外，公司有义务支付期限费，金额为交割一周年时未偿本金的 0.125% 及交割十五个月周年时未偿本金的 0.25%。截至 2026 年 3 月 31 日，公司遵守 SpaceX 过桥贷款项下的所有契约。

paras.en: The obligations of the Company under the SpaceX Bridge Loan are guaranteed on a joint and several basis by X Corp., X.AI LLC, and CTC Property LLC (each a subsidiary of the Company). The SpaceX Bridge Loan may be prepaid at any time, in whole or in part, without premium or penalty. The Company is required to use an amount equal to the net cash proceeds of certain debt financings to repay amounts outstanding under the SpaceX Bridge Loan and to apply an amount equal to the net proceeds of a qualified initial public offering, including this offering, to repay such amounts within six months following receipt of such proceeds.
paras.zh: 公司于 SpaceX 过桥贷款项下的义务由 X Corp.、X.AI LLC 及 CTC Property LLC（均为公司子公司）以连带责任方式提供担保。SpaceX 过桥贷款可随时全部或部分提前偿还，无需支付溢价或罚金。公司须将若干债务融资的净现金收益用于偿还 SpaceX 过桥贷款项下的未偿金额，并须将合格首次公开发行（包括本次发行）的净收益在收到该等收益后六个月内用于偿还该等金额。

paras.en: The SpaceX Bridge Loan contains customary events of default and affirmative and negative covenants, including restrictions on liens, subsidiary indebtedness, fundamental changes (including a prohibition on the disposition of Starlink assets and other material businesses outside the consolidated group), and changes in the nature of the Company’s business. The sole financial maintenance covenant requires the Company to maintain a Consolidated Leverage Ratio — defined as consolidated funded indebtedness (net of 85% of unrestricted cash) to Consolidated EBITDA (as defined in the SpaceX Bridge Loan) — of no greater than 3.75 to 1.0 as of the end of each fiscal quarter, with a temporary step-up to 4.25 to 1.0 for four fiscal quarters following a qualifying acquisition of at least $1.0 billion.
paras.zh: SpaceX 过桥贷款包含惯常的违约事件及肯定性和否定性契约，包括对留置权、子公司债务、根本性变更（包括禁止在合并集团之外处置 Starlink 资产及其他重要业务）以及公司业务性质变更的限制。唯一的财务维持契约要求公司维持合并杠杆率——定义为合并融资债务（扣除 85% 的非受限现金）与合并 EBITDA（按 SpaceX 过桥贷款定义）之比——在每个财季末不高于 3.75 比 1.0，并在完成至少 $1.0 billion 的合格收购后四个财季内临时上调至 4.25 比 1.0。

paras.en: #### Material Cash Commitments
paras.zh: #### 重大现金承诺

paras.en: From time to time in the ordinary course of business, we enter into agreements with suppliers for the purchase of parts and raw materials to manufacture our products. However, due to contractual terms, variability in the precise growth curves of our development and production ramps, and opportunities to renegotiate pricing, these contracts generally do not have long-term binding and enforceable purchase orders, and the timing and magnitude of purchase orders beyond the short term is difficult to accurately project. Because we do not have long-term purchase orders for these parts and raw materials, future purchases may result in material cash commitments. For additional information about this risk, please refer to “Risk Factors” in this prospectus.
paras.zh: 在日常经营过程中，我们不时与供应商订立协议，采购用于制造产品的零部件和原材料。然而，由于合同条款、我们开发和生产爬坡的精确增长曲线存在可变性，以及重新协商定价的机会，这些合同通常没有长期具有约束力和可强制执行的采购订单，短期之后的采购订单的时间和规模难以准确预测。由于我们对该等零部件和原材料没有长期采购订单，未来采购可能导致重大现金承诺。有关此风险的更多信息，请参阅本招股说明书中的“风险因素”。

paras.en: On September 7, 2025, the Company entered into a License Purchase Agreement (the “Spectrum License Purchase Agreement”) with Spectrum Business Trust 2025-1, a Nevada Business Trust (“Trust”) and EchoStar Corporation (“EchoStar”) for the purchase of EchoStar’s licenses related to 50 MHz of spectrum (the “AWS-4 and H-Block Licenses” and the transactions contemplated thereby, “Spectrum Transaction”). On November 5, 2025 the parties amended and restated the Spectrum License Purchase Agreement to include EchoStar’s licenses for up to 15 MHz of additional unpaired AWS-3 spectrum (together with the AWS-4 and H-Block Licenses, the “Spectrum Licenses”).
paras.zh: 2025 年 9 月 7 日，本公司与 Spectrum Business Trust 2025-1（一家内华达州商业信托，“信托”）及 EchoStar Corporation（“EchoStar”）签订了一份许可购买协议（“频谱许可购买协议”），以购买 EchoStar 与 50 MHz 频谱相关的许可（“AWS-4 及 H-Block 许可”，连同其拟进行的交易，统称“频谱交易”）。2025 年 11 月 5 日，各方对频谱许可购买协议进行了修订和重述，以纳入 EchoStar 最多 15 MHz 额外非成对 AWS-3 频谱的许可（连同 AWS-4 及 H-Block 许可，统称“频谱许可”）。

paras.en: The total consideration for the acquisition of the Spectrum Licenses is approximately $19.6 billion, consisting of (i) approximately $11.1 billion in equity, payable through the issuance of approximately 261.8 million shares of the Company’s Class A common stock at a fixed value of $42.40 per share, and (ii) up to $8.5 billion related to the payoff of designated EchoStar debt, with any shortfall below $8.5 billion to be paid in cash. The allocation of cash and equity consideration is subject to certain adjustments based on the amount of EchoStar debt satisfied at or prior to closing. The Spectrum License Purchase Agreement provides that the transfer of the Spectrum Licenses occurs in two steps: first, the transfer of the Spectrum Licenses by EchoStar to the Trust (the “Spectrum Transfer Closing”), and second, the Spectrum Licenses will be transferred by the Trust to the Company (the “Spectrum Acquisition Closing”). The Foreign Assets will be transferred directly to the Company at the Spectrum Acquisition Closing, to the extent the required regulatory approvals have been obtained by such date; provided, however, that the failure to obtain such approvals will not delay or prevent the Spectrum Acquisition Closing.
paras.zh: 收购频谱许可的总对价约为$19.6 billion，包括(i)约$11.1 billion 的股权对价，通过按每股$42.40 的固定价值发行约 261.8 million 股本公司的 A 类普通股支付，以及(ii)最多$8.5 billion 用于偿还指定的 EchoStar 债务，低于$8.5 billion 的任何差额将以现金支付。现金与股权对价的分配将根据交割时或之前已清偿的 EchoStar 债务金额进行某些调整。频谱许可购买协议规定，频谱许可的转让分两步进行：第一步，EchoStar 将频谱许可转让给信托（“频谱转让交割”）；第二步，信托将频谱许可转让给本公司（“频谱收购交割”）。在截至该日期已获得所需监管批准的情况下，境外资产将在频谱收购交割时直接转让给本公司；但未能获得该等批准不会延迟或阻止频谱收购交割。

paras.en: In connection with the Spectrum License Purchase Agreement, the Company and the Trust entered into a credit agreement (the “Spectrum Credit Agreement”), pursuant to which the Company has agreed upon the Spectrum Transfer Closing, to make payments to the Trust (via loans which are contemplated to be forgiven at six-month intervals), for the Trust to make payments on EchoStar’s debt (interest only) through at least November 30, 2027, but in no event later than November 30, 2028. Although these payments are structured as loans from the Company to the Trust, there is no expectation of repayment as the loan payments are forgiven and are accounted for as additional consideration for the acquisition of the Spectrum Licenses. Accordingly, the payments are recognized as prepaid assets until the Spectrum Acquisition Closing at which point they will be recognized as intangible assets. Total payments expected to be made under the Spectrum Credit Agreement are $1,241 million in 2026 and $828 million in 2027, assuming an expected closing date of November 30, 2027. The Company may need to make additional payments totaling $827 million if the Spectrum Acquisition Closing occurs at November 30, 2028.
paras.zh: 就频谱许可购买协议而言，本公司与信托签订了一份信贷协议（“频谱信贷协议”），据此，本公司已同意在频谱转让交割时向信托付款（通过拟每六个月豁免一次的贷款），以便信托至少到 2027 年 11 月 30 日（但无论如何不迟于 2028 年 11 月 30 日）支付 EchoStar 债务的款项（仅利息）。尽管该等付款在结构上为本公司向信托提供的贷款，但预计不会获得偿还，因为贷款付款被豁免并作为收购频谱许可的额外对价进行会计处理。因此，该等付款在频谱收购交割前确认为预付资产，在频谱收购交割时确认为无形资产。假设预期交割日为 2027 年 11 月 30 日，根据频谱信贷协议预计将支付的款项总额为 2026 年$1,241 million 及 2027 年$828 million。如果频谱收购交割于 2028 年 11 月 30 日发生，本公司可能需要支付总额为$827 million 的额外款项。

paras.en: The Spectrum Transaction was approved by the FCC on May 12, 2026, and the Spectrum Transfer Closing occurred on May 22, 2026. On that date, the Spectrum Licenses were transferred to the Trust, where they will remain until the Spectrum Acquisition Closing. Upon closing, the Company intends to either use cash and cash equivalents on hand or seek alternative financing sources to fund the cash payment to EchoStar. The $11.1 billion equity consideration will be issued at the Spectrum Acquisition Closing.
paras.zh: 频谱交易已于 2026 年 5 月 12 日获得 FCC 批准，频谱转让交割于 2026 年 5 月 22 日完成。在该日，频谱许可证被转让至信托，并将一直保留在该信托中，直至频谱收购交割。交割时，公司拟使用手头现金及现金等价物，或寻求其他融资来源，以支付向 EchoStar 支付的现金对价。$11.1 billion 的股权对价将在频谱收购交割时发行。

paras.en: As of March 31, 2026, we and our subsidiaries had outstanding$29,132 million in aggregate principal amount of indebtedness and no debt principal payments are due until August 28, 2027 if we choose not to extend. As of March 31, 2026, our total minimum lease payments was $5,823 million, of which$1,026 million is due within this fiscal year. For details regarding our indebtedness and lease obligations, refer to Note 10, Debt, and Note 11, Leases of our audited consolidated financial statements and Note 9, Debt of our unaudited consolidated financial statements included elsewhere in this prospectus.
paras.zh: 截至 2026 年 3 月 31 日，我们及我们的子公司未偿债务本金总额为 $29,132 million，且如果我们选择不展期，则直至 2027 年 8 月 28 日才需支付债务本金。截至 2026 年 3 月 31 日，我们的最低租赁付款总额为 $5,823 million，其中 $1,026 million 于本财年内到期。有关我们的债务和租赁义务的详情，请参阅本招股说明书其他部分所载我们经审计合并财务报表附注 10“债务”和附注 11“租赁”，以及我们未经审计合并财务报表附注 9“债务”。

paras.en: Summary of Cash flows
paras.zh: 现金流量摘要

paras.en: The following table summarizes our cash flows for the periods indicated:
paras.zh: 下表概述了所示期间我们的现金流量：

paras.en: **Three Months Ended March 31,**
paras.zh: **截至 3 月 31 日的三个月，**

paras.en: #### Operating Activities
paras.zh: #### 经营活动

paras.en: Net cash provided by operating activities increased by $320 million from $727 million during the three months endedMarch 31, 2025 to $1,047 million during the three months endedMarch 31, 2026. This increase was primarily driven by an increase in working capital for deferred revenue of $1,153 million from upfront payments from our Space and Connectivity customers, partially offset by lower net income exclusive of non-cash items.
paras.zh: 经营活动提供的现金净额从截至 2025 年 3 月 31 日止三个月的 $727 million 增加 $320 million，至截至 2026 年 3 月 31 日止三个月的 $1,047 million。该增加主要由于来自我们太空与连接业务客户预付款的递延收入营运资金增加 $1,153 million，部分被剔除非现金项目后的净利润下降所抵消。

paras.en: Net cash provided by operating activities increased by $1,009 million from $5,776 million during the year ended December 31, 2024 to $6,785 million during the year ended December 31, 2025. This increase was primarily driven by higher net income exclusive of non-cash items and an increase of $1,080 million for accounts payable and other liabilities as we continue to expand our infrastructure and timing of payments, and higher deferred revenue from cash received from upfront payments from our aviation customers. This increase was partially offset by $449 million for higher prepaid expenses and inventory.
paras.zh: 经营活动提供的现金净额从截至 2024 年 12 月 31 日止年度的 $5,776 million 增加 $1,009 million，至截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日止年度的 $6,785 million。该增加主要由于剔除非现金项目后的净利润上升，以及随着我们持续扩展基础设施和付款时间安排，应付账款及其他负债增加 $1,080 million，以及来自我们航空客户预付款所收现金的递延收入增加。该增加部分被预付费用和存货增加 $449 million 所抵消。

paras.en: Net cash provided by operating activities increased by $1,256 million from $4,520 million during the year ended December 31, 2023 to $5,776 million during the year ended December 31, 2024. This increase was primarily driven by higher net income exclusive of non-cash items, partially offset by $628 million for higher inventory and prepaid expenses and other assets due to increase in our revenue and production of Starlink Kits.
paras.zh: 经营活动提供的现金净额从截至 2023 年 12 月 31 日止年度的 $4,520 million 增加 $1,256 million，至截至 2024 年 12 月 31 日止年度的 $5,776 million。该增加主要由于剔除非现金项目后的净利润上升，部分被因我们收入增长和 Starlink Kits 生产而增加的存货、预付费用及其他资产 $628 million 所抵消。

paras.en: #### Investing Activities
paras.zh: #### 投资活动

paras.en: Net cash used in investing activities increased by $12,554 million from $4,170 million during the three months endedMarch 31, 2025 to $16,724 million during the three months endedMarch 31, 2026. This increase was primarily driven by an increase in capital expenditures of $5,967 million related to the build out of data centers and related infrastructure, and space launch facilities and related infrastructure, as well as an increase in purchases of marketable securities of $7,489 million in the period. This increase was partially offset by an increase in cash received from product rebates of $1,195 million.
paras.zh: 投资活动所用现金净额增加 $12,554 百万，由截至 2025 年 3 月 31 日止三个月的 $4,170 百万增至截至 2026 年 3 月 31 日止三个月的 $16,724 百万。该增加主要由于与数据中心及相关基础设施、以及航天发射设施及相关基础设施的建设相关的资本支出增加 $5,967 百万，以及本期购买有价证券增加 $7,489 百万。该增加部分被产品返利收到的现金增加 $1,195 百万所抵销。

paras.en: Net cash used in investing activities increased by $8,779 million from $10,796 million during the year ended December 31, 2024 to $19,575 million during the year ended December 31, 2025. This increase was primarily driven by an increase in capital expenditures of $9,574 million related to the build out of data centers and related infrastructure, and space launch facilities and related infrastructure, partially offset by a net increase in cash received from marketable securities of $1,264 million.
paras.zh: 投资活动所用现金净额增加 $8,779 百万，由截至 2024 年 12 月 31 日止年度的 $10,796 百万增至截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日止年度的 $19,575 百万。该增加主要由于与数据中心及相关基础设施、以及航天发射设施及相关基础设施的建设相关的资本支出增加 $9,574 百万，部分被有价证券收到的现金净增加 $1,264 百万所抵销。

paras.en: Net cash used in investing activities increased by $5,929 million from $4,867 million during the year ended December 31, 2023 to $10,796 million during the year ended December 31, 2024. This increase was primarily driven by an increase in capital expenditures of $6,748 million related to the build out of data centers and related infrastructure, and space launch facilities and related infrastructure, partially offset by an increase in cash received for the maturities of marketable securities of $981 million.
paras.zh: 投资活动所用现金净额增加 $5,929 百万，由截至 2023 年 12 月 31 日止年度的 $4,867 百万增至截至 2024 年 12 月 31 日止年度的 $10,796 百万。该增加主要由于与数据中心及相关基础设施、以及航天发射设施及相关基础设施的建设相关的资本支出增加 $6,748 百万，部分被有价证券到期收到的现金增加 $981 百万所抵销。

paras.en: #### Financing Activities
paras.zh: #### 融资活动

paras.en: Net cash provided by financing activities increased by $6,771 million from $354 million during the three months endedMarch 31, 2025 to $7,125 million during the three months endedMarch 31, 2026. This increase was primarily driven by an increase in proceeds from the SpaceX Bridge Loan and other financing arrangements of $17,950 million and proceeds from sale of our capital stock of $7,420 million, partially offset by an increase in payment on existing debt obligations and debt extinguishment costs of $14,703 million from the proceeds from the SpaceX Bridge Loan as well as an increase in repurchases of our capital stock of $3,838 million following the xAI Merger.
paras.zh: 融资活动提供的现金净额增加 $6,771 百万，由截至 2025 年 3 月 31 日止三个月的 $354 百万增至截至 2026 年 3 月 31 日止三个月的 $7,125 百万。该增加主要由于 SpaceX 过桥贷款及其他融资安排所得款项增加 $17,950 百万以及出售我们股本所得款项 $7,420 百万，部分被以下各项所抵销：以 SpaceX 过桥贷款所得款项偿付现有债务义务及债务清偿成本的付款增加 $14,703 百万，以及 xAI 合并后我们股本回购增加 $3,838 百万。

paras.en: Net cash provided by financing activities increased by $14,520 million from $11,830 million during the year ended December 31, 2024 to $26,350 million during the year ended December 31, 2025. This increase was primarily driven by an increase in proceeds from debt and other financing arrangements for our AI segment of $16,055 million and proceeds from sale of our capital stock of $5,706 million, partially offset by an increase in repayments on debt and other financing arrangements for our AI segment of $6,781 million.
paras.zh: 融资活动提供的现金净额增加 $14,520 百万，由截至 2024 年 12 月 31 日止年度的 $11,830 百万增至截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日止年度的 $26,350 百万。该增加主要由于我们 AI 分部的债务及其他融资安排所得款项增加 $16,055 百万以及出售我们股本所得款项 $5,706 百万，部分被我们 AI 分部的债务及其他融资安排还款增加 $6,781 百万所抵销。

paras.en: Net cash provided by financing activities increased by $11,408 million from $422 million during the year ended December 31, 2023 to $11,830 million during the year ended December 31, 2024. This increase was primarily driven by an increase in proceeds from the sale of our capital stock of $12,327 million, partially offset by an increase in the buyback of common and preferred shares by the Company of $104 million.
paras.zh: 融资活动提供的现金净额增加 $11,408 百万，由截至 2023 年 12 月 31 日止年度的 $422 百万增至截至 2024 年 12 月 31 日止年度的 $11,830 百万。该增加主要由于出售我们股本的所得款项增加 $12,327 百万，部分被公司回购普通股和优先股增加 $104 百万所抵销。

paras.en: The preparation of financial statements and related disclosures in conformity with GAAP and the Company’s discussion and analysis of its financial condition and operating results require the Company’s management to make judgments, assumptions and estimates that affect the amounts reported. Note 2, “Summary of Significant Accounting Policies” of the Notes to audited consolidated financial statements included elsewhere in this prospectus describes the significant accounting policies and methods used in the preparation of the Company’s consolidated financial statements. Management bases its estimates on historical experience and on various other assumptions it believes to be reasonable under the circumstances, the results of which form the basis for making judgments about the carrying values of assets and liabilities.
paras.zh: 按照 GAAP 编制财务报表及相关披露，以及公司对其财务状况和经营成果的讨论与分析，均要求公司管理层作出影响所报告金额的判断、假设和估计。本招股说明书其他部分所载经审计合并财务报表附注中的附注 2“重要会计政策摘要”描述了编制公司合并财务报表时所采用的重要会计政策和方法。管理层基于历史经验及其认为在相关情况下合理的各项其他假设作出估计，这些估计的结果构成对资产和负债账面价值作出判断的基础。

paras.en: #### Revenue Recognition
paras.zh: #### 收入确认

paras.en: Space contract revenue is derived from fixed-price contracts related to the development and provision of launch services for the deployment of spacecraft and other payloads to their intended orbit for both commercial customers and governmental agency space programs. Connectivity contract revenue for Starshield customers is mostly derived from fixed-price contracts related to the development of a secure satellite network designed specifically for government and national security applications.
paras.zh: 太空合同收入来自固定价格合同，涉及为商业客户和政府机构太空项目开发和提供发射服务，将航天器及其他有效载荷部署至预定轨道。Starshield 客户的连接合同收入主要来自固定价格合同，涉及开发专为政府及国家安全应用设计的安全卫星网络。

paras.en: The Company recognizes revenue over time when the Company’s performance on the contract creates an asset with no alternative use and when the Company has an enforceable right to payment for performance to date. The Company measures progress on these contracts using the cost-to-cost input method, as the Company believes this represents the most appropriate measure towards satisfaction of its performance obligation. Under the cost-to-cost input method, the Company records revenue based upon costs (such as materials and labor hours) incurred to date relative to the total estimated cost at completion.
paras.zh: 当公司在合同上的履约行为形成一项无替代用途的资产，且公司对迄今已完成的履约享有可强制执行收款权利时，公司在一段时间内确认收入。公司采用成本对成本投入法计量这些合同的履约进度，因为公司认为这是衡量履约义务完成情况的最适当方法。在成本对成本投入法下，公司根据迄今已发生的成本（如材料和人工工时）相对于预计完工总成本确认收入。

paras.en: The Company’s contracts recognized over time using the cost-to-cost input method are complex and require the Company to estimate the total costs to perform over the term of the contracts, as well as the measurement of progress towards completion for each performance obligation. For Space contracts, developing the estimated total cost at completion for each performance obligation requires the use of significant management judgment, including assumptions regarding launch timing, labor hours, allocation of shared costs for launch vehicles that have been identified as reusable for multiple launches, as well as expected technological changes to launch vehicles and spacecraft. For Connectivity contracts, developing the estimated total cost at completion for each performance obligation requires the use of significant management judgment, including assumptions regarding labor hours, allocation of shared costs used in the production of satellites, satellite material costs, as well as expected technological changes to satellites. Material changes in estimated contract revenue or costs at completion and the resulting changes in contract profit could have a material impact on the Company’s financial condition and operating results.
paras.zh: 公司采用成本对成本投入法在一段时间内确认收入的合同较为复杂，要求公司估计合同期内履行合同的全部成本，并计量每项履约义务的完工进度。对于太空合同，确定每项履约义务的预计完工总成本需要管理层作出重大判断，包括关于发射时间、人工工时、已被确定为可多次发射重复使用的运载火箭共享成本分摊的假设，以及运载火箭和航天器预期技术变化的假设。对于连接合同，确定每项履约义务的预计完工总成本需要管理层作出重大判断，包括关于人工工时、卫星生产中使用的共享成本分摊、卫星材料成本的假设，以及卫星预期技术变化的假设。预计合同收入或完工成本的重大变化以及由此导致的合同利润变化，可能对公司的财务状况和经营成果产生重大影响。

paras.en: The impact of net adjustments from contracts recognized over time using the cost-to-cost input method to our revenue and operating income was not material for the years ended December 31, 2025, 2024, and 2023 and for the three months ended March 31, 2026. If the combined gross margins for our contracts recognized over time using the cost-to-cost input method had been estimated to be higher or lower by 1% during 2025, it would have increased or decreased operating income for the year by approximately $110 million.
paras.zh: 对于截至 2025 年、2024 年和 2023 年 12 月 31 日的年度以及截至 2026 年 3 月 31 日的三个月，采用成本比例投入法按时间确认的合同所产生的净调整对我们的收入和经营利润的影响并不重大。如果在 2025 年期间，我们采用成本比例投入法按时间确认的合同的综合毛利率被估计为高出或低出 1%，则会使该年度的经营利润增加或减少约$110 million。

paras.en: #### Property, Plant, and Equipment, Net
paras.zh: #### 物业、厂房及设备，净额

paras.en: Property, plant, and equipment, net is stated at cost less accumulated depreciation. The Company depreciates these assets primarily using the straight-line method over the estimated useful lives of the assets except flight vehicles and spacecraft, which are depreciated over the expected number of average flights for each flight vehicle and spacecraft. Leasehold improvements are depreciated over the shorter of their estimated useful lives or the related lease term.
paras.zh: 物业、厂房及设备，净额按成本减累计折旧列示。公司主要采用直线法在资产的估计使用寿命内计提折旧，但飞行器和航天器除外，其按每架飞行器和航天器的预期平均飞行次数计提折旧。租赁改良按估计使用寿命或相关租赁期中较短者计提折旧。

paras.en: Determining the useful lives and the number of average flights a flight vehicle and spacecraft can fly require the Company to estimate the period over which we expect to recover the economic value of our property, plant, and equipment. For each of our flight vehicle hardware and spacecraft, we consider recovery and refurbishment success rates, refurbishment economics, customer acceptance limits that may prohibit the use of vehicles that have been flown more than a certain number of launches, expected future launches included in the mission manifest, as well as any anticipated retirement timing of certain flight vehicle and spacecraft models such as Falcon as a result of anticipated transition to Starship to determine the expected number of average flights for each vehicle.
paras.zh: 确定飞行器和航天器的使用寿命及平均飞行次数需要公司估计预期收回物业、厂房及设备经济价值的期间。对于我们的每项飞行器硬件和航天器，我们考虑回收和翻新成功率、翻新经济性、可能禁止使用已飞行超过一定发射次数的飞行器的客户接受限制、任务清单中包含的预期未来发射，以及因预期向 Starship 过渡而导致的某些飞行器和航天器型号（如 Falcon）的任何预期退役时间，以确定每架飞行器的预期平均飞行次数。

paras.en: For our satellites assets, we consider factors such as on-orbit performance, orbit-raise timing, expected service capability, and the evolution of constellation density and technology.
paras.zh: 对于我们的卫星资产，我们考虑在轨性能、升轨时间、预期服务能力以及星座密度和技术的演变等因素。

paras.en: When we determine that the useful lives or expected remaining flights of assets are shorter or longer than we had originally estimated, we adjust the rate of depreciation to reflect the assets' revised useful lives or number of remaining flights.
paras.zh: 当我们确定资产的使用寿命或预期剩余飞行次数短于或长于我们最初的估计时，我们调整折旧率以反映资产修订后的使用寿命或剩余飞行次数。

paras.en: The Company periodically evaluates impairment of its property, plant, and equipment assets whenever events or circumstances indicate that the carrying value of an asset or asset group may not be recoverable. Factors we consider to identify indicators of potential impairment include significant changes or planned changes in our use of certain property, plant and equipment, technological developments that reduce the utility of the existing assets, declines in forecasted cash flows, and significant negative industry or economic trends.
paras.zh: 每当事件或情况表明某项资产或资产组的账面价值可能无法收回时，公司会定期评估其物业、厂房及设备资产的减值。我们用于识别潜在减值迹象的因素包括我们对某些物业、厂房及设备的使用发生重大变化或计划变化、降低现有资产效用的技术发展、预测现金流下降以及重大不利的行业或经济趋势。

paras.en: Impairment is assessed at the lowest level for which identifiable cash flows are largely independent of the cash flows of other assets and liabilities. If estimated future cash flows are less than the carrying value of the asset or asset group, an impairment charge is recognized to the extent its carrying value exceeds its estimated fair value to cost of revenue or selling, general, and administrative expenses depending on the nature of the assets, or to impairment charges if the impairment is considered to be outside the normal course of business. For the years ended December 31, 2025, 2024, and 2023, and for the three months ended March 31, 2026, impairments on fixed assets were not material.
paras.zh: 减值在可辨认现金流量在很大程度上独立于其他资产和负债现金流量的最低层级进行评估。如果估计的未来现金流量低于资产或资产组的账面价值，则在其账面价值超过估计公允价值的范围内确认减值费用，计入营业成本或销售、一般及管理费用（取决于资产的性质），或者如果该减值被视为不属于正常经营过程，则计入减值费用。截至 2025 年、2024 年和 2023 年 12 月 31 日止年度以及截至 2026 年 3 月 31 日止三个月，固定资产减值并不重大。

paras.en: If the average remaining flights for our flight vehicle and spacecraft had been estimated to be five more or fewer flights, the impact to our operating income for the year ended December 31, 2025 and three months ended March 31, 2026 would not be material. If the average useful life of our satellite assets had been changed by one year, it would have an approximately $480 million and $170 million impact on our operating income for the year ended December 31, 2025 and three months ended March 31, 2026, respectively.
paras.zh: 如果我们的飞行器和航天器的平均剩余飞行次数被估计为增加或减少五次，则对截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日止年度和截至 2026 年 3 月 31 日止三个月的经营利润的影响将不重大。如果我们的卫星资产的平均使用寿命变动一年，则将对截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日止年度和截至 2026 年 3 月 31 日止三个月的经营利润分别产生约 $480 million 和 $170 million 的影响。

paras.en: #### Legal and Other Contingencies
paras.zh: #### 法律及其他或有事项

paras.en: The Company is subject to various legal proceedings and claims that arise in the ordinary course of business, the outcomes of which are inherently uncertain. The Company records a liability when it is probable a loss has been incurred and the amount is reasonably estimable, the determination of which requires significant judgment. Resolution of legal matters in a manner inconsistent with management’s expectations could have a material impact on the Company’s financial condition and operating results.
paras.zh: 公司面临在正常经营过程中产生的各种法律诉讼和索赔，其结果本质上具有不确定性。当很可能已发生损失且金额能够合理估计时，公司确认负债，该确定需要作出重大判断。法律事项的解决方式若与管理层的预期不一致，可能对公司的财务状况和经营成果产生重大影响。

paras.en: Refer toNote 2, Summary of Significant Accounting Policies, to the audited consolidated financial statements included elsewhere in this prospectus.
paras.zh: 请参阅本招股说明书其他部分所载经审计合并财务报表中的附注 2“重要会计政策摘要”。

full.sec: Quantitative and Qualitative Disclosures About Market Risk
full.secZh: 关于市场风险的定量与定性披露

paras.en: #### Foreign Currency Risk
paras.zh: #### 外币风险

paras.en: Our Connectivity and AI businesses operate in many countries and transact in multiple currencies. In general, we are a net receiver of currencies other than the U.S. dollar for our foreign subsidiaries. Accordingly, we are exposed to foreign currency risk both from fluctuations in exchange rates affecting foreign-currency denominated transactions and from the impact of translating the assets, liabilities, revenues, costs of revenue, and other operating expenses of our foreign subsidiaries into U.S. dollars. We have experienced, and will continue to experience, fluctuations in our net income as a result of gains (losses) on the settlement and the re-measurement of monetary assets and liabilities not denominated in our functional currencies. We do not hedge foreign currency risk and changes in exchange rates could have an adverse impact on our operating results and cash flows.
paras.zh: 我们的互联业务和 AI 业务在多个国家运营，并以多种货币进行交易。总体而言，就我们的境外子公司而言，我们是美元以外货币的净接收方。因此，我们面临的外币风险既来自影响外币计价交易的汇率波动，也来自将境外子公司的资产、负债、收入、收入成本及其他经营费用折算为美元所产生的影响。我们已经并将继续因非以功能货币计价的货币性资产和负债的结算与重新计量所产生的收益（亏损）而经历净收入的波动。我们未对外币风险进行对冲，汇率变动可能对我们的经营业绩和现金流量产生不利影响。

paras.en: We considered the historical trends in foreign currency exchange rates and determined that it is reasonably possible that adverse changes in foreign currency exchange rates of 10% for all currencies could be experienced in the near-term. These changes were applied to our total monetary assets and liabilities denominated in our non-functional currencies at the balance sheet date to compute the impact these changes would have had on our income (loss) before income taxes. These changes would have resulted in an immaterial gain or lossas of March 31, 2026 and December 31, 2025, respectively.
paras.zh: 我们考虑了外币汇率的历史趋势，并判断在近期内，所有货币的外币汇率出现 10% 的不利变动是合理可能的。这些变动已应用于我们在资产负债表日以非功能货币计价的货币性资产和负债总额，以计算这些变动本应对我们的所得税前利润（亏损）产生的影响。截至 2026 年 3 月 31 日和 2025 年 12 月 31 日，这些变动本应分别导致不重大的收益或亏损。

paras.en: #### Interest Rate Risk
paras.zh: #### 利率风险

paras.en: Our exposure to changes in interest rates relates primarily to our investment portfolio, interest income on cash and cash equivalents and our credit facilities.
paras.zh: 我们对利率变动的敞口主要与我们的投资组合、现金及现金等价物的利息收入以及我们的信贷融资有关。

paras.en: Our cash and cash equivalents consist of cash, time deposits, money market funds, U.S. government and agency securities. Our investment policy and strategy are focused on preservation of capital and supporting our liquidity requirements. Changes in U.S. interest rates affect the interest earned on our cash and cash equivalents. A hypothetical 100 basis point increase or decrease in market interest rates would have resulted in an immaterial increase or decrease in interest income for the year ended December 31, 2025 and three months ended March 31, 2026.
paras.zh: 我们的现金及现金等价物包括现金、定期存款、货币市场基金、美国政府及机构证券。我们的投资政策和策略侧重于保全资本并支持我们的流动性需求。美国利率的变动会影响我们现金及现金等价物所赚取的利息。市场利率假设性上升或下降 100 个基点，本应导致截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日止年度和截至 2026 年 3 月 31 日止三个月的利息收入出现不重大的增加或减少。

paras.en: The effective interest rate on outstanding borrowings under the SpaceX Bridge Loan was 4.58% as of March 31, 2026. A hypothetical 100 basis point increase in U.S. interest rates would increase annual interest expense by approximately $200 million.
paras.zh: 截至 2026 年 3 月 31 日，SpaceX 过桥贷款项下未偿还借款的实际利率为 4.58%。美国利率假设性上升 100 个基点，将使年度利息费用增加约 $200 million。

paras.en: “You want to wake up in the morning and think the future is going to be great— and that’s what being a space-faring civilization is all about. It’s about believing in the future and thinking that the future will be better than the past. And I can’t think of anything more exciting than going out there and being among the stars.”
paras.zh: “你希望早晨醒来时觉得未来会很美好——而这就是成为一个太空文明的全部意义所在。它关乎对未来的信念，关乎认为未来会比过去更好。我想不出还有什么比走出去、置身群星之间更令人兴奋的事了。”

paras.en: — Elon Musk
paras.zh: —— Elon Musk

paras.en: Our mission is to build the systems and technologies necessary to make life multiplanetary, to understand the true nature of the universe, and to extend the light of consciousness to the stars. To do this, we have formed the most ambitious, vertically integrated innovation engine on (and off) Earth with unmatched capabilities to rapidly manufacture and launch space-based communications that connect the world, to harness the Sun to power a truth-seeking artificial intelligence that advances scientific discovery, and ultimately to build a base on the Moon and cities on other planets.
paras.zh: 我们的使命是构建必要的系统与技术，使生命得以在多行星间延续，理解宇宙的真正本质，并将意识之光延伸至群星。为此，我们在地球上（以及地球之外）打造了最具雄心的垂直整合创新引擎，具备无可匹敌的能力，能够快速制造并发射连接世界的天基通信系统，驾驭太阳能为追求真理、推动科学发现的人工智能提供动力，并最终在月球建立基地、在其他行星上建设城市。

paras.en: Founded in 2002, SpaceX is the only company building the integrated hardware and software infrastructure of the future across space, connectivity, and AI. At our core, we are builders. We design, manufacture, launch, and operate products and services built on cutting-edge technologies, including the world’s most advanced rockets and spacecraft. We safely and reliably transport astronauts, satellites, and other payloads on missions that benefit life on Earth. Since 2023, we have launched more than 80% of mass to orbit for the world each year with an over 99% mission success rate with Falcon rockets. We also operate a high-speed, low-latency global broadband data and communications network powered by approximately 9,600 Starlink broadband and mobile satellites in Low-Earth Orbit, delivering connectivity to million s of consumer, enterprise, and government customers across 164 countries, territories, and other markets, as of March 31, 2026. Using our dedicated satellite-to-mobile constellation, we offer connectivity services, supplementing terrestrial networks and substantially reducing mobile “dead zones” across approximately 30 countries.
paras.zh: SpaceX 成立于 2002 年，是唯一一家在太空、连接和 AI 领域构建未来软硬件一体化基础设施的公司。我们的核心是建设者。我们设计、制造、发射和运营基于前沿技术的产品与服务，包括全球最先进的火箭和航天器。我们安全可靠地运送宇航员、卫星及其他有效载荷，执行造福地球生命的任务。自 2023 年以来，我们每年以 Falcon 火箭为全球发射了超过 80% 的入轨质量，任务成功率超过 99%。我们还运营一个高速、低延迟的全球宽带数据与通信网络，由约 9,600 颗低地球轨道上的 Starlink 宽带和移动卫星提供支持，截至 2026 年 3 月 31 日，为 164 个国家、地区及其他市场的数百万消费者、企业和政府客户提供连接。利用我们专用的卫星直连移动星座，我们提供连接服务，补充地面网络，并大幅减少约 30 个国家的移动“盲区”。

paras.en: With the potential to improve both space exploration and life on Earth, AI accelerates SpaceX’s mission to make life multiplanetary, to understand the true nature of the universe, and to extend the light of consciousness to the stars. xAI, which was founded in 2023 and acquired by SpaceX in early 2026, is now an integral pillar of our vertically integrated company. We are rapidly constructing AI compute infrastructure—starting on Earth with the goal of extending to space—at industry-leading pace and cost efficiency. Our infrastructure supports training and inference for Grok, which has emerged as one of the world’s most advanced frontier models. Grok is designed as a truth-seeking AI model, built on our founder Elon Musk’s mission to enable humanity to understand the universe. We believe that accomplishing this mission requires a truth-seeking approach to AI. We define truth seeking as the active, relentless pursuit of what is objectively true about reality, and grounded in evidence, logic, empirical data, and first principles thinking. Our goal is to understand and explain what the universe appears to be doing, as accurately as current knowledge allows. Within two years of its initial model release, Grok achieved frontier-level performance in scientific reasoning, as measured by its GPQA Diamond score, an industry benchmark that evaluates AI models on a standardized set of questions written and validated by experts, on a faster timeline than reported by other leading model providers. Grok also benefits from integration with X, our real-time information, entertainment, and free speech platform, which serves as a foundational distribution and data engine for our AI ecosystem and further enhances Grok’s truth-seeking objective.
paras.zh: AI 具有改善太空探索和地球生命的潜力，加速了 SpaceX 的使命——让生命多行星化、理解宇宙的真正本质，并将意识之光延伸至星辰。xAI 成立于 2023 年，于 2026 年初被 SpaceX 收购，现已成为我们垂直整合公司不可或缺的支柱。我们正以行业领先的速度和成本效率快速构建 AI 算力基础设施——从地球起步，目标是延伸至太空。我们的基础设施支持 Grok 的训练和推理，Grok 已成为全球最先进的前沿模型之一。Grok 被设计为一个追求真相的 AI 模型，建立在我们的创始人 Elon Musk 的使命之上，即让人类理解宇宙。我们相信，实现这一使命需要对 AI 采取追求真相的方法。我们将追求真相定义为积极、不懈地追求关于现实的客观真实，并以证据、逻辑、经验数据和第一性原理思维为基础。我们的目标是，在现有知识允许的范围内，尽可能准确地理解和解释宇宙似乎正在做的事情。在其初始模型发布后的两年内，Grok 在科学推理方面达到了前沿水平，以 GPQA Diamond 分数衡量——这是一项行业基准，通过一组由专家编写和验证的标准化问题来评估 AI 模型——其时间线快于其他领先模型提供商所报告的。Grok 还得益于与 X 的整合，X 是我们的实时信息、娱乐和言论自由平台，作为我们 AI 生态系统的基础分发和数据引擎，并进一步增强 Grok 的追求真相目标。

paras.en: We believe that space represents the largest economic frontier in human history, unlocking unprecedented opportunities in orbit and on Earth. Earth has limits, so we must build infrastructure and industries in space, expanding human capabilities to improve life on Earth and to establish life beyond. Connectivity infrastructure in space is designed to help everyone on Earth have access to education, healthcare, entertainment, and communications, and to enable people to overcome many traditional limits, such as physical and political borders. We believe AI infrastructure in space can utilize the virtually limitless power of the Sun and thereby enable the use of AI as a transformative force for understanding the universe and improving the daily lives of all humans. We believe the convergence of these areas will enable an unprecedented expansion in the global economy, leading to an age of abundance. Our innovations and technological advancements are redefining industries on Earth, while we aim to create new ones on the Moon, Mars, and beyond. We are truly building the infrastructure of the future.
paras.zh: 我们相信，太空代表着人类历史上最大的经济前沿，在轨道上和地球上释放出前所未有的机遇。地球有其极限，因此我们必须在太空中建设基础设施和产业，拓展人类的能力，以改善地球上的生活，并在地球之外建立生命。太空中的连接基础设施旨在帮助地球上的每个人都能获得教育、医疗、娱乐和通信，并使人们能够克服许多传统限制，例如物理边界和政治边界。我们相信，太空中的 AI 基础设施可以利用几乎无限的太阳能，从而使 AI 成为理解宇宙和改善全人类日常生活的变革性力量。我们相信，这些领域的融合将推动全球经济实现前所未有的扩张，引领一个富足时代。我们的创新和技术进步正在重新定义地球上的各个行业，同时我们的目标是在月球、火星及更远的地方创造新的行业。我们正在真正建设未来的基础设施。

paras.en: SpaceX is the only company that has cracked the code on accessing space at scale, revolutionizing an industry characterized by decades of stagnation, risk aversion, and economically perverse cost structures. SpaceX upended this paradigm through the application of first-principles thinking, which rejects industry assumptions and builds solutions based on the fundamental laws of physics. Our intense, mission-driven, engineering-first culture and focus on extreme vertical integration have propelled us to achieve what many deemed impossible. We have demonstrated the ability to achieve groundbreaking technological innovations with speed, quality control, and precision. We pioneered high-cadence, reliable, and affordable access to space with our Falcon family of rockets, with a goal to transform the rocket launch industry into airline-like operations. In 2015, we established at least a 10-year lead over the industry by successfully landing our first Falcon 9 booster back from space before anyone else. We have continued to invest significantly in further increasing our lead by pursuing full and rapid reusability at scale, including investing over $15 billion in our next-generation rocket, Starship.
paras.zh: SpaceX 是唯一一家破解了规模化进入太空难题的公司，彻底改变了一个数十年来停滞不前、规避风险且成本结构在经济上不合理的行业。SpaceX 通过运用第一性原理思维颠覆了这一范式，这种思维拒绝行业假设，并基于物理学的基本定律构建解决方案。我们强烈的、以使命为驱动、工程优先的文化以及对极致垂直整合的专注，推动我们实现了许多人认为不可能的事情。我们已经展示了以速度、质量控制和精度实现突破性技术创新的能力。我们通过猎鹰系列火箭开创了高频率、可靠且可负担的太空进入方式，目标是推动火箭发射行业转型为类似航空公司的运营模式。2015 年，我们成功将首枚猎鹰 9 号助推器从太空回收着陆，领先其他任何人，从而确立了相对于行业至少 10 年的领先优势。我们持续大举投资以进一步扩大领先优势，追求规模化全面快速可重复使用，包括在我们的下一代火箭 Starship 上投资超过 $15 billion。

paras.en: We believe rocket launches and landings should be as routine and commonplace as airplanes taking off and landing. To achieve this sort of cadence, our iterative approach emphasizes rapid designing, testing, and process optimization, putting flight hardware in the flight environment as often as possible. This allows us to accelerate our learning by repeatedly using and improving our systems. This has resulted in a significantly higher flight rate at costs that are much lower than launch programs that existed before SpaceX. For example, according to NASA, the first version of Falcon 9 in 2010 had a launch cost of approximately $2,700 per kilogram, which represented a reduction of approximately 85% compared to the historical average launch cost per kilogram of $18,500. The first version of Falcon Heavy in 2018 further reduced this cost to approximately $1,400 per kilogram, a reduction of approximately 92% compared to the historical average cost. With the future deployment of Starship, which is designed to be the world’s first fully and rapidly reusable spacecraft, we aim to further reduce the cost to reach orbit by 99% or more relative to the historical average launch cost. Central to our cost advantage is the reusability of key hardware—most notably boosters—which we recover, refurbish, and refly many times instead of discarding after single use. This dramatically lowers per-launch costs by minimizing hardware replacement expenses and spreading fixed production costs across repeated uses. Space flight that historically cost billion s per launch now costs in the tens of million s, fundamentally reducing the cost of space access, providing the opportunity to build new enterprises in space.
paras.zh: 我们认为火箭发射和着陆应当像飞机起降一样常规和普遍。为实现这种节奏，我们的迭代方法强调快速设计、测试和流程优化，尽可能频繁地将飞行硬件置于飞行环境中。这使我们能够通过反复使用和改进系统来加速学习。由此，我们实现了显著更高的飞行频率，且成本远低于 SpaceX 之前存在的发射项目。例如，根据 NASA 的数据，2010 年第一版 Falcon 9 的发射成本约为每公斤$2,700，相比历史平均每公斤发射成本$18,500 降低了约 85%。2018 年第一版 Falcon Heavy 进一步将这一成本降至约每公斤$1,400，相比历史平均成本降低了约 92%。随着未来 Starship 的部署——其设计目标是成为世界上首个完全且快速可重复使用的航天器——我们的目标是将入轨成本相对于历史平均发射成本进一步降低 99%或更多。我们成本优势的核心在于关键硬件的可重复使用性——最显著的是助推器——我们将其回收、翻新并多次复飞，而不是单次使用后丢弃。通过最大限度地减少硬件更换费用并将固定生产成本分摊到多次使用中，这大幅降低了每次发射的成本。历史上每次发射耗资数十亿美元的太空飞行现在仅需数千万美元，从根本上降低了太空进入成本，为在太空中建立新企业提供了机会。

paras.en: Similarly, xAI has cracked the code in the complexities of building and scaling AI compute infrastructure, becoming the first company to deploy a coherent gigawatt-scale AI training cluster. We believe the combination of our proprietary AI infrastructure capability, our truth-seeking frontier model, Grok, and our access to real-time data on X creates a formidable competitive advantage, allowing us to maintain a leading position in the development of advanced artificial intelligence. This advantage stems from our complete vertical integration and the common vision infused by our founder, Elon Musk. In just a few years, we have demonstrated an ability to build coherent compute at scale and rapid speed with lower cost. COLOSSUS and COLOSSUS II collectively provide approximately 1.0 gigawatt of compute power, with additional power capacity available for data center operations. We believe speed is a competitive advantage. In order to bring compute clusters online as fast as possible, we employ a vertically integrated, nimble approach to construction. At COLOSSUS, we brought online the first cluster of approximately 100,000 H100 processors, approximately 130 megawatts of compute power, in just 122 days, repurposing the shell of an existing factory. At COLOSSUS II, we brought online the first cluster of approximately 110,000 GB200 processors, approximately 210 megawatts of compute power, even faster in 91 days. As an illustrative comparison, an industry benchmark to bring online a 100 megawatt greenfield data center is approximately two years. Furthermore, in the case of COLOSSUS II, following the initial cluster, we brought online the second cluster of 110,000 GB300 processors and 220 megawatts of compute power in 64 days, demonstrating our ability to rapidly scale our facilities once built. We expect that once fully operational, the next phase of expansion at COLOSSUS II will bring online at least 220,000 additional GB300 processors and over 400 additional megawatts of compute power. We also demonstrated asignificant improvement in cost efficiency, achieving data center construction costs for COLOSSUS II that are considerably lower than industry benchmarks on a per megawatt basis.
paras.zh: 同样，xAI 已攻克了构建和扩展 AI 算力基础设施的复杂难题，成为首家部署连贯的吉瓦级 AI 训练集群的公司。我们相信，我们专有的 AI 基础设施能力、我们追求真相的前沿模型 Grok，以及我们对 X 上实时数据的访问权限，三者结合创造了强大的竞争优势，使我们能够在先进人工智能的开发中保持领先地位。这一优势源于我们完全的垂直整合以及我们的创始人 Elon Musk 所注入的共同愿景。在短短几年内，我们已经展示了以更低成本、大规模、快速构建连贯算力的能力。COLOSSUS 和 COLOSSUS II 合计提供约 1.0 吉瓦的算力，另有额外电力容量可用于数据中心运营。我们相信速度是一种竞争优势。为了尽快让算力集群上线，我们采用垂直整合、灵活敏捷的建设方式。在 COLOSSUS，我们在短短 122 天内让首个约 100,000 块 H100 处理器、约 130 兆瓦算力的集群上线，并改造利用了现有工厂的外壳。在 COLOSSUS II，我们在更快的 91 天内让首个约 110,000 块 GB200 处理器、约 210 兆瓦算力的集群上线。作为说明性对比，让一个 100 兆瓦的新建数据中心上线的行业基准约为两年。此外，在 COLOSSUS II 的案例中，在首个集群之后，我们在 64 天内让第二个由 110,000 块 GB300 处理器和 220 兆瓦算力组成的集群上线，展示了我们一旦建成即可快速扩展设施的能力。我们预计，一旦全面投入运营，COLOSSUS II 的下一阶段扩建将新增至少 220,000 块 GB300 处理器和超过 400 兆瓦的算力。我们还展示了成本效率的显著提升，COLOSSUS II 的数据中心建设成本按每兆瓦计算大幅低于行业基准。

paras.en: We are able to deploy power and compute significantly faster than other AI companies through first-principles thinking, behind-the-meter power generation, coupled with what we believe is the world’s largest network of sustainable battery storage systems, and innovations in advanced liquid cooling, high-density rack layouts, and efficient networking. Our facilities also incorporate innovative design features that limit the effects on regional electricity pricing for neighbors and include advanced water cleaning, reclamation, and recycling processes to support sustainable operations. We partner with utilities and communities to connect to and enhance the grid over time, and do so while pledging to cover costs of all new power delivery infrastructure upgrades to service our data centers, including adequate network upgrade costs, to ensure that these expenses are not passed on to the ordinary household. Our ability to rapidly and cost-effectively scale with the latest processors keeps us ahead of competitors who deploy traditional and more expensive methods. As a result, we believe COLOSSUS II became one of the world’s first data centers to deploy GB200s and GB300s, the most advanced AI processors available at the time, at significant scale, and is currently powering training for our next frontier models, including Grok-5. Furthermore, through our Terafab initiative together with Tesla to build a manufacturing facility capable of producing 1 terawatt per year of compute hardware, we intend to further extend our vertical integration to chip design and manufacturing to alleviate potential future chip shortages at SpaceX, optimize compute performance, and potentially reduce overall compute costs. Intel, which has the ability to design, fabricate, and package ultra-high-performance chips at scale, also joined the Terafab project in early April 2026. Our shovels-to-tokens approach allows us to train and iterate our frontier models at high velocity, accelerating development cycles, eliminating external bottlenecks, and driving rapid, continuous improvements in model performance.
