paras.en: We believe our compute infrastructure and related strategy provides us with substantial flexibility in how we allocate and monetize capacity. We have the ability to use compute resources to support our proprietary AI applications (such as Grok-5, which is currently being trained at COLOSSUS II), while also providing access to select compute capacity to third-party customers. For example, in May 2026, we entered into Cloud Services Agreements with Anthropic, an AI research and development public benefit corporation, with respect to access to compute capacity across COLOSSUS and COLOSSUS II. Compute capacity provided includes approximately 325,000 NVIDIA GPUs, backed by hyperscale-class CPUs, exabyte-scale storage and high-speed networking and interconnects purpose-built for AI workloads. Pursuant to these agreements, the customer has agreed to pay us $1.25 billion per month through May 2029, with capacity ramping in May and June 2026 at a reduced fee. After the initial three-month period, the agreements may be terminated by either party upon 90 days’ notice. The customer will retain ownership and intellectual property rights in its content, AI models, and related data. This structure allows us to monetize a portion of the compute capacity in our infrastructure, while still permitting reallocation of that capacity for our own internal initiatives if needed in the future. We have sufficient capacity to provide compute for our own AI models, including support of our training and inference demands, and to satisfy the obligations under these agreements. We expect to enter into additional similar services contracts for compute capacity with third parties. To the extent we become compute constrained due internal and external utilization, we would need to expand our compute infrastructure. We believe this opportunity highlights the increasing importance of large-scale, frontier-level AI infrastructure and positions us as a differentiated provider of high-performance compute capacity to both internal and third-party AI workloads. We believe our dual monetization strategy provides multiple pathways to generate returns on invested capital.
paras.zh: 我们认为，我们的算力基础设施及相关战略使我们在如何分配和变现算力方面具备极大的灵活性。我们既能够利用算力资源支持我们专有的 AI 应用（例如目前正在 COLOSSUS II 上训练的 Grok-5），同时也能够向第三方客户提供部分算力资源的使用权。例如，2026 年 5 月，我们与 Anthropic（一家 AI 研发公益公司）就使用 COLOSSUS 和 COLOSSUS II 的算力资源签订了云服务协议。所提供的算力包括约 325,000 块 NVIDIA GPU，并配备超大规模级 CPU、EB 级存储以及专为 AI 工作负载打造的高速网络和互连。根据该等协议，客户已同意在截至 2029 年 5 月期间每月向我们支付 $1.25 billion，其中 2026 年 5 月和 6 月的算力将按较低费用逐步提升。在最初三个月期限之后，任何一方均可提前 90 天通知终止该等协议。客户将保留其内容、AI 模型及相关数据的所有权和知识产权。这一结构使我们能够将基础设施中一部分算力变现，同时仍允许在未来有需要时将该部分算力重新分配用于我们自身的内部计划。我们拥有充足的算力，既能为自有 AI 模型提供算力（包括支持我们的训练和推理需求），也能履行该等协议项下的义务。我们预计将与第三方就算力签订更多类似的服务合同。若因内部和外部使用而导致我们的算力受限，我们将需要扩展算力基础设施。我们认为，这一机遇凸显了大规模、前沿级 AI 基础设施日益增长的重要性，并使我们在为内部和第三方 AI 工作负载提供高性能算力方面成为一家具有差异化优势的供应商。我们认为，我们的双变现战略提供了多条实现投资资本回报的路径。

paras.en: #### Our Repeatable Business Model
paras.zh: #### 我们可复制的商业模式

paras.en: Our business model is built on a repeatable, engineering-driven framework that combines our unparalleled launch capabilities, extreme vertical integration, rapid iteration, and disciplined capital investment to create durable, large-scale businesses. We execute this framework through the following core principles:
paras.zh: 我们的商业模式建立在一个可复制、以工程为驱动的框架之上，该框架将我们无与伦比的发射能力、极致的垂直整合、快速迭代和严谨的资本投资相结合，以打造持久的大规模业务。我们通过以下核心原则来执行这一框架：

paras.en: 1. Leverage our unparalleled launch capabilities to enable massive scale. Our rockets—with unmatched launch cadence, best-in-class reliability, and dramatically reduced cost-to-orbit—are the foundation that we expect will enable us to create economic opportunities in space and deliver a diversified portfolio of services. Our launch capabilities enable large-scale deployment of assets that would not otherwise be economically viable.
paras.zh: 1. 借助我们无与伦比的发射能力实现大规模部署。我们的火箭——凭借无可匹敌的发射频率、业界一流的可靠性以及大幅降低的入轨成本——是我们预期创造太空经济机遇并交付多元化服务组合的基础。我们的发射能力使原本在经济上不可行的大规模资产部署成为可能。

paras.en: 2. Identify and create new trillion-dollar market opportunities. We focus on market opportunities that are useful for humanity and that present trillion-dollar opportunities, including global broadband and mobile connectivity for consumers, enterprises, and governments; and AI applications and computational infrastructure. We prioritize opportunities where structural inefficiencies or legacy technological limitations have constrained supply.
paras.zh: 2. 识别并创造新的万亿美元市场机遇。我们专注于对人类有用且能带来万亿美元机遇的市场机会，包括面向消费者、企业和政府的全球宽带与移动连接；以及 AI 应用和算力基础设施。我们优先考虑那些因结构性低效或传统技术局限而制约供给的机遇。

paras.en: 3. Design a solution with world-class engineering and first-principles thinking. We apply physics-based engineering and first-principles thinking to design products and systems from the ground up—boiling things down to the most fundamental truths and reasoning up from there. This helps us drive massive, step-function improvements in performance, scalability, and cost.
paras.zh: 3. 以世界级工程能力和第一性原理思维设计解决方案。我们运用基于物理学的工程方法和第一性原理思维，从零开始设计产品和系统——将问题归结为最基本的真理，并由此向上推理。这帮助我们在性能、可扩展性和成本方面实现巨大的阶跃式提升。

paras.en: 4. Apply “The Algorithm” (make less dumb, delete, optimize, accelerate, automate). We operate under a set of core execution principles that we refer to as “The Algorithm,” a five-step iterative process that we use as our guiding principles day-to-day. We make the requirements less dumb, delete unnecessary processes or parts (embracing the principle that the best part is no part), only then optimize the necessary processes or parts, and then accelerate cycle time (many entities have launched once; no one other than us has ever launched over 100 times per year), and automate only proven processes after the first four steps are completed. We apply the Algorithm across every aspect of our organization, creating a cultural and operational standard of excellence that has defined SpaceX since inception.
paras.zh: 4. 应用“算法”（减少愚蠢、删除、优化、加速、自动化）。我们在一套核心执行原则下运营，我们称之为“算法”，这是一个五步迭代流程，我们将其作为日常工作的指导原则。我们让需求变得不那么愚蠢，删除不必要的流程或部件（秉持“最好的部件就是没有部件”这一原则），然后才优化必要的流程或部件，接着加速周期时间（许多实体只发射过一次；除我们之外，没有任何实体曾做到每年发射超过 100 次），并且仅在前四步完成后，才对经过验证的流程进行自动化。我们将“算法”应用于组织的方方面面，创造出一种自 SpaceX 成立以来便定义其卓越的文化和运营标准。

paras.en: 5. Vertically integrate all the way to the end customer. We design and manufacture a significant portion of our components in-house, including engines, avionics, structures, and software, even producing the “tools that make the tools,” enabling us to test, fail, and iterate rapidly. We can then release newer, more advanced hardware with speed and cost efficiency.
paras.zh: 5. 一路垂直整合至终端客户。我们在内部设计和制造相当大一部分组件，包括发动机、航空电子设备、结构和软件，甚至生产“制造工具的工具”，使我们能够快速测试、失败和迭代。随后，我们能够以速度和成本效率推出更新、更先进的硬件。

paras.en: 6. Continuously drive cost down and throughput up. Through rocket reusability, manufacturing at scale, advanced automation, and rigorous operational discipline, we continuously reduce unit costs while increasing launch cadence, satellite network, and AI hosting capacity.
paras.zh: 6. 持续降低成本、提升产能。通过火箭可重复使用、规模化制造、先进自动化和严格的运营纪律，我们持续降低单位成本，同时提高发射频率、卫星网络和 AI 托管容量。

paras.en: 7. Generate significant cash flow and reinvest in the future. As our businesses scale, they generate significant cash flow, which we reinvest into nascent market opportunities—driving a self-reinforcing cycle of constant innovation and potentially creating significant additional value.
paras.zh: 7. 产生可观的现金流并再投资于未来。随着业务规模扩大，它们产生可观的现金流，我们将其再投资于新兴市场机遇——推动持续创新的自我强化循环，并可能创造可观的额外价值。

paras.en: Starship is a powerful example of this business model in action. Upon achieving a fully and rapidly reusable design, we believe Starship will support a step-function increase in launch capacity and be capable of landing massive amounts of cargo on the Moon. Once there, we believe it will be possible to establish a permanent presence for scientific and manufacturing pursuits. For example, we believe that factories on the Moon could take advantage of lunar resources to manufacture million s of AI compute satellites and deploy them farther into space. Additionally, we are collaborating with NASA under the Artemis program to land humans on the Moon, with the goal of using Starship for transportation, which will be the first such mission since 1972.
paras.zh: 星舰是这一商业模式付诸实践的强有力例证。在实现完全且快速可重复使用的设计后，我们相信星舰将支撑发射能力实现阶跃式增长，并能够将大量货物送上月球。一旦抵达月球，我们相信将有可能建立永久存在，以开展科学和制造活动。例如，我们相信月球上的工厂可以利用月球资源制造数百万颗 AI 算力卫星，并将其部署到更远的太空。此外，我们正根据阿尔忒弥斯计划与 NASA 合作，将人类送上月球，目标是使用星舰进行运输，这将是自 1972 年以来的首次此类任务。

paras.en: We will continue leveraging our expanding launch capabilities, combined with our engineering and manufacturing expertise, to create and scale new markets in space for the benefit of humanity—on Earth, the Moon, Mars, and beyond.
paras.zh: 我们将继续利用不断扩展的发射能力，结合我们的工程和制造专长，为造福人类——在地球、月球、火星及更远的地方——创造并扩大太空中的新市场。

paras.en: #### Our Engineering-First Culture
paras.zh: #### 我们的工程优先文化

paras.en: We are able to achieve transformative technological breakthroughs because we accept only the laws of physics as the limiting factors to our work and mission. Our core approach is deeply rooted in first-principles thinking, which rejects any preconceived notions or experience-based norms. Our unparalleled track record demonstrates our capacity to execute space missions and achieve technological breakthroughs with speed and precision that others have not achieved. We have a track record of achieving what many have deemed impossible. Some of our industry-defining achievements and historic milestones include:
paras.zh: 我们能够实现变革性的技术突破，是因为我们只接受物理定律作为我们工作和任务的限制因素。我们的核心方法深深植根于第一性原理思维，拒绝任何先入为主的观念或基于经验的常规。我们无与伦比的过往记录证明了我们以他人未曾达到的速度和精度执行太空任务并实现技术突破的能力。我们拥有将许多人认为不可能的事情变为现实的过往记录。我们一些定义行业的成就和历史性里程碑包括：

paras.en: - The first private company to develop and launch a liquid-fuel rocket to reach orbit (2008);
paras.zh: - 首家开发并发射液体燃料火箭进入轨道的私营公司（2008 年）；

paras.en: - The first private company to successfully dock a private spacecraft with the International Space Station (2012);
paras.zh: - 首家成功将私人航天器与国际空间站对接的私营公司（2012 年）；

paras.en: - The first to successfully propulsively land (2015) and refly orbital-class rocket boosters (2017);
paras.zh: - 首家成功实现轨道级火箭助推器推进式着陆（2015 年）并再次飞行（2017 年）；

paras.en: - The first to begin deploying a large-scale LEO broadband satellite constellation (2019);
paras.zh: - 首家开始部署大规模低地球轨道（LEO）宽带卫星星座的公司（2019 年）；

paras.en: - The first private company to transport astronauts to orbit, returning America’s ability to fly astronauts to and from the International Space Station (2020);
paras.zh: - 首家将宇航员送入轨道的私营公司，恢复了美国将宇航员往返国际空间站的能力（2020 年）；

paras.en: - The first to manufacture consumer-grade phased-array user terminals at scale (2022);
paras.zh: - 首家大规模制造消费级相控阵用户终端的公司（2022 年）；

paras.en: - The first to deploy a large-scale LEO satellite-to-mobile constellation (2025);
paras.zh: - 首家部署大规模低地球轨道（LEO）卫星到移动星座的公司（2025 年）；

paras.en: - The first to build a gigawatt-scale AI training cluster and largest coherent supercomputer (2026);
paras.zh: - 首家建造吉瓦级 AI 训练集群和最大相干超级计算机的公司（2026 年）；

paras.en: - The first gigawatt-scale Megapack battery installation (2026); and
paras.zh: - 首个吉瓦级 Megapack 电池装置（2026 年）；以及

paras.en: - The only company capable of building orbital AI compute at scale.
paras.zh: - 唯一有能力大规模建设轨道 AI 算力的公司。

paras.en: Our organizational philosophy fosters an engineering-and data-led culture that embraces failure as an essential learning opportunity and is maniacally focused on efficiency and speed. This culture allows us to deliberately move quickly to test new hardware, knowing that early failures provide more valuable data than protracted analysis. We view our factories as the machines that build the machines and maintain a relentless focus on our ability to move, fail, and fix fast.
paras.zh: 我们的组织理念培育了一种以工程和数据为导向的文化，这种文化将失败视为必不可少的学习机会，并极度专注于效率和速度。这种文化使我们能够刻意快速行动以测试新硬件，因为我们深知早期失败所提供的数据比旷日持久的分析更有价值。我们将工厂视为制造机器的机器，并始终不渝地专注于我们快速行动、快速失败和快速修复的能力。

full.sec: Our AI Compute Infrastructure Advantage and Growth Strategy
full.secZh: 我们的 AI 算力基础设施优势与增长战略

paras.en: We believe AI leadership will be defined by the ability to rapidly scale compute capacity to support exponential usage growth and frontier intelligence. There is a meaningful compounding benefit of greater usage, creating more data for training, driving improvements in model performance, and in turn leading to greater usage. We believe that our highly vertically integrated, shovels-to-tokens approach allows us to train and iterate our frontier models at lower cost and higher velocity, accelerating development cycles, eliminating external bottlenecks, and driving rapid, continuous improvements in model performance. This dynamic reinforces the criticality of scale and cost efficiency in compute infrastructure as the primary differentiator in the AI landscape. In addition, our leadership in compute infrastructure positions us to monetize not only AI software applications built on our models, but also the underlying compute that powers them. As we continue to scale our terrestrial and orbital compute infrastructure to support internal model development, training, and inference workloads, we intend to sell our high-performance compute capacity to a limited number of third party customers.
paras.zh: 我们认为，AI 领导地位将由能否快速扩展算力容量以支撑指数级的使用量增长和前沿智能来界定。使用量越大，会带来显著的复利效应：产生更多用于训练的数据，推动模型性能提升，进而带来更大的使用量。我们相信，我们高度垂直整合的“从铲子到 token”模式，使我们能够以更低的成本和更高的速度训练和迭代我们的前沿模型，加速开发周期，消除外部瓶颈，并推动模型性能快速、持续地提升。这一动态进一步凸显了算力基础设施的规模与成本效率作为 AI 领域首要差异化因素的关键性。此外，我们在算力基础设施领域的领先地位，使我们不仅能够将基于我们模型构建的 AI 软件应用变现，还能将支撑这些应用的底层算力变现。随着我们持续扩展我们的地面和轨道算力基础设施，以支持内部模型开发、训练和推理工作负载，我们打算向有限数量的第三方客户出售我们的高性能算力容量。

paras.en: Why Compute Matters. The training and inference demanded by advanced AI models require substantial computational resources. Greater compute capacity enables more intelligence by training new generations of models with increasing frequency and creating more capable models, ability to support inference, or usage, across a large and growing user base, and extraction of the highest performance from those models. As the AI user base expands, we also expect compute demand per user to increase significantly. Reasoning models introduced in 2024 demonstrated that allocating more computational resources during inference directly leads to higher-quality intelligence. AI agents popularized in 2026 demonstrated that allocating more computational resources enabled multi-step task execution, meaningfully increasing compute demand per human user interaction. In addition, compute infrastructure with end-to-end, cluster-level coherence through tight integration across software and hardware systems enables more efficient, stable, and higher-fidelity training and inference at scale—ultimately enhancing model intelligence and performance. Within inference, we expect computationally-intensive reasoning, agentic, and multi-modal workloads will continue to grow as a portion of overall usage. We therefore expect demand for compute will continue to increase across consumer, enterprise, and government applications as AI adoption accelerates. For example, U.S. compute demand has already outpaced available power supply with estimated demand of 62 gigawatts in 2025 exceeding the power generation of 49 gigawatts, according to industry sources. We expect the gap between demand for compute and power supply to continue to widen meaningfully as AI compute needs proliferate. Furthermore, we believe that third-party estimates on data center demand are constrained by the practical supply limitations that exist in a terrestrial context and the power shortage may be far greater than what research estimates suggest. We believe operators with superior model-to-compute integration—the ability to efficiently support and allocate compute across both training and inference workloads—are best positioned to win the AI race.
paras.zh: 为何算力至关重要。先进 AI 模型所需的训练和推理需要大量计算资源。更大的算力容量能够带来更强的智能：以更高的频率训练新一代模型，打造能力更强的模型，在庞大且不断增长的用户群体中支撑推理或使用，并从这些模型中挖掘出最高性能。随着 AI 用户群体扩大，我们预计每位用户的算力需求也将显著增加。2024 年推出的推理模型表明，在推理阶段分配更多计算资源可直接带来更高质量的智能。2026 年普及的 AI 智能体表明，分配更多计算资源可实现多步骤任务执行，从而显著提高每次人类用户交互所对应的算力需求。此外，通过软件与硬件系统的紧密集成实现端到端、集群级一致性的算力基础设施，能够以更大规模实现更高效、更稳定、更高保真度的训练和推理——最终提升模型智能与性能。在推理方面，我们预计计算密集型的推理、智能体和多模态工作负载在整体使用中所占比例将持续增长。因此，随着 AI 采用加速，我们预计消费级、企业级和政府应用领域的算力需求将持续增加。例如，据行业来源，美国算力需求已超过可用电力供应，2025 年估计需求为 62 吉瓦，超过 49 吉瓦的发电量。我们预计，随着 AI 算力需求激增，算力需求与电力供应之间的缺口将持续显著扩大。此外，我们认为，第三方对数据中心需求的估计受到陆地环境下实际供应限制的制约，电力短缺可能远超研究估计所显示的水平。我们相信，在模型与算力集成方面具有优势——即能够在训练和推理工作负载之间高效支持和分配算力——的运营者最有条件赢得 AI 竞赛。

paras.en: Self-Reinforcing Network Effects Among Lower Cost Per Token, Model Quality, and User Adoption. AI systems are ultimately constrained or differentiated by the cost, speed, and scale at which they can generate and process tokens. A “token” represents the fundamental unit of data consumed and produced by modern AI models, for example corresponding to words, images, audio, or other modalities. It serves as the atomic unit through which models read, reason, and generate output. As such, tokens are the primary basis for measuring both the cost of training and cost of inference, making them a foundational economic metric in the AI space. Companies that can structurally reduce energy, compute, networking, and deployment costs per token will be positioned to train faster, iterate more rapidly, and ultimately manufacture greater intelligence, scale models more rapidly, and deliver increasingly powerful and accessible AI solutions. This creates a self-reinforcing advantage in which lower token costs drive greater model quality and user adoption, reinforcing AI leadership. This is because lower cost per token enables more frequent model training, larger and more sophisticated models, longer chains of processing for reasoning and agentic workloads, and significantly higher inference volumes at economically viable prices. This dynamic directly impacts model quality, responsiveness, and accessibility, while also determining the ability to serve the rising global demand across consumer, enterprise, and mission-critical AI applications. As AI systems scale toward increasingly complex reasoning tasks and higher usage intensity, improvement in cost per token enables meaningful advantages in performance quality, scaled distribution, and monetization. This is particularly true as the industry converges towards recursive self-improving learning that minimizes human intervention, which is highly token consumptive.
paras.zh: 更低单 token 成本、模型质量与用户采用之间的自我强化网络效应。AI 系统最终受制于或区别于其生成和处理 token 的成本、速度和规模。“token”代表现代 AI 模型所消耗和产生的基本数据单位，例如对应文字、图像、音频或其他模态。它是模型读取、推理和生成输出的原子单位。因此，token 是衡量训练成本和推理成本的主要基础，使其成为 AI 领域的一项基础性经济指标。能够在结构上降低每 token 的能源、算力、网络和部署成本的公司，将有能力更快训练、更快速迭代，并最终制造出更强的智能、更迅速地扩展模型规模，并提供日益强大且易于获取的 AI 解决方案。这形成了一种自我强化的优势：更低的 token 成本推动更高的模型质量和用户采用，从而强化 AI 领导地位。这是因为更低的单 token 成本能够实现更频繁的模型训练、更大更复杂的模型、针对推理和智能体工作负载的更长的处理链条，以及以经济可行的价格实现显著更高的推理量。这一动态直接影响模型质量、响应能力和可及性，同时也决定了满足消费者、企业和关键任务 AI 应用中不断增长的全球需求的能力。随着 AI 系统扩展至日益复杂的推理任务和更高的使用强度，单 token 成本的改善能够在性能质量、规模化分发和变现方面带来有意义的优势。随着行业趋向于最大限度减少人工干预的递归自我改进学习——这种学习高度消耗 token——这一点尤为明显。

paras.en: Cost of Compute is the Main Driver of Cost Per Token. The cost of compute is the primary driver of cost per token across both training and inference workloads. Each token processed by an AI model requires a quantifiable amount of computational effort. The total cost per token is determined by the efficiency, availability, and unit economics of the underlying compute resources. According to SemiAnalysis, for most AI companies without a build cost advantage, their total capital cost of building compute infrastructure derives approximately 30% from data center construction costs (including, but not limited to, the shell; mechanical, electrical, and plumbing (“MEP”); and grid interconnection) and approximately 70% from the cost of procuring processors and critical IT equipment. Ongoing operational costs of utilizing this compute infrastructure include the cost of power to run the processors, cost of maintaining those processors, and cost of delivering inference workloads to the end user. Improvement in the cost of building and operating this compute infrastructure—whether through lower data center construction cost, lower power infrastructure cost, shorter time to grid interconnection, or higher cluster-level throughput—translates directly into lower cost per token. Accordingly, for a given level of intelligence, we expect the long-term economics of AI companies to be driven by the ability to consistently deliver bleeding-edge compute at the lowest possible cost per token. Put simply, we view cost per token as a function of three primary inputs—the underlying AI model, the compute hardware, and energy, and we expect to have a competitive advantage in the latter two cost components. We believe we have a pathway over time that will significantly reduce compute hardware costs through continued vertical integration and development of proprietary chips, building on our experience designing custom silicon for our Starlink satellites. We also expect that the marginal cost of energy for our AI compute satellites will be minimal because our satellites are powered by solar arrays in space. By driving the energy component to minimal levels and pursuing improvements in compute hardware cost, we believe we can achieve a meaningfully lower overall cost per token in the future.
paras.zh: 算力成本是每 Token 成本的主要驱动因素。算力成本是训练和推理工作负载中每 Token 成本的主要驱动因素。AI 模型处理的每个 Token 都需要可量化的计算工作量。每 Token 的总成本由底层算力资源的效率、可用性和单位经济性决定。根据 SemiAnalysis 的数据，对于大多数不具备建设成本优势的 AI 公司而言，其建设算力基础设施的总资本成本中约 30% 来自数据中心建设成本（包括但不限于外壳；机械、电气和管道（“MEP”）；以及电网互联），约 70% 来自采购处理器和关键 IT 设备的成本。使用该算力基础设施的持续运营成本包括运行处理器的电力成本、维护这些处理器的成本，以及向最终用户交付推理工作负载的成本。建设和运营该算力基础设施的成本改善——无论是通过降低数据中心建设成本、降低电力基础设施成本、缩短电网互联时间，还是提高集群级吞吐量——都会直接转化为更低的每 Token 成本。因此，对于给定的智能水平，我们预计 AI 公司的长期经济性将取决于能否以尽可能低的每 Token 成本持续提供最前沿的算力。简而言之，我们将每 Token 成本视为三个主要输入的函数——底层 AI 模型、算力硬件和能源，我们预计在后两项成本组成部分上具有竞争优势。我们相信，凭借我们为 Starlink 卫星设计定制芯片的经验，通过持续的垂直整合和专有芯片的开发，我们有一条随时间推移显著降低算力硬件成本的路径。我们还预计，我们的 AI 算力卫星的边际能源成本将极低，因为我们的卫星由太空中的太阳能阵列供电。通过将能源组成部分降至最低水平并追求算力硬件成本的改善，我们相信我们未来能够实现显著更低的整体每 Token 成本。

paras.en: We Have a Dual Speed and Cost Advantage in Terrestrial AI Compute. We have established a leading position in building and scaling terrestrial AI compute infrastructure, becoming the first company to deploy a coherent gigawatt-scale AI training cluster. We own and operate what we believe to be the largest AI training data center clusters on Earth. Our AI compute facilities, COLOSSUS and COLOSSUS II, collectively provide approximately 1.0 gigawatt of compute power, with additional power capacity available for data center operations. Our first-principles thinking enables us to build coherent compute at scale and at rapid speed with lower costs than most other companies in the industry. We brought the first cluster of COLOSSUS online in 122 days, repurposing the shell of an existing factory, and the first cluster of COLOSSUS II online even faster in 91 days. As an illustrative comparison, an industry benchmark to bring online a 100 megawatt greenfield data center is approximately two years. We also demonstrated a significant improvement in cost efficiency, achieving data center construction costs for COLOSSUS II that are considerably lower than industry benchmarks on a per megawatt basis. We are able to deploy power and compute significantly faster than other AI companies through first-principles thinking, behind-the-meter power generation, coupled with what we believe is the world’s largest network of sustainable battery storage systems, and innovations in advanced liquid cooling, high-density rack layouts, and efficient networking.
paras.zh: 我们在地面 AI 算力方面具备速度与成本的双重优势。我们已在构建和扩展地面 AI 算力基础设施方面确立了领先地位，成为首家部署连贯的吉瓦级 AI 训练集群的公司。我们拥有并运营着我们认为是地球上规模最大的 AI 训练数据中心集群。我们的 AI 算力设施 COLOSSUS 和 COLOSSUS II 合计提供约 1.0 吉瓦的算力，并另有可用于数据中心运营的电力容量。我们的第一性原理思维使我们能够以低于行业内大多数其他公司的成本，大规模、快速地构建连贯算力。我们在 122 天内让 COLOSSUS 的首个集群上线，利用了现有工厂的外壳进行改造；而 COLOSSUS II 的首个集群上线更快，仅用 91 天。作为说明性对比，行业内让一座 100 兆瓦新建数据中心上线的基准时间约为两年。我们还在成本效率方面实现了显著提升，COLOSSUS II 的数据中心建设成本按每兆瓦计算大幅低于行业基准。凭借第一性原理思维、表后发电，以及我们认为是全球最大的可持续电池储能系统网络，再加上先进液冷、高密度机架布局和高效网络方面的创新，我们能够以显著快于其他 AI 公司的速度部署电力和算力。

paras.en: Our first-principles thinking and innovations in advanced liquid cooling, high-density rack layouts, and efficient networking enable rapid, cost-effective scaling with the latest processors—keeping us ahead of competitors deploying traditional methods. Faster deployments reinforce our cost advantage: we are able to access and bring online the highest performing hardware before our competitors, allowing us to sustain a token cost advantage. For example, we believe COLOSSUS II became one of the world’s first data centers to deploy GB200s and GB300s at significant scale and is currently powering training for our next frontier models, including Grok-5. We have already proven in multiple large-scale terrestrial data centers that we have built not only faster than competitors in the industry, but also at a lower cost.
paras.zh: 我们在先进液冷、高密度机架布局和高效网络方面的第一性原理思维与创新，使我们能够利用最新处理器实现快速、高性价比的扩展，从而领先于采用传统方法的竞争对手。更快的部署强化了我们的成本优势：我们能够先于竞争对手获取并上线性能最高的硬件，从而维持 token 成本优势。例如，我们认为 COLOSSUS II 已成为全球首批大规模部署 GB200 和 GB300 的数据中心之一，目前正在为我们的下一代前沿模型（包括 Grok-5）的训练提供算力。我们已在多个大型地面数据中心证明，我们不仅建设速度快于行业竞争对手，而且成本更低。

paras.en: We have a Unique Right to Win in Orbital AI. The Sun contains approximately 99.8% of the solar system’s energy and offers what we believe is the only truly scalable solution to terrestrial energy constraints, as we expect the cost and availability of terrestrial energy sources over time will necessitate a transition to orbital AI solutions. The logical path forward is to move power-intensive AI workloads into orbit, where solar energy is near-constant and uninterrupted. With such accessibility to energy, we believe that our launch business will enable us to consistently activate the highest performing hardware before our competitors without such access, shrinking the timeline to useful tokens on bleeding-edge hardware and sustaining our token cost advantage. Manufacturing next-generation satellites and launching them into space in very large numbers is a core component of our plans. We believe we are the only company with a commercially viable path to building orbital AI compute at scale. This is underpinned by our unique ability to launch substantial mass into orbit cost-efficiently through reusable rockets and to manufacture secure, reliable, and high-performance satellites at low cost and high volume.
paras.zh: 我们在轨道 AI 领域拥有独特的制胜权。太阳蕴含了太阳系约 99.8% 的能量，我们认为这是应对地球能源约束的唯一真正可扩展的解决方案，因为我们预计，随着时间推移，地球能源来源的成本和可获得性将迫使向轨道 AI 解决方案转型。合乎逻辑的前进路径是将高能耗的 AI 工作负载转移到轨道上，在那里太阳能几乎恒定且不中断。凭借如此便利的能源获取条件，我们相信，我们的发射业务将使我们能够在没有此类条件的竞争对手之前，持续率先启用性能最高的硬件，缩短在尖端硬件上产出有用 token 的时间线，并维持我们的 token 成本优势。制造下一代卫星并将其大规模发射入太空是我们计划的核心组成部分。我们相信，我们是唯一一家拥有商业可行路径来大规模构建轨道 AI 算力的公司。这得益于我们独特的能力：通过可重复使用火箭以低成本将大量质量送入轨道，并以低成本、高产量制造安全、可靠且高性能的卫星。

paras.en: - Terrestrial compute leadership. We believe the same cost and build advantages that have underpinned our leadership in gigawatt-scale terrestrial data centers will enable us to innovate across other terrestrial data center formats such as modular data centers for inference. We believe our modular terrestrial data center architectures will provide a foundation for the deployment of compute infrastructure in orbit given similarities in form factor in contrast to a gigawatt-scale campus.
paras.zh: - 地面算力领先地位。我们相信，正是支撑我们在吉瓦级地面数据中心领先地位的成本与建设优势，将使我们能够在其他地面数据中心形态（例如用于推理的模块化数据中心）上实现创新。我们相信，我们的模块化地面数据中心架构将为在轨道上部署算力基础设施奠定基础，因为与吉瓦级园区相比，二者在形态上具有相似性。

paras.en: - Satellites. Just as we expect our expertise in terrestrial data centers will enable us to package AI compute into modular, satellite form factors, we expect our leadership in satellite communications to allow us to interconnect our fleet of AI compute satellites into a massive, coherent constellation of compute. For example, as of March 31, 2026, our constellation already incorporated over 23,000 inter-satellite lasers that create a dynamic mesh network in space, enabling traffic to route through orbit rather than relying solely on terrestrial backhaul infrastructure. We are designing next-generation, high-performance AI compute satellites built for high volume, low cost, and with the reliability required for long-duration operation in space.
paras.zh: - 卫星。正如我们预计我们在数据中心领域的专业能力将使我们能够将 AI 算力封装为模块化的卫星形态，我们预计我们在卫星通信领域的领先地位将使我们能够将我们的 AI 算力卫星群互联成一个庞大、连贯的算力星座。例如，截至 2026 年 3 月 31 日，我们的星座已整合了超过 23,000 条星间激光链路，在太空中构建了一个动态网状网络，使流量能够经由轨道路由，而不必仅依赖地面回传基础设施。我们正在设计下一代高性能 AI 算力卫星，其面向高产量、低成本，并具备在太空长期运行所需的可靠性。

paras.en: - Starship. We expect each of our Starship V3 vehicles to carry 100 metric tons to Earth’s orbit in a reusable configuration, and future generations could reach 200 metric tons in capacity, potentially as soon as Starship V4 . Future generations of Starship are being designed to eventually deliver million s of tons to orbit and beyond per year. Delivering large amounts of mass to orbit at low cost will be critical to deploying AI compute satellites at scale.
paras.zh: - Starship。我们预计每艘 Starship V3 飞行器在可重复使用配置下可将 100 公吨载荷送入地球轨道，未来世代运力可能达到 200 公吨，最早可能在 Starship V4 实现。未来世代的 Starship 正被设计为最终每年向轨道及更远空间运送数百万吨载荷。以低成本将大量质量送入轨道，对于大规模部署 AI 算力卫星至关重要。

paras.en: We Believe Orbital AI Can Accelerate Time to Power and Reduce Token Costs. The Sun contains approximately 99.8% of the solar system’s energy and offers what we believe is the only truly scalable solution to the challenge of accelerating demand for compute relative to terrestrial energy constraints. The logical path forward is to move power-intensive AI workloads into orbit, where solar energy is near-constant and uninterrupted. With such accessibility to energy, we believe that our launch business will enable us to consistently activate the highest performing hardware before our competitors without such access. We believe SpaceX is uniquely positioned to deploy and operate data centers in orbit that can eventually achieve a lower cost than terrestrial data centers over time due to our extreme vertically integrated approach across launch, satellite manufacturing at scale, network connectivity and terrestrial data center expertise.
paras.zh: 我们相信轨道 AI 能够加快通电时间并降低 token 成本。太阳蕴含了太阳系约 99.8% 的能量，我们相信，面对算力需求加速增长与地球能源约束之间的矛盾，这是唯一真正可扩展的解决方案。合乎逻辑的前进路径是将高耗能的 AI 工作负载转移到轨道上，在那里太阳能近乎恒定且不中断。凭借如此便利的能源获取条件，我们相信，我们的发射业务将使我们能够持续先于不具备此类条件的竞争对手启用性能最高的硬件。我们相信，SpaceX 具有独特的优势，能够在轨道上部署和运营数据中心，凭借我们在发射、规模化卫星制造、网络连接和地面数据中心专业能力方面的高度垂直整合模式，这些数据中心的成本最终有望低于地面数据中心。

paras.en: - Time to useful tokens on new generations of infrastructure. Although we have already demonstrated an ability to rapidly scale new generations of compute in terrestrial deployments, we believe orbital AI will accelerate our time to useful tokens on bleeding-edge AI infrastructure. Physical deployment of new hardware is expected to be enabled by our launch business, where we believe reusability and launch cost efficiency will drive rapid cycles of payload delivery. Rapid time to useful tokens on that hardware will be enabled by the Sun’s near-constant, uninterrupted supply of power, which would circumvent terrestrial power infrastructure constraints such as power procurement, grid interconnections, and permitting. As new generations of AI infrastructure continue to deliver step-function improvements in token efficiency, we believe that maintaining an AI fleet consistently at the bleeding edge of the frontier curve has the potential to deliver a sustainable cost per token advantage relative to our competitors.
paras.zh: - 新一代基础设施实现可用 token 的时间。尽管我们已证明有能力在地面部署中快速扩展新一代算力，但我们相信，轨道 AI 将加快我们在最前沿 AI 基础设施上实现可用 token 的时间。我们预计，新硬件的物理部署将由我们的发射业务来实现，我们相信，可复用性和发射成本效率将推动有效载荷交付的快速循环。太阳近乎恒定、不中断的电力供应将使该硬件能够快速实现可用 token，这将绕开地面电力基础设施的制约，例如电力采购、电网互联和许可审批。随着新一代 AI 基础设施持续在 token 效率上带来阶跃式提升，我们相信，让 AI 机队始终保持在技术前沿曲线的最前沿，有望相对竞争对手带来可持续的单位 token 成本优势。

paras.en: - Construction, power, and cooling infrastructure. In orbit, construction costs are replaced by launch costs and satellite production costs. We expect reusable launch systems and high flight cadence will significantly reduce the cost per kilogram to orbit, enabling more efficient deployment of compute payloads to orbit, and eventually approach the cost of fuel. We believe our advanced satellite manufacturing capabilities enable us to build AI compute satellites at scale and lower cost than competitors. Other terrestrial data center construction costs such as building the shell, MEP, and grid interconnection are not applicable in space. As a result, once Starship and our AI compute satellites are fully deployed at scale, we believe that the initial deployment costs of in-orbit compute in the aggregate will be less than construction costs of others’ terrestrial data centers.
paras.zh: - 建设、电力和冷却基础设施。在轨道上，建设成本被发射成本和卫星生产成本所取代。我们预计，可复用发射系统和高发射频次将大幅降低每公斤入轨成本，从而能够更高效地将算力有效载荷部署至轨道，并最终接近燃料成本。我们相信，我们先进的卫星制造能力使我们能够以规模化、低于竞争对手的成本制造 AI 算力卫星。其他地面数据中心建设成本，例如建造外壳、MEP 和电网互联，在太空中并不适用。因此，一旦星舰和我们的 AI 算力卫星实现全面规模化部署，我们相信，在轨算力的初始部署成本总计将低于其他方地面数据中心的建设成本。

paras.en: - Cost to procure and service processors. The cost of processors is a significant cost for both terrestrial and orbital data centers. We do not believe that moving compute to space in and of itself will have a meaningful impact on the cost of procuring processors. However, we believe that diversifying our long-term access to the supply of processors, including through our Terafab initiative with Tesla and Intel, will be a key driver in reducing the overall cost of compute hardware over time. By combining internally manufactured, lower cost chips with those we source from third-party suppliers, we expect the overall cost of our processors to decline. In addition to reducing costs, we also expect that this hybrid sourcing strategy will help alleviate potential future chip shortages at SpaceX. In addition, we intend to conduct intensive pre-deployment testing to reduce the rate of chip failure in space, as we do not anticipate servicing or repairing processors in space.
paras.zh: - 处理器采购与服务成本。处理器成本是地面和轨道数据中心的一项重大成本。我们认为，将算力迁移至太空本身并不会对处理器采购成本产生实质性影响。然而，我们相信，通过包括与 Tesla 和 Intel 合作的 Terafab 计划在内的多种方式，实现处理器供应长期获取渠道的多元化，将成为随时间推移降低算力硬件整体成本的关键驱动因素。通过将内部制造的低成本芯片与从第三方供应商采购的芯片相结合，我们预计处理器的整体成本将会下降。除降低成本外，我们还预计这一混合采购策略将有助于缓解 SpaceX 未来可能出现的芯片短缺。此外，我们打算开展密集的部署前测试，以降低芯片在太空中的故障率，因为我们预计不会在太空对处理器进行维护或维修。

paras.en: - Ongoing operations. The total cost of operating data centers is heavily influenced by energy, cooling, and distribution requirements. In orbit, chips are expected to be powered by solar energy which is low cost and unlimited, and we expect to leverage radiative cooling architectures, which incur no operating costs compared to liquid or air cooling. Our integrated, space-based Starlink network architecture also enables more cost efficient routing of data between compute clusters and to end users on a global basis.
paras.zh: - 持续运营。数据中心的总运营成本在很大程度上受能源、冷却和配电需求的影响。在轨道上，芯片预计将由低成本且无限的太阳能供电，我们预计将采用辐射冷却架构，与液冷或风冷相比，该架构不产生运营成本。我们集成的天基 Starlink 网络架构还能在全球范围内实现算力集群之间以及向终端用户更经济高效的数据路由。

paras.en: We Believe We Are Well-Positioned to Deliver Orbital AI Compute. We believe orbital AI compute is an incredibly difficult technical challenge that only we can solve at scale in the near term. We are the only company that has already accomplished the key technical challenges associated with evolving connectivity satellites into AI compute satellites. In our view, due to our proven experience, we are well-positioned to deliver a full-scale AI compute satellite constellation. Significant work remains, but we are confident in our singular leadership position.
paras.zh: 我们相信我们具备充分优势来交付轨道 AI 算力。我们认为，轨道 AI 算力是一项极其艰巨的技术挑战，短期内只有我们能够大规模解决。我们是唯一一家已经攻克将连接卫星演进为 AI 算力卫星相关关键技术挑战的公司。在我们看来，凭借经过验证的经验，我们具备充分优势来交付全规模的 AI 算力卫星星座。仍有大量工作要做，但我们对我们独一无二的领导地位充满信心。

paras.en: - We have unmatched satellite launch capabilities to enable deployment at scale. Our ability to launch mass at scale and low cost is our foundational competitive advantage. Deployment of 100 gigawatts per year via satellites carrying over 100 kilowatts of compute power per metric ton will require thousand s of launches per year and the transport of approximately one million metric tons to orbit annually. The fully reusable nature of Starship positions us to be capable of launching this level of mass. We plan to leverage our PEZ dispenser system, an integrated payload deployment system for Starship, along with our experience in developing fully deployable single-unit systems that are designed to substantially reduce the risks associated with in-orbit assembly. Starlink Broadband V1 and V2 Minisatellites have already demonstrated launch survivability and high reliability under vibration, shock, g-loads, acoustic stress, and vacuum exposure, achieving 99.9% average uptime. Although introducing AI processors would traditionally increase component-level failure rates, we plan to subject compute hardware to extensive pre-deployment testing on Earth to identify early life failures before launch.
paras.zh: - 我们拥有无可匹敌的卫星发射能力，能够实现规模化部署。我们以低成本大规模发射载荷的能力是我们的基础性竞争优势。通过每公吨算力超过 100 千瓦的卫星实现每年 100 吉瓦的部署，将需要每年数千次发射，并每年向轨道运送约 100 万公吨。星舰完全可重复使用的特性使我们有能力发射这一量级的载荷。我们计划利用我们的 PEZ 分配器系统——一种用于星舰的集成式载荷部署系统——以及我们在开发完全可部署单机系统方面的经验，这些系统旨在大幅降低与在轨组装相关的风险。Starlink 宽带 V1 和 V2 迷你卫星已在振动、冲击、g 载荷、声学应力和真空暴露条件下证明了发射生存能力和高可靠性，实现了 99.9% 的平均正常运行时间。尽管引入 AI 处理器传统上会增加组件级故障率，但我们计划在地球上对算力硬件进行广泛的部署前测试，以便在发射前识别早期失效。

paras.en: - We have already solved many of the significant technical hurdles to evolving connectivity satellites into
paras.zh: - 我们已解决将连接卫星演进为

paras.en: AI compute satellites. Through our leading expertise in connectivity satellites and Starlink’s existing technical and operational capabilities—including constellation-scale satellite management, autonomous operations, over-the-air software updates, inter-satellite laser communications, mesh network deployment, radiation-hardened system design, proprietary chip development, and the ability to operate computers reliably in the space environment—we have already solved the hardest part in the development of AI compute satellites. AI compute satellites represent an evolution of spacecraft engineering already demonstrated at scale through Starlink’s connectivity satellites, and we believe development of AI compute satellites will be easier for us than for anyone else. AI compute satellites must integrate high-density compute payloads developed with radiation-tolerant designs and components with high electrical power generation, advanced thermal management, and inter satellite networking. To source the electricity needed to power our AI processors, we aim to continuously scale our existing space-grade solar technologies through insourced process development and build a constellation in dawn-dusk Sun-synchronous orbit that delivers near-constant solar exposure. We expect solar cells optimized for the space environment will be produced at a rapid rate, with early satellites generating 100 kilowatts of compute power and scaling from there. In orbit, thermal control must be accomplished through radiation rather than convection and conduction. We plan to advance thermal control systems—many of which have been proven on Starlink—by using radiators, vapor chambers, active cooling loops, and coatings to dissipate the heat generated by AI hardware in space’s vacuum. We will also utilize inter-satellite lasers pioneered by Starlink for mesh networking at scale, creating coherent computing clusters across free space instead of wired connections used in terrestrial data centers. Our existing Starlink constellation, with over 23,000 inter-satellite lasers, will be a crucial enabler of orbital AI compute, as its global network allows data from our AI compute satellites in Sun-synchronous orbit to reach ground stations anywhere on Earth. The SpaceX AI compute satellites will be designed for high rate, automated production to enable the scale of satellites needed for the large amounts of compute planned in space.
paras.zh: AI 算力卫星。凭借我们在连接卫星领域的领先专业能力以及 Starlink 现有的技术和运营能力——包括星座级卫星管理、自主运行、空中软件更新、星间激光通信、网状网络部署、抗辐射系统设计、专有芯片开发，以及在太空环境中可靠运行计算机的能力——我们已解决了 AI 算力卫星开发中最困难的部分。AI 算力卫星代表了航天器工程的演进，而这一演进已通过 Starlink 的连接卫星实现规模化验证，我们相信，对我们而言，AI 算力卫星的开发将比任何人都更容易。AI 算力卫星必须集成采用耐辐射设计和组件开发的高密度算力载荷，并配备高发电能力、先进热管理和星间组网。为获取驱动我们 AI 处理器所需的电力，我们计划通过自研工艺开发持续扩大现有航天级太阳能技术的规模，并在晨昏太阳同步轨道上构建星座，以实现近乎持续的日照。我们预计，针对太空环境优化的太阳能电池将以快速的速度生产，早期卫星将产生 100 千瓦的算力功率，并由此扩展。在轨道上，热控制必须通过辐射而非对流和传导来实现。我们计划推进热控制系统——其中许多已在 Starlink 上得到验证——通过使用散热器、均热板、主动冷却回路和涂层，在太空真空中散发 AI 硬件产生的热量。我们还将利用 Starlink 首创的星间激光进行规模化网状组网，在自由空间中创建连贯的计算集群，而非地面数据中心使用的有线连接。我们现有的 Starlink 星座拥有超过 23,000 条星间激光链路，将成为轨道 AI 算力的关键赋能因素，因为其全球网络使我们位于太阳同步轨道的 AI 算力卫星的数据能够到达地球任何地方的地面站。SpaceX 的 AI 算力卫星将面向高速自动化生产而设计，以实现太空中计划的大量算力所需的卫星规模。

paras.en: There are material differences between connectivity satellites and AI compute satellites. Connectivity satellites are primarily designed for communications, with substantial onboard equipment dedicated to phased-array antennas, radio systems, and data transmission. In contrast, AI compute satellites are optimized for high-performance computing. Key differences include significantly larger solar arrays to support higher power requirements, substantially larger radiators for thermal management, different electronics centered on AI accelerators rather than communications processors, and the removal of much of the communications hardware. Our V3 satellite platform already incorporates proprietary chips, providing a strong foundation for the ability to operate AI-focused electronics in space, and we expect to begin deploying our orbital AI compute satellites as early as 2028.
paras.zh: 连接卫星与 AI 算力卫星之间存在重大差异。连接卫星主要面向通信设计，搭载大量专用设备用于相控阵天线、射频系统和数据传输。相比之下，AI 算力卫星针对高性能计算进行优化。主要差异包括：为支持更高功率需求而显著加大的太阳能电池阵列、为热管理而显著加大的散热器、以 AI 加速器而非通信处理器为核心的不同电子设备，以及移除大部分通信硬件。我们的 V3 卫星平台已集成专有芯片，为在太空运行以 AI 为核心的电子设备奠定了坚实基础，我们预计最早于 2028 年开始部署我们的轨道 AI 算力卫星。

paras.en: The primary remaining challenge is one of scale. For example, a deployment rate of approximately 10 gigawatts per year would require a materially lower manufacturing and launch cadence, which we believe would still enable a commercially attractive AI compute business with strong economic returns. While our long-term vision includes the ambition of deploying up to 100 gigawatts of power to orbit annually, which would require the deployment of thousand s of launches per year, assuming 100 kilowatts of compute power per metric ton and Starship capacity to orbit of 100 metric tons, we believe we can be economically successful at significantly more modest volumes.
paras.zh: 剩余的主要挑战在于规模。例如，约每年 10 吉瓦的部署速率将要求大幅降低制造和发射节奏，我们认为这仍能支撑一个具有商业吸引力且经济回报强劲的 AI 算力业务。虽然我们的长期愿景包括每年向轨道部署高达 100 吉瓦功率的雄心，这将要求每年执行数千次发射，但假设每公吨算力功率为 100 千瓦且 Starship 的入轨运力为 100 公吨，我们认为我们可以在显著更为温和的规模下取得经济上的成功。

paras.en: Our 100 gigawatt annual power deployment goal is based on reasoned engineering analyses and design parameters developed through our ongoing design and development work on next-generation AI compute satellites. These analyses are based on currently available space-grade solar technology and do not require fundamental technological advances beyond existing capabilities. Specifically, we expect these satellites to leverage our already-designed V3 satellite platform. The core V3 satellite design is complete, and the AI compute satellites are expected to generate substantially more power than V3 satellites. This performance is expected to be achieved primarily through the use of significantly larger solar arrays. These satellites are targeted to generate approximately 100 kW of compute power per ton, which initially will require approximately five times the solar array output compared to V3 satellite designs.
paras.zh: 我们每年部署 100 吉瓦功率的目标基于合理的工程分析以及我们在下一代 AI 算力卫星持续设计与开发工作中形成的设计参数。这些分析基于当前可用的航天级太阳能技术，且不需要超出既有能力的根本性技术突破。具体而言，我们预计这些卫星将依托我们已完成设计的 V3 卫星平台。V3 卫星的核心设计已完成，而 AI 算力卫星预计将产生显著高于 V3 卫星的功率。这一性能预计主要通过使用显著加大的太阳能电池阵列来实现。这些卫星的目标是每吨产生约 100 千瓦的算力功率，初期所需的太阳能电池阵列输出约为 V3 卫星设计的五倍。

paras.en: We currently do not anticipate material supply constraints for space-based solar panels, as global production capacity, including through our vertical integration efforts, is believed to be sufficient to meet its requirements. We are actively developing the manufacturing, launch cadence, and operational capabilities that we believe would be needed to support such launch rates.
paras.zh: 我们目前预计太空太阳能电池板不会出现重大供应约束，因为全球产能（包括通过我们的垂直整合努力形成的产能）被认为足以满足其需求。我们正在积极发展我们认为支持此类发射速率所需的制造、发射节奏和运营能力。

paras.en: The precise solar collection area, total system mass per satellite, and on-orbit assembly requirements associated with this goal continue to be refined as part of our ongoing engineering efforts. In general, the approach contemplates larger deployable solar arrays on each satellite, with no significant on-orbit assembly currently anticipated.
paras.zh: 与该目标相关的精确太阳能收集面积、每颗卫星的系统总质量以及在轨组装要求，仍在我们的持续工程工作中不断完善。总体而言，该方案设想在每颗卫星上采用更大的可展开太阳能电池阵列，目前预计无需进行大规模在轨组装。

paras.en: - We will use our proven Starlink in-orbit technology to optimize our orbital AI compute. In order to operate orbital AI compute satellites, we plan to build on our vast experience of operating approximately 9,600 Starlink broadband and mobile satellites in Low-Earth Orbit. In 2025 alone, Starlink satellites proactively performed over 1,000 automated collision avoidance maneuvers per day guided by this technology to safely and efficiently operate the constellation. This operating model gives us control over workload placement across Earth and space while maintaining resilience through redundancy and fail safe systems. To ensure optimized thermal management and power generation, we will design each satellite’s solar arrays to face the sun for constant power while its housing radiator panels face cold deep space for radiative cooling. A high degree of controllability will allow the satellite to be optimized for brightness mitigation, disposal, and other modes of operation. As more advanced AI hardware becomes available, we plan to manage the lifecycle of deployed systems by shifting older hardware to lower intensity workloads as performance characteristics evolve, and retiring systems that are no longer needed through controlled end of life disposition, including transition to graveyard orbits where appropriate. These retirements may occur sooner than our estimates for the useful lives of our satellites, which estimates are based on engineering studies, historical on-orbit performance, propellant life, utilization patterns, design enhancements across generations, and planned transitions to newer satellite technology. Space based compute also introduces orbital debris risk, which we already manage at constellation scale through our autonomous collision avoidance system across Starlink. To date, we have not experienced any failures of our autonomous collision avoidance system that have resulted in satellite loss.
paras.zh: - 我们将利用经过验证的 Starlink 在轨技术来优化我们的轨道 AI 算力。为了运营轨道 AI 算力卫星，我们计划依托我们在低地球轨道运营约 9,600 颗 Starlink 宽带和移动卫星所积累的丰富经验。仅 2025 年，Starlink 卫星在该技术的引导下每天主动执行超过 1,000 次自动避碰机动，以安全高效地运营星座。这一运营模式使我们能够控制地球与太空之间的工作负载分配，同时通过冗余和故障安全系统保持韧性。为确保优化的热管理和发电，我们将把每颗卫星的太阳能电池阵列设计为朝向太阳以获得持续电力，同时其外壳散热板朝向寒冷的深空进行辐射冷却。高度可控性将使卫星能够针对亮度缓解、处置及其他运行模式进行优化。随着更先进的 AI 硬件问世，我们计划管理已部署系统的生命周期，在性能特征演变时将较旧的硬件转向强度较低的工作负载，并通过受控的寿命终止处置方式退役不再需要的系统，包括在适当情况下转移至坟墓轨道。这些退役可能早于我们对卫星使用寿命的估计，该估计基于工程研究、历史在轨性能、推进剂寿命、使用模式、跨代设计改进以及向更新卫星技术的计划过渡。天基算力还带来轨道碎片风险，我们已通过 Starlink 全星座的自主避碰系统在星座规模上对此进行管理。迄今为止，我们的自主避碰系统尚未发生任何导致卫星损失的故障。

paras.en: - We can manufacture our AI compute constellations at scale with rapid upgrade cycles. We have built one of the largest satellite manufacturing operations in the world with standardized bus architectures, rapid iteration cycles, and automotive-style production lines, enabling us to evolve bus architecture and subsystem design with limited reliance on third-party suppliers. Our highly vertically integrated approach will be key to our mass-scaling efforts and should allow us to deploy the latest AI processors. Our ability to quickly develop and deploy new generations of AI compute to orbit will be a key advantage in maintaining frontier performance of the constellation. We believe SpaceX will be the first and only company to manufacture satellites at the scale of automotive manufacturing.
paras.zh: - 我们能够以快速升级周期大规模制造我们的 AI 算力星座。我们已建成世界上最大的卫星制造运营体系之一，拥有标准化总线架构、快速迭代周期和汽车式生产线，使我们能够在有限依赖第三方供应商的情况下演进总线架构和子系统设计。我们高度垂直整合的方式将是我们大规模扩展努力的关键，并应使我们能够部署最新的 AI 处理器。我们快速开发并将新一代 AI 算力部署至轨道的能力，将是保持星座前沿性能的关键优势。我们相信 SpaceX 将成为首家也是唯一一家以汽车制造规模制造卫星的公司。

paras.en: - We are building chip manufacturing capabilities to scale our access to AI compute hardware. We announced a collaboration with Tesla in March 2026 to build the Terafab initiative with a long-term goal of producing one terawatt of compute hardware each year. Intel joined the project in April 2026 and is expected to contribute its expertise in designing, fabricating, and packaging ultra-high-performance chips to help Terafab scale. In connection with such collaboration, we have agreed with Tesla on a general framework for the future development of Terafab. Any specific projects undertaken pursuant to this framework will be subject to separate negotiations and agreements (including any development timelines, milestones and capital expenditures) and have not yet been determined. Our strategy for Terafab is to vertically integrate across design of lithography masks, fabrication of logic and memory chips, design of advanced packaging and rapidly test and iterate in order to improve chip design and performance. With this internal manufacturing capability, we plan to alleviate potential future chip shortages at SpaceX, especially as we develop orbital AI at scale, and design chips that are optimized for the space environment. We expect that our speed and cost advantage from vertical integration will allow us to scale efficiently in AI chip manufacturing.
paras.zh: - 我们正在建设芯片制造能力，以扩大我们获取 AI 算力硬件的渠道。我们于 2026 年 3 月宣布与 Tesla 合作，共同推进 Terafab 计划，长期目标是每年生产一太瓦的算力硬件。Intel 于 2026 年 4 月加入该项目，预计将贡献其在设计、制造和封装超高性能芯片方面的专业能力，以帮助 Terafab 扩大规模。就该等合作而言，我们已与 Tesla 就 Terafab 的未来发展达成总体框架。根据该框架开展的任何具体项目均须另行协商并签订协议（包括任何开发时间表、里程碑和资本支出），且尚未确定。我们对 Terafab 的战略是，在光刻掩模设计、逻辑芯片和存储芯片制造、先进封装设计方面进行垂直整合，并快速测试和迭代，以改进芯片设计和性能。借助这一内部制造能力，我们计划缓解 SpaceX 未来潜在的芯片短缺问题，尤其是在我们大规模开发轨道 AI 的过程中，并设计针对太空环境优化的芯片。我们预计，垂直整合带来的速度和成本优势将使我们能够在 AI 芯片制造领域高效扩张。

paras.en: - We can leverage our terrestrial experience to build and operate compute clusters and AI workloads at
paras.zh: - 我们可以利用我们的地面经验，在

paras.en: scale. We believe our experience operating compute infrastructure on Earth provides the technical and operational foundation to extend these capabilities into orbit. For example, manufacturing and silicon defects in AI processors can cause failures early in life. We plan to subject compute hardware to extensive pre-deployment testing on Earth to identify early life failures before launch to reduce in-orbit disruption. Over time, we plan to design AI compute processors optimized for the space environment. Our operating experience will be critical in informing our orbital data center designs for highly reliable operations even with potential chip failures. This capability is further supported by our flexible allocation of AI workloads across compute clusters, enabling us to utilize orbital data centers for workloads without hardware reconfigurations or maintenance. For compute hardware that does fail, we plan to leverage existing Starlink fleet management software to reallocate traffic to other satellites and prevent cluster-level downtime. We further believe that our strong relationships with chip makers enhance our ability to build a well-functioning, integrated AI compute system in space.
paras.zh: 规模上建设和运营算力集群及 AI 工作负载。我们相信，我们在地球上运营算力基础设施的经验提供了技术和运营基础，可将这些能力延伸至轨道。例如，AI 处理器中的制造缺陷和硅缺陷可能导致早期失效。我们计划在地球上对算力硬件进行广泛的部署前测试，以在发射前识别早期失效，从而减少在轨中断。随着时间推移，我们计划设计针对太空环境优化的 AI 算力处理器。我们的运营经验对于指导我们的轨道数据中心设计至关重要，使其即使在芯片可能出现故障的情况下也能实现高度可靠的运行。这一能力还得到我们在各算力集群之间灵活分配 AI 工作负载的支持，使我们能够利用轨道数据中心处理工作负载，而无需重新配置硬件或进行维护。对于确实发生故障的算力硬件，我们计划利用现有的 Starlink 机队管理软件将流量重新分配到其他卫星，并防止集群级停机。我们进一步相信，我们与芯片制造商的牢固关系增强了我们在太空中构建运行良好、集成化的 AI 算力系统的能力。

paras.en: We Believe Our Infrastructure is a Distinct Advantage in Delivering Superior AI.We believe that the key constraints in the continued growth of AI are physical – chip manufacturing, data center infrastructure, and power generation; the future of AI will be determined by the control of the physical stack. We believe no other AI company has better control over the full physical stack than SpaceX. We expect the combination of competitive cost per token, our ability to deploy and operate data centers in orbit, and our strength in connectivity to result in more scalable intelligence that is accessible globally at high speeds by way of the following structural advantages:
paras.zh: 我们相信，我们的基础设施是交付卓越 AI 的独特优势。我们认为，AI 持续增长的关键制约因素是物理层面的——芯片制造、数据中心基础设施和发电；AI 的未来将由对物理技术栈的控制权决定。我们相信，没有其他 AI 公司能比 SpaceX 更好地控制完整的物理技术栈。我们预计，具有竞争力的每 token 成本、我们在轨道上部署和运营数据中心的能力，以及我们在连接性方面的优势，三者相结合将带来更具可扩展性的智能，并通过以下结构性优势，使全球用户能够以高速访问这些智能：

paras.en: - Time to power. If we are able to deploy our AI compute satellite constellation, we believe it will enable compute capacity to be deployed and expanded efficiently as capacity requirements grow. This approach will also allow us to deploy new generations of compute hardware in quicker succession relative to terrestrial approaches where data centers cannot be easily retrofitted for new compute hardware. Due to terrestrial retrofitting limitations, adding terrestrial capacity typically demands building large, new data centers designed for specific generations of compute hardware. This approach is usually burdened with long lead times for activities such as power procurement, utility grid interconnections, and permitting before new computing hardware can generate useful tokens. We believe our orbital, modular approach will allow us to circumvent terrestrial power infrastructure constraints.
paras.zh: - 通电时间。如果我们能够部署我们的 AI 算力卫星星座，我们相信，随着算力需求的增长，这将使算力容量得以高效部署和扩展。这种方法还将使我们能够比地面方案更快地迭代部署新一代算力硬件，因为地面数据中心无法轻易改造以适配新的算力硬件。由于地面改造的局限性，增加地面算力通常需要建设专为特定代际算力硬件设计的大型新数据中心。这种方法通常在新计算硬件能够生成有用的 token 之前，就因电力采购、电网互联和许可等活动而面临漫长的前置时间。我们相信，我们的轨道模块化方法将使我们能够绕开地面电力基础设施的制约。

paras.en: - Highly scalable compute capacity. Unlike terrestrial facilities constrained by physical footprint and availability of power in a given location, orbital data centers leverage a decentralized mesh architecture. This permits the aggregation of massive compute clusters interconnected over long distances by inter-satellite lasers pioneered by Starlink. Space offers effectively unlimited power and vast expanse to sustain uninterrupted operations as capacity grows. We believe this abundance of power and physical area will allow us to scale our connected compute capacity faster and far beyond levels that are terrestrially viable.
paras.zh: - 高度可扩展的算力容量。与受限于物理占地和特定地点电力可用性的地面设施不同，轨道数据中心利用去中心化的网状架构。这允许通过 Starlink 首创的星间激光链路，将远距离互连的大规模算力集群聚合起来。太空提供几乎无限的电力 and 广阔的空间，以在算力增长时维持不间断运行。我们相信，这种丰富的电力和物理空间将使我们能够比地面可行水平更快、更大幅度地扩展我们的互联算力容量。

paras.en: - Low latency. Our satellite constellation provides a direct, orbital data path that circumvents the bottlenecks of terrestrial communications networks. This architecture is particularly suitable to support high-speed connectivity for latency-sensitive workloads, which we believe are increasingly valued in certain consumer-and enterprise-facing applications.
paras.zh: - 低延迟。我们的卫星星座提供了一条直接的轨道数据路径，绕开了地面通信网络的瓶颈。这种架构特别适合为延迟敏感型工作负载提供高速连接，我们相信这类工作负载在某些面向消费者和企业的应用中正日益受到重视。

paras.en: - Global distribution. Because of the global coverage of our satellite constellation, not only can we deliver high-speed, ultra-low latency AI solutions, we can do so anywhere in the world. We believe our increasingly global network of Starlink satellites will enable us to deliver frontier intelligence, at high speed and reliability, to communities and economies around the world.
paras.zh: - 全球分布。得益于我们卫星星座的全球覆盖，我们不仅能够交付高速、超低延迟的 AI 解决方案，还能在世界任何地方做到这一点。我们相信，我们日益全球化的 Starlink 卫星网络将使我们能够以高速和可靠性，向世界各地的社区和经济体交付前沿智能。

paras.en: Design and manufacture our own chips. Terafab aims to be the world’s largest chip manufacturing facility, with the goal of achieving one terawatt of annual compute production capacity. While Terafab is intended to expand our internal chip manufacturing capabilities, we expect to continue sourcing a significant portion of our compute hardware from third-party suppliers. We view Terafab as complementary to these relationships, enabling us to augment our access to compute hardware at massive scale and further complete our highly vertically integrated compute platform by extending our control to the foundational chip layer. By developing end-to-end capabilities spanning the design of lithography masks, fabrication of logic and memory chips, and advanced packaging, all in a vertically integrated closed-loop single plant, we will be able to more rapidly iterate to improve chip design and performance. We plan to design chips that are optimized for the space environment. This collaboration directly enables our planned orders-of-magnitude increases in AI compute deployment in orbit which would be constrained by pure reliance on external foundries. Leveraging shared engineering resources, intellectual property, and infrastructure across Tesla and SpaceX, as well as Intel’s proposed contribution of its expertise in designing, fabricating and packaging ultra-high-performance chips at scale, Terafab creates powerful ecosystem synergies that accelerate innovation cycles and reduce costs. Just as we manufacture approximately 80% of Starship in-house, enabling it to be the world’s most powerful and, eventually, the most cost-effective launch vehicle through full and rapid reusability, we expect significant speed and cost advantages from Terafab’s vertical integration. We believe this will provide us with a critical competitive advantage in the race to scale AI infrastructure, especially as we begin our orbital AI compute satellite deployments.
paras.zh: 设计并制造我们自己的芯片。Terafab 的目标是成为全球最大的芯片制造设施，目标是实现每年一太瓦的算力产能。尽管 Terafab 旨在扩大我们内部的芯片制造能力，但我们预计将继续从第三方供应商采购相当一部分算力硬件。我们将 Terafab 视为对这些关系的补充，使我们能够大规模扩充算力硬件的获取渠道，并通过将控制延伸至基础芯片层，进一步完善我们高度垂直整合的算力平台。通过在一个垂直整合的闭环单一工厂内构建涵盖光刻掩模设计、逻辑与存储芯片制造以及先进封装的全流程端到端能力，我们将能够更快速地迭代以改进芯片设计和性能。我们计划设计针对太空环境优化的芯片。这一合作直接使我们计划中在轨 AI 算力部署的数量级增长成为可能，而纯粹依赖外部代工厂将对此形成制约。借助 Tesla 和 SpaceX 共享的工程资源、知识产权和基础设施，以及 Intel 拟贡献的在大规模设计、制造和封装超高性能芯片方面的专业能力，Terafab 创造了强大的生态系统协同效应，可加速创新周期并降低成本。正如我们约 80% 的 Starship 为内部制造，使其通过全面且快速的重复使用成为全球最强大、并最终成为最具成本效益的运载火箭，我们预计 Terafab 的垂直整合将带来显著的速度和成本优势。我们相信，这将在扩大 AI 基础设施规模的竞赛中为我们提供关键的竞争优势，尤其是在我们开始进行轨道 AI 算力卫星部署之际。

paras.en: We are focused on three rapidly evolving industries: space, connectivity, and AI. Technological advancements and breakthrough innovation are enabling what we believe is the next great economic frontier, as progress across space launch, global communications, frontier models, AI compute, robotics, and automation reshape what is possible on and off Earth. There are several key trends driving the growth and evolution of these industries in which we operate:
paras.zh: 我们聚焦于三个快速演进的行业：太空、连接和 AI。技术进步与突破性创新正在开启我们认为的下一个伟大经济前沿，太空发射、全球通信、前沿模型、AI 算力、机器人和自动化领域的进展正在重塑地球之上和地球之外的可能性。有几大关键趋势正在推动我们所处这些行业的增长与演进：

paras.en: - Reusable launch and industrialized space operations are materially reducing the cost of access to orbit, increasing mass carried per launch, and enabling high-cadence deployment of space-based infrastructure;
paras.zh: - 可重复使用发射和工业化太空运营正在大幅降低进入轨道的成本，提高单次发射运载质量，并实现天基基础设施的高频次部署；

paras.en: - High‑volume satellite manufacturing, combined with rapid constellation refresh cycles, is expanding the ability for ubiquitous connectivity across unconnected, underconnected, and mobile “dead zone” areas; and
paras.zh: - 大批量卫星制造，叠加快速的星座更新周期，正在扩大在未连接、连接不足及移动“盲区”区域实现无处不在连接的能力；以及

paras.en: - AI, automation, and robotics are accelerating engineering iteration cycles, streamlining operations, and revolutionizing complex construction, reducing reliance on scarce specialized labor while delivering faster, more precise, and cost-optimized infrastructure.
paras.zh: - AI、自动化和机器人正在加速工程迭代周期、简化运营并革新复杂建造，减少对稀缺专业劳动力的依赖，同时交付更快、更精准、成本更优的基础设施。

paras.en: #### The Space Industry
paras.zh: #### 太空行业

paras.en: For most of the space age—dating back to the first launches in the 1950s—spaceflight was shaped by onerous regulatory requirements and government budgets that determined launch cadence. The prevailing cost-plus procurement model offered limited incentives to reduce costs or increase launch cadence, creating an operating environment that constrained technological innovation. Government agencies served as the primary launch services providers and the industry remained stagnant for decades. According to NASA, until the 2000s and the introduction of the Falcon 9 rocket by SpaceX, global commercial launch activity averaged 25 to 35 launches per year. As a result, the space industry remained a niche domain with limited ability to support large commercial markets or scaled space-based infrastructure.
paras.zh: 在太空时代的大部分时间里——可追溯至 20 世纪 50 年代的首次发射——航天飞行受到繁重监管要求和政府预算的塑造，而这些预算决定了发射频率。盛行的成本加成采购模式对降低成本或提高发射频率提供的激励有限，形成了一种制约技术创新的运营环境。政府机构是主要的发射服务提供方，该行业数十年来停滞不前。根据 NASA 的数据，直到 2000 年代 SpaceX 推出 Falcon 9 火箭之前，全球商业发射活动平均每年为 25 至 35 次。因此，航天行业始终是一个细分领域，支持大型商业市场或规模化天基基础设施的能力有限。

paras.en: During this period, satellites—which comprised the majority of launch payload—were typically bespoke, expensive systems requiring significant non-recurring engineering that consisted of development cycles that were measured in decades. Launch vehicles were designed to be largely expendable and optimized for single-mission use, reinforcing a low-throughput ecosystem that lacked flexibility, scalability, and responsiveness to evolving customer requirements.
paras.zh: 在此期间，卫星——占发射载荷的大部分——通常是定制化、昂贵的系统，需要大量非经常性工程投入，其开发周期以十年计。运载火箭在设计上基本为一次性使用，并针对单次任务进行优化，强化了一个吞吐量低、缺乏灵活性、可扩展性以及对不断变化的客户需求响应能力的生态系统。

paras.en: The need for more advanced launch capabilities became clear as space-based use cases expanded to include communications, navigation, Earth observation, environmental monitoring, scientific research, Intelligence, Surveillance and Reconnaissance, and access to the International Space Station. In 2006, NASA awarded SpaceX, along with Rocketplane Kistler, the landmark Commercial Orbital Transportation Services contract that heralded the age of commercial space launch, marking a shift toward a more scalable approach to accessing space. This inflection point catalyzed a transition toward systems designed for more frequent operations, lower cost, and greater operational flexibility.
paras.zh: 随着天基应用场景扩展至通信、导航、对地观测、环境监测、科学研究、情报、监视与侦察以及国际空间站访问，对更先进发射能力的需求变得清晰。2006 年，NASA 将具有里程碑意义的商业轨道运输服务合同授予 SpaceX 以及 Rocketplane Kistler，宣告了商业太空发射时代的到来，标志着向更具可扩展性的太空进入方式转变。这一拐点催化了向为更频繁运营、更低成本和更大运营灵活性而设计的系统转型。

paras.en: Fundamental breakthroughs in high cadence, reliable, and affordable access to space—driven largely by SpaceX— have expanded space from a purely mission-driven activity to a fully industrialized and commercial sector capable of supporting and enabling industries far beyond traditional launch and satellites. SpaceX’s advancements reduced the cost of access to orbit from tens of thousand s of dollars per kilogram to just a few thousand dollars per kilogram.
paras.zh: 高频次、可靠且可负担的太空进入方式所取得的根本性突破——主要由 SpaceX 推动——已将太空从纯粹以任务为导向的活动扩展为一个完全工业化、商业化的领域，能够支持和赋能远超传统发射与卫星的众多行业。SpaceX 的技术进步将进入轨道的成本从每公斤数万美元降至每公斤仅数千美元。

paras.en: Cost of Space Launches to Low-Earth Orbit (constant 2021 $ per kilogram; plotted on a logarithmic axis)
paras.zh: 低地球轨道太空发射成本（以 2021 年不变美元/公斤计；采用对数坐标轴绘制）

paras.en: As launch economics have changed rapidly over the last decade, demand for orbital infrastructure has expanded dramatically. Commercial operators have launched thousand s of satellites since 2015 as constellation architectures scale and diversify. The number of active maneuverable satellites in orbit has grown from less than 1,000 in 2015 to approximately 12,700 as of March 31, 2026. With approximately 9,600 Starlink broadband and mobile satellites in Low-Earth Orbit as of March 31, 2026, SpaceX owns and operates approximately 75% of all active maneuverable satellites. Additionally, launch activity has continued to grow, with approximately 220 metric tons of payload launched to orbit in 2012 increasing to approximately 2,600 metric tons in 2025, of which over 80% was launched by SpaceX.
paras.zh: 随着过去十年发射经济性的快速变化，对轨道基础设施的需求急剧扩大。自 2015 年以来，随着星座架构的规模化与多元化，商业运营商已发射数千颗卫星。在轨活跃可机动卫星数量已从 2015 年的不足 1,000 颗增长至截至 2026 年 3 月 31 日的约 12,700 颗。截至 2026 年 3 月 31 日，SpaceX 在低地球轨道拥有约 9,600 颗 Starlink 宽带及移动卫星，拥有并运营着全部活跃可机动卫星中约 75% 的份额。此外，发射活动持续增长，2012 年发射入轨的有效载荷约 220 公吨，到 2025 年增至约 2,600 公吨，其中超过 80% 由 SpaceX 发射。

paras.en: Government demand is rising in parallel: according to the Space Foundation, excluding classified spending, U.S. Government space spending in 2024 totaled approximately $77 billion. Notably, U.S. national security customers have also awarded approximately $13.7 billion across the National Security Space Launch (“NSSL”) Program’s Phase 3 Lane 2 contracts through 2032, supporting approximately 54 missions from 2025 to 2032, with the overall Phase 3 manifest nearly doubling Phase 2’s manifest to 84 missions. Amid escalating geopolitical tensions that further underscore the critical role of resilient launch infrastructure, we believe government space budgets around the world are positioned for sustained, long‑term growth.
paras.zh: 政府需求也在同步上升：根据太空基金会（Space Foundation）的数据，剔除机密支出后，2024 年美国政府的太空支出总计约 $77 billion。值得注意的是，美国国家安全客户还通过国家安全太空发射（“NSSL”）计划第 3 阶段第 2 通道合同，在截至 2032 年的期间内授予了约 $13.7 billion，支持 2025 年至 2032 年的约 54 次任务，而第 3 阶段的整体任务清单几乎达到第 2 阶段任务清单的两倍，达 84 次任务。在地缘政治紧张局势不断升级、进一步凸显韧性发射基础设施关键作用之际，我们认为全球政府太空预算有望实现持续、长期增长。

paras.en: Falcon Heavy Boosters Landing
paras.zh: Falcon Heavy 助推器着陆

paras.en: On the back of dramatically reduced launch cost pioneered by SpaceX over the past two decades, the global economy is reorganizing around a new domain: space. We believe the development of a lunar economy will be central to unlocking the full potential of this new domain and advancing the long-term transition to a multiplanetary civilization.
paras.zh: 在 SpaceX 过去二十年开创的大幅降低发射成本的基础上，全球经济正围绕一个新领域进行重组：太空。我们相信，月球经济的发展将成为释放这一新领域全部潜力、并推动向多行星文明长期转型的核心。

paras.en: #### The Connectivity Industry
paras.zh: #### 连接产业

paras.en: Modern life relies on connectivity. Over the past several decades, the technologies that underpin global connectivity have evolved rapidly, reshaping the way individuals, families, and organizations communicate, collaborate, and access information.
paras.zh: 现代生活依赖于连接。过去几十年来，支撑全球连接的技术快速演进，重塑了个人、家庭和组织沟通、协作及获取信息的方式。

paras.en: Despite remarkable technological advancements, terrestrial networks remain constrained by the same inherent structural limitations that have hindered them since their inception. According to the Global Satellite Operators Association, terrestrial network infrastructure only covers approximately 20% of global land mass, resulting in significant unserved and underserved regions across both developed and developing economies. This terrestrial connectivity gap spans areas that are remote, difficult to build in, or economically impractical to serve—and also includes mobile “dead zones” within otherwise well-connected areas and in urban markets. According to the J.D. Power U.S. Wireless Network Quality Performance Study, U.S. wireless customers experienced service problems in approximately one out of every 11 mobile interactions, even in well-connected areas. As demand for ubiquitous, high-reliability connectivity continues to rise, terrestrial networks alone are increasingly unable to bridge the widening gap between user demand and available coverage.
paras.zh: 尽管技术取得了显著进步，地面网络仍然受制于自其诞生以来就一直阻碍其发展的固有结构性局限。根据全球卫星运营商协会的数据，地面网络基础设施仅覆盖约 20% 的全球陆地面积，导致发达经济体和发展中经济体中都存在大量未覆盖和服务不足的地区。这一地面连接缺口涵盖偏远、难以建设或经济上不适宜提供服务的地区——也包括其他连接良好地区以及城市市场中的移动“盲区”。根据 J.D. Power 美国无线网络质量性能研究，美国无线客户在约每 11 次移动交互中就有一次遇到服务问题，即使在连接良好的地区也是如此。随着对无处不在、高可靠性连接的需求持续上升，仅靠地面网络越来越难以弥合用户需求与可用覆盖之间不断扩大的差距。

paras.en: The development of large-scale LEO constellations represented a paradigm shift, breaking from the long-standing dependence on terrestrial networks for global connectivity. Deployed at unprecedented scale—such as through SpaceX’s Starlink and Mobile constellations—these satellites can provide high-speed, low-latency service that integrates seamlessly with terrestrial infrastructure. This evolution has transformed satellite connectivity from a solution of last resort into a core pillar of resilient, ubiquitous global communications.
paras.zh: 大规模 LEO 星座的发展代表了一次范式转变，打破了全球连接长期依赖地面网络的局面。这些卫星以前所未有的规模部署——例如通过 SpaceX 的 Starlink 和 Mobile 星座——能够提供高速、低延迟的服务，并与地面基础设施无缝集成。这一演进已将卫星连接从最后手段的解决方案转变为具有韧性、无处不在的全球通信的核心支柱。

paras.en: Consumer Broadband
paras.zh: 消费者宽带

paras.en: Residential internet access began with the dial-up connection in the late 1990s with maximum speeds of .056 Mbps, when early users relied on narrowband copper phone lines to connect. As demand for speed and reliability grew, dial-up gave way to DSL, cable, and eventually fiber, each increasing bandwidth and enabling more connected devices. According to the Speedtest Global Index, the global average broadband download speed has increased to approximately 120 Mbps. Satellite internet also emerged in the 1990s through geostationary orbit (GEO) systems that extended coverage to remote and unconnected regions—beginning with early offerings such as Hughesnet’s first satellite service DirecPC, which provided downstream speeds of roughly 400 kbps compared to dial-up averages of 28.8 kbps—but these systems were constrained by limited throughput and high latency, making it difficult to keep pace as consumer requirements evolved. Starlink satellites operate in Low-Earth Orbit, substantially closer to the Earth’s surface than traditional geostationary communications satellites. This architecture reduces signal latency and is designed to support broadband connectivity in remote and underserved areas. Each launch of additional Starlink satellites increases the overall capacity of the network, which provides service globally.
paras.zh: 住宅互联网接入始于 20 世纪 90 年代末的拨号连接，最高速度为 .056 Mbps，当时的早期用户依赖窄带铜质电话线进行连接。随着对速度和可靠性的需求增长，拨号上网让位于 DSL、有线电视，并最终发展为光纤，每一代都提升了带宽并支持更多联网设备。根据 Speedtest Global Index，全球平均宽带下载速度已提升至约 120 Mbps。卫星互联网也在 20 世纪 90 年代通过地球静止轨道（GEO）系统出现，将覆盖范围扩展至偏远和未联网地区——最早的产品包括 Hughesnet 的首项卫星服务 DirecPC，其下行速度约为 400 kbps，而拨号上网的平均速度为 28.8 kbps——但这些系统受限于吞吐量有限和延迟较高，难以跟上消费者需求的变化。Starlink 卫星运行在低地球轨道，比传统地球静止通信卫星距地球表面近得多。这种架构降低了信号延迟，旨在支持偏远和服务不足地区的宽带连接。每次发射更多 Starlink 卫星都会提升网络的整体容量，从而在全球范围内提供服务。

paras.en: In today’s digital landscape, consumers increasingly rely on seamless, high-performance connectivity to power all aspects of connected life—from every day digital services to demanding applications that require high throughput, consistent performance, and low latency. These needs are particularly challenging to satisfy in regions where terrestrial networks are limited, degraded, or unavailable due to prohibitive deployment costs, rugged terrain, low population density, or outdated infrastructure. Consequently, consumer broadband has evolved into a multifaceted ecosystem, where diverse access technologies converge and providers compete based on superior reliability, consistent performance, and an exceptional overall user experience.
paras.zh: 在当今的数字环境中，消费者日益依赖无缝、高性能的连接来支撑互联生活的方方面面——从日常数字服务到需要高吞吐量、稳定性能和低延迟的高要求应用。在地面网络因部署成本高昂、地形崎岖、人口密度低或基础设施陈旧而受限、性能下降或无法覆盖的地区，满足这些需求尤为困难。因此，消费宽带已演变为一个多层面的生态系统，多种接入技术在此汇聚，提供商围绕更卓越的可靠性、稳定的性能和出色的整体用户体验展开竞争。

paras.en: Consumer demand for data is surging at a pace that terrestrial infrastructure has struggled to match. According to International Data Corporation’s Global DataSphere, in 2025, global data generation was estimated to have reached more than 585 exabytes of per day—up from approximately 10.8 exabytes per day in 2010—reflecting an immense escalation in consumption. With fixed broadband connections projected to reach two billion by 2030 according to Ericsson, and terrestrial expansion often economically unfeasible in remote and challenging regions, only space-based systems can deliver truly global, ubiquitous, high-throughput coverage capable of supporting this explosive growth in data demand.
paras.zh: 消费者对数据的需求正以地面基础设施难以企及的速度激增。根据国际数据公司（International Data Corporation）的 Global DataSphere，2025 年全球每日数据生成量估计已超过 585 exabytes——高于 2010 年每日约 10.8 exabytes——反映出数据消费量的巨大攀升。根据 Ericsson 的预测，到 2030 年固定宽带连接数将达到 two billion，而在地处偏远和条件艰苦的地区，地面网络扩张往往在经济上不可行，因此只有天基系统才能提供真正全球覆盖、无处不在的高吞吐量连接，以支撑数据需求的这一爆炸式增长。

paras.en: Enterprise and Government Broadband
paras.zh: 企业与政府宽带

paras.en: Enterprise broadband internet has evolved alongside residential internet, beginning with fixed private lines that connected offices and infrastructure. As businesses adopted real-time, distributed workflows, they needed secure, low-latency connectivity across multiple sites and mobile assets. Mobility became essential in sectors like manufacturing, transportation, and logistics, extending connectivity demands beyond fixed locations into dynamic environments that terrestrial networks often cannot support reliably or economically. Enterprises now expect seamless, uninterrupted performance with instant failover where terrestrial systems are unavailable or unstable— driving adoption of hybrid architectures that combine ground networks with space-based solutions.
paras.zh: 企业宽带互联网与住宅互联网同步演进，最初是连接办公室和基础设施的固定专线。随着企业采用实时、分布式的工作流程，它们需要在多个站点和移动资产之间实现安全、低延迟的连接。在制造业、运输和物流等行业，移动性变得至关重要，将连接需求从固定地点扩展到动态环境，而地面网络往往无法可靠或经济地支持这些环境。企业现在期望在地面系统不可用或不稳定的地方实现无缝、不间断的性能和即时故障切换——这推动了将地面网络与天基解决方案相结合的混合架构的采用。

paras.en: Enterprise connectivity demand continues to rise as organizations digitize operations and rely on real‑time, cloud‑based workflows that require secure, low‑latency connectivity across distributed sites and mobile environments. This is particularly true in the case of aviation, maritime, and land mobility applications, where aircraft, vessels, and ground fleets are inherently mobile and therefore unable to depend on continuous terrestrial network coverage for connectivity. These platforms increasingly require resilient communications to support flight and voyage operations, crew applications, passenger internet access, telematics, and port or shipboard logistics. In aviation, legacy GEO-based systems that are still prevalent across most major commercial fleets typically provide low Mbps speeds and significantly higher latency, often exceeding 500 milliseconds, falling well short of the approximately 100 Mbps throughput and sub-50 milliseconds latency that today’s applications—such as streaming, cloud services, and real-time collaboration—increasingly demand. Therefore, there is a need for modern LEO-powered in-flight connectivity systems—such as Starlink Broadband—that can deliver passenger download speeds exceeding 400 Mbps with latency as low as 21 milliseconds. Terrestrial networks cannot meet these evolving demands where deployment is costly, complex, and slowed by regulatory constraints, and legacy satellite solutions have not delivered the latency or consistency needed for enterprise‑grade applications, with average terrestrial ISP download speeds at 120 Mbps and average latency from 7-34 milliseconds.
paras.zh: 随着各组织推进运营数字化，并依赖基于云的实时工作流，而此类工作流需要在分布式站点和移动环境中实现安全、低时延的连接，企业连接需求持续上升。在航空、海事和陆地移动应用中尤其如此，因为飞机、船舶和地面车队本身具有移动性，因而无法依赖持续的地面网络覆盖来获得连接。这些平台日益需要具备韧性的通信，以支持飞行和航行运营、机组人员应用、乘客互联网接入、远程信息处理以及港口或船上物流。在航空领域，目前仍在大多数主要商业机队中普遍使用的传统 GEO 系统通常仅提供较低的 Mbps 速度，且时延显著更高，往往超过 500 毫秒，远不能满足当今应用——如流媒体、云服务和实时协作——日益要求的约 100 Mbps 吞吐量和低于 50 毫秒的时延。因此，需要现代化的 LEO 驱动机上连接系统——例如 Starlink Broadband——其可提供超过 400 Mbps 的乘客下载速度，时延低至 21 毫秒。地面网络无法满足这些不断演变的需求，因为其部署成本高昂、复杂，并因监管限制而放缓；而传统卫星解决方案未能提供企业级应用所需的时延或一致性，地面 ISP 的平均下载速度为 120 Mbps，平均时延为 7-34 毫秒。

paras.en: Defense and civil agencies similarly require secure, resilient, and global connectivity, often operating in contested or infrastructure-poor regions where terrestrial networks are unavailable or vulnerable. As the battlefield becomes increasingly connected, the need for robust, persistent connectivity across all domains is more urgent than ever. Modern missions depend on high-throughput, low-latency connectivity for command and control, autonomous systems, emergency response, and humanitarian operations, driving demand for architectures that maintain performance where terrestrial systems fail. Substantial government investment into mission-critical, space-based communication services illustrates the institutional reliance on LEO architecture for defense applications. High-throughput, low-latency LEO constellations add a new architectural layer that enhances redundancy, operational continuity, and flexibility across mission sets. There is an increasing need for purpose-built secure platforms—such as Starshield, that can provide encrypted, high-assurance communications and modular payload integration—further expand the utility of space-based connectivity for defense, civil, and national resilience needs. Together, these advances position space as the foundational component of future mission‑critical communications architectures.
paras.zh: 国防和民用机构同样需要安全、具备韧性且覆盖全球的连接，它们往往在有争议或基础设施薄弱的地区运营，在这些地区地面网络不可用或较为脆弱。随着战场互联程度日益提高，对跨所有域的强大、持续连接的需求比以往任何时候都更加迫切。现代任务依赖高吞吐量、低时延的连接来支持指挥与控制、自主系统、应急响应和人道主义行动，这推动了对在地面系统失效时仍能保持性能的架构的需求。政府对任务关键型天基通信服务的大量投资，体现了机构对 LEO 架构在国防应用中的依赖。高吞吐量、低时延的 LEO 星座增加了一个新的架构层，可增强各任务集的冗余性、运营连续性和灵活性。对专用安全平台——例如 Starshield——的需求日益增长，此类平台可提供加密的高保障通信和模块化载荷集成，进一步拓展天基连接在国防、民用和国家韧性需求方面的效用。综合来看，这些进步使太空成为未来任务关键型通信架构的基础组成部分。

paras.en: Satellite-to-Mobile Service
paras.zh: 卫星到移动服务

paras.en: Since the early rise of mobile phones, terrestrial networks have expanded at immense cost and increasing density to support successive generations of cellular technology—from the primarily voice-centric networks of the 1980s to today’s high-speed 5G data networks. These investments have enabled much of the global population to become well‑connected, yet the capital‑intensive nature of terrestrial build‑outs has resulted in vast geographic mobile “dead zones” where coverage remains too expensive or is nonexistent. In many regions particularly those that are remote or sparsely populated, extending towers is economically impractical for mobile network operators, resulting in large segments of the population with limited or no access to reliable connectivity. Early satellite-based cellular options, beginning in the 1980s with dedicated satellite phones, helped fill these gaps but required bulky hardware and carried high usage cost, limiting them to narrow and mission-driven use cases. As consumer expectations for ubiquitous coverage have grown, mobile network operators face structural limits in closing these “dead zones” with terrestrial infrastructure alone, making LEO-based augmentation the most viable path to continuous, reliable mobile connectivity at global scale.
paras.zh: 自手机早期兴起以来，地面网络以巨大的成本和不断增加的密度扩张，以支持一代又一代的蜂窝技术——从 20 世纪 80 年代以语音为主的网络到如今的高速 5G 数据网络。这些投资使全球大部分人口实现了良好连接，然而地面网络建设属于资本密集型，导致大片地理上的移动“盲区”，在这些区域覆盖成本过高或根本不存在覆盖。在许多地区，尤其是偏远或人口稀少的地区，扩建基站对移动网络运营商而言在经济上不可行，致使很大一部分人口只能获得有限或无法获得可靠连接。早期的卫星蜂窝方案始于 20 世纪 80 年代的专用卫星电话，曾帮助填补这些空白，但需要笨重的硬件且使用成本高昂，使其局限于狭窄且任务驱动的用例。随着消费者对无处不在的覆盖期望不断提高，移动网络运营商仅靠地面基础设施在填补这些“盲区”方面面临结构性限制，使得基于低轨（LEO）的增强成为在全球范围内实现持续、可靠移动连接的最可行路径。

paras.en: Early satellite-to-mobile services (i.e., those connecting directly to standard smartphones) emerged in the 2020s with support for basic messaging and, in some cases, voice in areas without terrestrial coverage. These offerings provided more contiguous communication for safety, continuity, and remote operations. However, they were introduced at the same time mobile data consumption was accelerating dramatically, and consumer expectations for “always-connected” devices were rising. As a result, satellite-to-mobile technology is now evolving beyond emergency-only communication.
